read:evaluation.area: Measurement and labels: sever/evaluation.py, sever/normalize.py comparison(), analysis/ground-truth-expanded-provisional.json, tools/compare_runs.py, deploy/evaluate_server_results.py, README label/customer sections
read:evaluation.summary:
The 35/44 benchmark has three problems: it is small, it measures the wrong things in places, and it is aimed away from where the compute goes.

1. **Too small and too clustered.** The Wilson 95% interval for 35/44 is [65.5%, 88.8%]. 21 of the 44 rows are repeat showings, and the rows hold only 7 distinct values from 2 document sets.

2. **Biased in measurable ways.**
   - All 4 labelled consignee_address values still use the old postal-only boundary. The source crop shows that field (4) contains the organisation, ИНН/КПП and РЦ, so any output that follows the 11.10 rule is scored wrong (verified with comparison()).
   - The 8 "missed intervals" are probably mostly a matching artefact: V7 produced 87 leaves for 88 truth intervals and had 7 unmatched predictions. The one case the README documents (the TTN front frame at 21.324 s) falls inside the label's own end bracket.

3. **Blind where the time is spent.** evaluation.py skips the 44 "not visible on this leaf" rows. These rows are exactly the role-confusion traps, and they are the only labels on the 4 continuation leaves that take 74% of video-5 time. As a result, no speed change there (phase-1 no-progress stop, early other-side stop) can show a precision effect.

The labels also say nothing about TORG-12 and ТрН (0 video labels for 9 of the 19 fields). The 7 unlabelled videos took 74% of V7 batch compute.

Small code changes, ranked below, would give 88 to 96 scored checks without new labelling: abstention checks, bracket-tolerant matching, Wilson intervals and McNemar tests in compare_runs, per-class speed, and the comparison() date and literal-match fixes. For ±5 points at 95%, about 250 independent value labels are needed (370 to 490 with clustering). The 2.5 to 3 hour plan below starts with the five short unlabelled videos.

Business-rule bends are named in each finding.

findings.title: Score the 44 'not_visible_on_this_leaf' rows as abstention (hallucination) checks
findings.claim:
evaluate() drops every labeled:false field, so 52 of 96 required instances are invisible to the metric. 44 of them are marked not_visible_on_this_leaf and 8 semantic_confirmation_needed. These 44 rows are exactly the role-confusion traps, a known error class: the creator or signer footer on UPD continuations, and the payer or unloading point on TTN reverses. A pipeline that writes the document creator into consignor on those leaves loses nothing in 35/44.

Change: in evaluate(), when target.labeled is False and manual_visibility == 'not_visible_on_this_leaf', record an abstention check.
- Correct only if type_ok and the delivered status is 'unreadable' or 'conflict' (no value delivered).
- 'recognized' counts as wrong and increments errors['hallucinated:<field>'].
- 'not_present' also counts as wrong, because not visible does not mean printed absent.
- Report abstention_accuracy per kind.field.
- Add 'fully_specified' leaves (every required field is either value-labelled or abstention-labelled) so e2e can be measured on 16 target leaves instead of 8. The 4 UPD continuations stay out until the customer answers Q3.

This is a speed prerequisite. Today's video-5 run spends 72% of calls and 74% of wall time (about 1970 of 2665 s) on 4 hard leaves. By class counts and ordering these are truth pages 012 to 015: TTN commodity continuations x2, which the pipeline typed torg12, and UPD continuations x2. All 20 of their required fields are not_visible or semantic_pending, so they carry 0 value labels. compare_runs therefore cannot show any precision change where phase-1's no-progress stop acts. With abstention checks it can. That makes it safe to cut these leaves to the cost of a TTN reverse (~120 s, 18 to 22 calls). The upper bound is about 1490 s saved on video 5 (-56%, from about 178 to about 78 s per leaf).

Эти роли не взаимозаменяются'; GT line 330 `"manual_visibility": "not_visible_on_this_leaf"`; sample-05-page-012 observed_form 'Товарный раздел ТТН, продолжение, страница 2' (truth type ttn); analysis/native-fix-status-20261010.json remaining_observed_errors 'Two lower UPD frames still assigned creator organizations to shipping roles'.
findings.expected_speed_effect: Indirect but the largest available. It makes an early other-side or continuation stop on 4/15 leaves measurable. Upper bound about -1490 s of 2665 s on video 5 (-56%).
findings.expected_precision_effect: Scored checks rise from 44 to 88 (96 after customer Q3). Measures the role-confusion and hallucination class directly. E2e denominator rises from 8 to 16 leaves.
findings.risk: Business rule 'invisibility is not printed absence' requires not_present to count as wrong. If the customer answers Q2/Q4 by merging sides into one physical document, these rows become value labels taken from the other side. Keep manual_visibility so both derivations stay possible. Wrong types (torg12 on a TTN continuation) fail these checks; report them apart from true hallucinations.
findings.how_to_test: Unit tests in tests/test_evaluation.py: truth field {labeled:false, manual_visibility:'not_visible_on_this_leaf'}. A prediction with status recognized and value 'ООО X' scores abstention wrong and hallucinated+1; unreadable scores correct; not_present scores wrong. Then rescore today's main and phase1-speed video-5 results.json with tools/compare_runs.py --truth (no model calls). Report k/16 on pages 012-015 and k/44 overall for both arms.

findings.title: The 'missed interval' class is largely a primary-timestamp matching artefact; add bracket-tolerant matching
findings.claim:
evaluate() credits a truth interval only if the prediction's primary-frame timestamp lies strictly inside [start_s, end_s). The truth boundaries, however, are midpoints between samples 1 to 1.5 s apart, and the label file already records boundary_uncertainty brackets.

V7 produced 87 leaves against 88 truth intervals (15/15, 53/53, 8/8, 11/12) but reported 8 missed intervals and 7 unmatched predictions. So at most 1 miss can be a genuinely missing leaf; at least 7 are predictions whose primary frame landed outside the approximate interval.

The README documents one such case. The readable TTN-front frame at 21.324 s lies inside page-005's own end bracket [20.658, 21.691] but after its end_s of 21.174. That cost 4 labelled fields (9 points of 44) and 1 of the 8 e2e leaves. So 'segmentation is the biggest loss' is at least partly a measurement artefact.

Change: keep stage 1 strict and unchanged. In stage 2, offer each still-unmatched truth interval only to still-unmatched predictions whose primary timestamp lies in [start_bracket_s[0], end_bracket_s[1]], choosing the nearest midpoint. Assignment uses time only, never correctness. Report detection_strict alongside detection_bracket_tolerant, list every bracket match, and for each unmatched prediction emit the truth interval its primary fell into.
findings.evidence: sever/evaluation.py:104-110 `if timestamp is not None and start <= timestamp < end: choices.append(...)`; GT sample-05-page-005 end_s 21.174306 (line 4294), end_bracket_s [20.657856, 21.690756] (lines 4371-4372); page-006 start_s 21.174306 (line 4419); README.md:121-122 'читаемый фронт ТТН в видео5 в 21,324 с находится вне ранее размеченного фронтового интервала'; README.md:327-329 'основной выбранный кадр вне неизменённого ручного интервала, поэтому все четыре поля остаются ошибкой'; analysis/monitor-native-v7-state.json:161-162 missed_intervals 8, unmatched_predictions 7; result_pages at lines 40/49/58/76 = 15/8/11/53; sever/video.py:477-478 boundaries are midpoints and :521 pages carry start_s/end_s.
findings.expected_speed_effect: None at runtime. It stops engineering effort going into segmentation fixes for misses that are labelling artefacts.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Up to 7 extra matched intervals. The documented case alone restores 4/44 fields and 1/8 e2e, which removes a downward bias of up to about 9 to 15 points.
findings.risk: README:123/329 forbids fitting boundaries to the system. This change uses only brackets already in the truth file, and the strict metric stays the headline until the customer agrees. A bracket-zone frame can genuinely show the neighbouring leaf mid-turn, so each bracket match needs a one-minute human look at the primary frame, recorded in selected_frame_usability. One-to-one matching is preserved (tests/test_evaluation.py:28 must still pass).
findings.how_to_test: Unit test: truth [19.109, 21.174) with end bracket [20.658, 21.691], and [21.174, 26.339); predictions with primaries at 21.324 and 23.5. Strict gives 1 match; tolerant gives 2. Then on the server (offline, no model calls) rescore the V7 results.json for videos 4 and 5 and today's two video-5 runs. Count misses under strict vs tolerant and view each newly matched primary frame.

findings.title: Relabel the 4 consignee_address values to the 11.10.2026 entire-block rule; keep the old value as legacy
findings.claim:
All 4 labelled consignee_address values (UPD fronts sample-04 p001/p004 and sample-05 p001/p004) are postal-only: '628422, Ханты-Мансийский автономный округ - Югра, г. Сургут, Индустриальная ул., д. 21, соор. 16'.

The customer rule and the prompt now require the entire field-(4) content. I viewed analysis/sample-05/selected-frames/upd-parties-crop.png: field (4) prints 'ООО "УМНЫЙ РИТЕЙЛ"; ИНН/КПП 7725382984/860245001,РЦ ООО "ПроФреш", 628422, ... соор. 16'.

I checked comparison() on the V8 candidate output for image-0001, which follows the rule. Against the current label it returns not-equal. Against an entire-block label it returns equal, even when the label joins lines with newlines and uses «» quotes. So 4/44 labels (9 points) penalise compliance with the rule and reward the obsolete boundary. The label's raw literal also has 'Профреш' where the print has 'ПроФреш'.

consignor_address is 'он же', which resolves to the seller's field 2а. That field holds only the postal line, so those 4 labels stay valid.

Change: set value and raw_value to the full block. Add legacy_value plus field_boundary_rule 'pre-2026-10-11', so the historical V7 batch can still be scored under the rule it ran with. Optionally add components [org, inn_kpp, rc, postal] so a diagnostic can show which part is missing or extra (this is the 'address block boundary' error class).

Labelling rule for new sheets:
- Transcribe everything printed inside the own field box, top to bottom then left to right, joining lines with '\n'. Separators are neutral in comparison() except between two digits.
- Add accepted_variants when the line order of a block is ambiguous.
- Never include the Покупатель/Адрес block.

Предварительную оценку адресов по прежней границе поля нельзя считать оценкой соответствия'; sever/image_reader.py:177 'ENTIRE literal value printed in the own Грузополучатель и его адрес field/block, including organization, warehouse/RC, INN/KPP'; sever/image_reader.py:59-63; analysis/accuracy-speed-v8-image-comparison.json candidate image-0001 consignee_address 'ООО "УМНЫЙ РИТЕЙЛ"; ИНН/КПП 7725382984/860245001,РЦ ООО "ПроФреш", 628422, ...'; analysis/accuracy-speed-v8-pixel-review.json 'The own combined consignee/address block contains organization, INN/KPP, RC name and postal address'.
findings.expected_speed_effect: None.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Removes a systematic 4/44 (9-point) bias against rule-compliant output. Affects 2 of the 22 labelled fields in every video-5 A/B.
findings.risk: Labels are provisional and need customer approval. Historical V7 numbers (pre-rule) would shift, so score them against legacy_value and label the result as such. The sample-04 crop must be checked separately, because the print may differ from sample-05.
findings.how_to_test: Edit the 4 labels, then assert comparison('consignee_address', V8_candidate_string) == comparison('consignee_address', new_label) and != against legacy_value. Rescore today's main and phase1 video-5 runs with tools/compare_runs.py. Expect sample-05-page-001/004 consignee_address to flip to ok in any arm that follows the rule.

findings.title: Report uncertainty: Wilson CI, exact McNemar and document-cluster bootstrap in compare_runs and the server evaluator
findings.claim:
For 35/44 the Wilson 95% interval is [65.5%, 88.8%] (±11.7 points). The effective sample is smaller still:
- 21 of the 44 rows are repeat showings (repeat_of).
- The 44 rows hold only 7 distinct values: 2559 x6, 2560 x6, 20.08.2026 x8, ФРЭШ-ЭКСПРЕСС x8, УМНЫЙ РИТЕЙЛ x8, and the two addresses x4 each.
- They come from 2 document sets with identical parties, so one glyph error class (РИТЕЙЛ read as РИТЕИЛ) can move the score by 8/44, i.e. 18 points.

How the 'visible interval including repeats' unit distorts errors:
- It inflates n and multiplies each systematic error by the number of showings.
- It penalises a legitimate merge of showings, because one prediction cannot cover two intervals.
- It hides nothing beyond what the labeled:false skip already hides.

Sample sizes:
- ±5 points at 95%: n = 246 independent fields at p = 0.8 (139 at p = 0.9). With within-sheet and repeat clustering (design effect 1.5 to 2), that becomes 370 to 490 rows from at least 50 distinct physical documents.
- A paired A/B detecting a 5-point change with 80% power needs about 250 to 310 paired fields (8 to 10% discordance).
- On video 5 alone (22 labelled fields), exact McNemar needs at least 6 flips in one direction with none the other way (p = 0.031); 5-0 gives p = 0.0625.

Change tools/compare_runs.py score() and markdown():
- Add Wilson CIs to labelled_fields, type and e2e.
- Add exact McNemar on the per_interval field_checks that already exist.
- Add a bootstrap over physical-document clusters (repeat_of chains).
- Add a 'per physical document' view (first showing only).
- Add verdict 'inconclusive' when p >= 0.05.
Do the same in deploy/evaluate_server_results.py aggregate().
findings.evidence: tools/compare_runs.py:154-156 pools only correct/total; :164-165 per_interval field_checks; :244-251 'Fields that changed' printed with no test; deploy/evaluate_server_results.py:41-46 'Pool numerators and denominators' without intervals; GT repeat_of on sample-04-page-004/005 and sample-05-page-004/005/006 (computed); sample-05 has 22 labelled fields (computed).
findings.expected_speed_effect: Prevents accepting phase-1 speedups, or rejecting them, on accuracy noise. A speed change ships only without a significant regression.
findings.expected_precision_effect: No change to the point estimate. Makes the ±11.7-point interval and the clustering explicit, and stops 1-to-3-field swings being read as improvements.
findings.risk: Bootstrapping over so few clusters (about 4 document identities today) is unstable. Report it as indicative until more videos are labelled.
findings.how_to_test: Unit tests: wilson(35,44) gives (0.655, 0.888); mcnemar_exact(6,0) gives 0.03125; (5,0) gives 0.0625 and the verdict is 'inconclusive'. Run compare_runs on today's main vs phase1 video-5 runs and check that the markdown shows the CI, the p-value and the verdict.

findings.title: Labelling plan, about 2.5 to 3 h for one person: migrate, convert, then the five short unlabelled videos
findings.claim:
Where the gaps are:
- The 7 unlabelled videos hold 190 leaves and took 6801 of 9222 V7 responses and 35377 of 48048 s (74% of both), with zero labels.
- The five short ones (20260821_144838: 11 leaves, 72 calls/leaf; 20260821_145110: 14, 56; 20260818-6_131851: 17, 49; 20260821_145342: 13, 46; 20260818_131702: 15, 34) are 70 leaves, 3524 calls and 19005 s (40%).
- TORG-12 and ТрН have no video labels at all, so 9 of the 19 fields are unmeasured on video.

Plan:

(1) 15 min. Address migration (finding 3) in analysis/ground-truth-expanded-review.html and the CSV's corrected_value and review_status columns, using the existing upd-parties-crop.png files. Confirm that the 4 consignor_address rows are postal-only.

(2) 20 min. Spot-check the 44 not_visible rows in the same HTML (already shown as 'Поле этой роли не видно на данной стороне') and set review_status=confirmed_not_visible. Send customer Q3 (8 UPD continuation number/date rows; the printed values are already in supplemental_observations).

(3) About 25 to 30 min per video for the five short ones, in the order above:
- a) Run `.venv/bin/python tools/inspect_video.py <video> analysis/<id> --interval 0.5` to get contact sheets of 24 tiles at 720 px.
- b) Group samples into leaves. start/end are midpoints and the brackets are the adjacent sample times, the same method as the existing boundary_uncertainty. Set repeat_of on revisits.
- c) Type each leaf. For unknown leaves, copy the literal heading.
- d) For target leaves, extract the sharpest sample at full resolution with `ffmpeg -ss T -i <video> -frames:v 1 analysis/<id>/selected-frames/original-NN.png`. For each required field choose exactly one of visible_readable (value plus raw literal; addresses as the entire block), not_visible_on_this_leaf, semantic_confirmation_needed, or illegible_in_capture.
- e) Run `tools/build_review_table.py --ground-truth <new.json> --csv <new.csv> --html <new.html>` for the customer employee.

(4) Before any scoring, set the 20260821_* videos to partition 'test'. Video 5 stays 'development'; it is the A/B video.

(5) A second person independently re-reads about 10% of the new value rows (about 20) to estimate the label error rate.

Expected yield, to be confirmed after the inventory: about 45 target leaves, giving roughly 100 to 120 new value labels and 90 to 110 abstention checks. Combined with the existing labels that is about 150 value labels (±6.5 points at p = 0.8). Reaching ±5 needs the target leaves of 20260818-3 (58 leaves) and 20260821_144256 (62 leaves), roughly 2 to 3 more hours. Use V7 document types only to rank which leaves to read first, never as values.
findings.evidence: analysis/monitor-native-v7-state.json:82-133 per-job result_pages/elapsed_seconds/responses for the 7 unlabelled videos and :64-70 (20260818-3, 2000 responses, 9976.98 s); deploy/evaluate_server_results.py:155-161 unlabelled videos 'accuracy_status': 'not_measured'; GT observed_target_types ['upd','ttn'], missing_target_types ['torg12','trn']; tools/inspect_video.py:13-87 contact sheets plus sampling.json; tools/build_review_table.py:43-51 CSV reviewer columns and :104-136 worksheet_rows; GT provenance 'no model/API predictions copied' (top-level provenance); GT partition at lines 49/3701.
findings.expected_speed_effect: Gives labels to the videos behind 40% (later 74%) of batch compute, so speed changes on them can be checked for precision.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Value labels rise from 44 to about 150, and to about 250+ after step 2 of the long videos. Brings the first TORG-12/ТрН labels if those types are present. Independent test partition.
findings.risk: Independence: the labeller must not see model outputs (current provenance forbids copying predictions). The pipeline's frame choice must not decide what gets labelled, which is why frames are extracted with ffmpeg. Repeat showings must be re-read, not copied. Yield is uncertain: high calls/leaf may mean mostly continuations, which give abstention rather than value labels.
findings.how_to_test: Record a timestamp per video in expansion.created_at and target at least 40 value rows per hour. After step 3, run deploy/evaluate_server_results.py (after finding 10) on the existing V7 results for these videos. Check the Wilson half-width on pooled labelled fields is at most 0.07, and the Cohen-style agreement on the 10% double-labelled rows is at least 0.95.

findings.title: Make seconds-per-sheet comparable: report speed per truth class and per repeat showing
findings.claim:
seconds_per_leaf is elapsed / len(pages), which depends on the leaf mix. V7 video 4 ran at 111 s/leaf (43 of its 53 intervals are out-of-scope) and video 5 at 275 s/leaf (5 of 15). Neither is comparable to the batch mean of 174 s/sheet or to each other.

Change compare_runs: join per_leaf to the evaluation details (prediction_page_id to truth_page_id) and tag each leaf in two dimensions.
- Content class: (a) target with visible labelled fields, (b) target whose required fields are all not_visible or semantic_pending (continuation or reverse), (c) out-of-scope.
- Showing: first, or repeat (repeat_of).

Report s/leaf, calls/leaf and the time share for each class, plus 'seconds on leaves with no visible labelled field'.

On today's video 5, class (b) is about 74% of wall time. Repeats are 5 of the 10 target intervals (pages 004, 005, 006, 014, 015), including 2 of the 4 hard leaves. That quantifies what cross-showing fusion could save if customer Q2 adopts a physical-document unit.
findings.evidence: tools/compare_runs.py:139 `summary["seconds_per_leaf"] = round(summary["elapsed_seconds"] / len(pages), 2)`; tools/compare_runs.py:118-127 per-leaf rows already carry interval, type, stop_reason and views; analysis/monitor-native-v7-state.json:42 (4123.89 s / 15 leaves) and :78 (5890.59 s / 53 leaves); GT repeat_of for sample-05-page-004/005/006/014/015; GT customer_questions[1] (unit: visible leaf vs physical document).
findings.expected_speed_effect: Turns 'seconds per sheet' into per-class numbers that can be compared across videos and versions. Identifies the roughly 74% (class b) and roughly 30-45% (repeats) targets for speed work.
findings.expected_precision_effect: None directly. Ties each speed change to the labels of the leaves it touches.
findings.risk: Needs labels for the video. For unlabelled videos, fall back to predicted class (stop_reason/type) and flag it as predicted. Reusing readings across showings would bend the two-frame-confirmation and no-replay rules unless the customer accepts the physical-document unit.
findings.how_to_test: Add a unit test with a 3-leaf truth (front, continuation, unknown) and synthetic per_leaf timings, and assert the class sums. Run compare_runs on today's video-5 main vs phase1 runs and check that class (b) is about 1970 s for main.

findings.title: Fix strictness bugs in normalize/comparison: quoted-day dates, unparseable literals, normalized-only matching
findings.claim:
I ran normalize/comparison directly (pure functions, no model calls). Three problems:
- Dates printed with a quoted day ('«20» августа 2026 г.' or '"20" августа 2026 г.', common in signature or header blocks) and abbreviated months ('20 авг. 2026') normalize to None.
- For two-digit years ('20.08.26'), comparison() returns None on both sides, and _value_matches requires `observed is not None`. Such a label can never be matched, even by an identical literal.
- _value_matches compares only the prediction's normalized_value. image_reader.py keeps a recognized value whose normalize() is None, so a correct raw literal is scored wrong.

Minor: in addresses, 'дом №158' does not equal 'дом № 158'. NFKC turns '№' into 'No', and the space after it then matters.

Changes:
- In the normalize() date regex, allow optional quote glyphs around the day.
- When date or number parsing fails, comparison() should fall back to the casefolded text() literal instead of None.
- _value_matches should fall back to comparison(name, found_raw_value) when normalized_value is None.
- Collapse '№\s*' to '№ ' for addresses.
The current 44 labels are unaffected, since they parse. The fixes matter for the new TORG-12/ТрН labels.
findings.evidence: sever/normalize.py:14-17 date regexes `(?<!\d)(\d{1,2})\s+(месяц)`, :29 `return None`, :59 numero handling, :63 final text() re-applies NFKC; sever/evaluation.py:49-53 `if found is None: return value is None` and `observed is not None and ...`; sever/image_reader.py:392-396 'If no safe normalized representation exists, keep the model's recognized status and exact raw value with normalized=null'; probe output: '«20» августа 2026 г.' gives norm None (NE); '20.08.26' gives both None (NE); 'дом №158' vs 'дом № 158' NE.
findings.expected_speed_effect: None.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Removes false 'wrong' outcomes on correctly read dates in quoted-day or short-year form. Small on today's 44 labels; meaningful on new form types.
findings.risk: The literal fallback must not weaken normalize(): tests/test_evaluation.py:42-45 requires normalize('31.02.2026') to be None. Keep that, and only compare the literals in comparison(). This stays consistent with the 'literal values' rule.
findings.how_to_test: Add parametrized cases to tests/test_evaluation.py:225: ('invoice_date', '«20» августа 2026 г.', '20.08.2026') EQ; ('document_date', '20.08.26', '20.08.26') EQ; ('consignor_address', 'дом №158', 'дом № 158') EQ. Keep the existing :238 'meaningful differences' cases NE. Add an evaluate() test where normalized_value is None and raw_value is correct, and expect ok.

findings.title: comparison() is more lenient than the literal rule: add a strict 'literal_exact' metric next to it
findings.claim:
comparison() maps 'Общество с ограниченной ответственностью' to 'ООО' (and likewise for ПАО, ЗАО, ОАО, АО and ИП) and casefolds everything. A test asserts that an expanded legal form equals the abbreviated one. The prompt, however, forbids expanding abbreviations, and the business rule is literal values with no expansion. An expansion error is therefore scored correct, and case errors are invisible; for example the label's own 'Профреш' vs the printed 'ПроФреш'.

Latin/Cyrillic homoglyphs, by contrast, are scored strictly (OOO vs ООО is NE). That is consistent with the README, but their mismatches are not reported as a separate class.

Change:
- Report literal_exact (NFKC, whitespace and quote glyphs only) alongside the current presentation_equivalent.
- Count presentation-only differences per field: legal-form, case, punctuation.
- Count confusable-script-only mismatches (fold a small Latin-Cyrillic confusable table for diagnostics only).
This shows whether the pipeline actually honours the literal rule, and separates glyph errors from content errors.
findings.evidence: sever/normalize.py:41 `result.casefold().replace("ё", "е")`; sever/normalize.py:43-52 legal-form canonicalization; tests/test_evaluation.py:226 `('consignor', 'Общество с ограниченной ответственностью "Диета +"', 'ООО «Диета+»')` asserted equal; sever/image_reader.py:66-67 'Не раскрывай сокращения и не добавляй отсутствующие сведения'; sever/evaluation.py:219 normalization_method 'Character-script aliases require per-field accepted_variants'; probe: 'OOO "УМНЫЙ РИТЕЙЛ"' (Latin) NE; 'Общество с ограниченной ответственностью "Умный ритейл"' EQ.
findings.expected_speed_effect: None.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Exposes literal-rule violations that are currently hidden, and splits errors into content, glyph and presentation classes. The headline number is unchanged.
findings.risk: Making literal_exact the headline would penalise formatting the customer may not care about. Keep it secondary until the customer decides.
findings.how_to_test: Unit test: the :226 pair stays presentation-EQ and becomes literal-NE; 'ООО "УМНЫЙ РИТЕЙЛ"' vs 'OOO "УМНЫЙ РИТЕЙЛ"' is NE under both and is counted as a confusable-only mismatch. Rescore today's two video-5 runs and compare the literal_exact vs presentation_equivalent gap.

findings.title: Measure formatting-only fusion conflicts: the fusion agreement key is stricter than the evaluation key
findings.claim:
fuse_readings compares dates and numbers by literal text (NFKC, case and whitespace only). The evaluator compares dates as ISO. Two frames reading '20 августа 2026 г.' and '20.08.2026' therefore become a 'conflict'. A conflict is then scored wrong because the status does not match 'recognized', and it triggers a joint review (55 of 424 calls on today's video 5).

First measure: across the V7 results and today's runs, count conflict fields whose recorded value_groups are all equal under normalize.comparison().

If the count is non-zero, compare dates and numbers in fusion through normalize() (ISO or digits). Each frame's raw literal stays as output.
findings.evidence: sever/image_fusion.py:53-60 docstring 'Numbers and dates use the unchanged literal comparison', :39-41 `_literal_comparison`; sever/image_fusion.py:174 `key = _field_comparison(name, field.raw_value)`; sever/image_fusion.py:211 value_groups with 'comparison' and 'frame_ids' persisted; sever/normalize.py:19-26 ISO canonicalization; sever/evaluation.py:133 status must equal wanted_status.
findings.expected_speed_effect: If such conflicts exist, fewer joint reviews and extra frames. Joint review is about 13% of video-5 calls; actual savings are unknown until measured.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Converts formatting-only conflicts into confirmed values that the evaluator already treats as equal.
findings.risk: Bends 'values must be literal' only for the agreement key, never for output. 'Two distinct frames agree' after date canonicalisation counts as presentation normalisation, which the stated rule allows; confirm with the customer. The prompt asks for printed form, so differing formats across frames may be rare.
findings.how_to_test: Offline script over the V7 and today's results.json (no model calls): for each field with status 'conflict', read the fusion value_groups and test pairwise comparison() equality. Report the count, and the joint_review calls on the affected leaves from trace.jsonl via tools/compare_runs.py trace_stats.

findings.title: Unblock scoring of new labels: remove the hard-coded 4-video check and add a review-CSV importer
findings.claim:
deploy/evaluate_server_results.py raises an error unless the truth has exactly 4 videos, so adding labels for any of the 7 unlabelled videos breaks server scoring.

Separately, build_review_table.py writes reviewer columns (reviewer_name, review_date, review_status, corrected_value, comments), but no code ever reads them back. The customer review and the address migration cannot flow into the truth JSON without hand-editing it.

Changes:
- Require that the 4 original hashes are present, accept additional videos, and aggregate per partition (development, test, negative_check).
- Add tools/import_review_csv.py. It applies review_status and corrected_value with reviewer and date provenance, refuses rows whose page_id, field_name or source_sha256 do not match the JSON, keeps customer_approved false unless the CSV status says 'approved', and never edits interval boundaries.
findings.evidence: deploy/evaluate_server_results.py:140-141 `if len(videos) != 4: raise ValueError("This evaluation requires the four original independently labelled videos")`; tools/build_review_table.py:43-51 CSV_COLUMNS incl. 'review_status', 'corrected_value'; :113 reviewer columns blank; repository grep: 'corrected_value' appears only in tools/build_review_table.py:49-50,113.
findings.expected_speed_effect: None.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Lets the new labels from finding 5 and the customer corrections reach the evaluator; without it they cannot be scored.
findings.risk: Lifting the 4-video check could silently change the 'all four originals as misses' denominator semantics. Keep that view restricted to the 4 originals and add a separate pooled view.
findings.how_to_test: Unit test with a 5-video truth fixture: run() succeeds, reports per-partition metrics, and the originals-only view is unchanged. Importer test: a CSV row with the wrong source_sha256 is rejected; a corrected_value row updates value and adds review provenance.

findings.title: Measure the out-of-scope 'unknown with heading' rule, which is not scored today
findings.claim:
The business rule says an out-of-scope form must be recorded as unknown together with its heading. unknown_rejection checks only document_type == 'unknown'. For unknown leaves the truth stores a descriptive observed_form ('Декларация о соответствии ЕАЭС', 'Акт, заголовок АКТ'), not the literal heading.

Change: label the literal heading for each unknown leaf, about 10 s each, or about 12 minutes for the 68 existing intervals. Score it with comparison-style text matching against the heading the prediction records, and report it as unknown_with_heading.
findings.evidence: sever/evaluation.py:117-121 `type_ok = not failure and prediction.get("document_type") == kind` with unknown counted only by type; GT unknown observed_form values such as 'Декларация о соответствии ЕАЭС', 'Официальное письмо на бланке' (sample-04/05 pages 007-053); sever/native_pipeline.py:183 'out_of_scope_form_confirmed' stop.
findings.expected_speed_effect: Small. It makes the cheap triage path (out-of-scope leaves cost 7 to 8 calls) checkable for content, so it can be tightened safely.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Adds 68 checks on a business rule that is currently unmeasured.
findings.risk: Need to confirm which result field carries the heading (classification_evidence or notes) and that it holds a literal heading rather than a description. Copying 'observed_form' as the label would be wrong; the heading must be read literally from the frame.
findings.how_to_test: Label the headings for video 5's 5 unknown leaves (pages 007-011), add the check, and rescore today's two runs. Expect 5/5 if triage records headings literally.

Do the 7 unlabelled videos, especially the 20260821_* videos recorded three days later, contain TORG-12 or ТрН fronts? Which video was the ТрН image-0005 ('153-1', ИП Боровинский) in the V8 comparison taken from?

Customer Q2/Q3/Q4: is the unit a visible leaf or a physical document? Does the own number/date on a UPD continuation count as invoice_number/date? Are fields printed only on the other side excluded or merged? These decide whether the 52 unlabelled rows become abstention checks or value labels, and whether reading across showings is allowed.

Was the V7 batch that produced 35/44 run under the pre-11.10 address prompt? If so, its consignee_address results should be scored against legacy_value, and today's main/phase1 against the entire-block label.
How much does run-to-run timing vary for the same arm on the llama.cpp server, given prefix caching and temperature 0? Two repeats per arm are needed before claiming speedups under about 10%.

read:fusion.area: Cross-frame fusion, stop policy and joint review (sever/image_fusion.py, sever/native_pipeline.py, sever/image_conflicts.py)
read:fusion.summary:
Phase1 has now been measured (analysis/ab-speed-20261017/comparison.md, video 20260818-5). It cut wall time from 2665 s to 1134 s and calls from 424 to 188. The 4 hard leaves went from 44/106/92/62 calls to 15/13/19/34. Labelled fields went from 16/22 to 15/22; the one lost field came from a joint review that returned "он же; ООО ..." as consignor_address.

Where the time goes in phase1: the six leaves that end in requires_other_document_side (0003, 0006, 0012-0015). They take 122 of 188 calls, about 821 of 1134 s (72%), and 33 of the 39 joint-review calls. They yield the same confirmed_fields in main and phase1.

Main read 51 more views on the 4 hard leaves than phase1 (9/20/15/9 vs 2/2/2/5). Its confirmed_fields were identical (0/2/0/2), so on this video the extra single-frame views gained nothing.

How a leaf's loop runs:
- Every read re-fuses all readings. Any second comparison key makes the field "conflict" for good (image_fusion.py:183), and only a joint review can override that (native_pipeline.py:552, :692).
- The initial field review runs once per leaf (:916), at view 2, on the same two frames.
- An other-side stop only counts if it comes from a joint review made at the current reading count (:821-823). If the initial review does not flag every unresolved field, nothing can stop the leaf on that ground until another review runs.
- Disagreements set stop=None (:910-913, :919-922). The leaf then reads until the pool is exhausted (V7) or until 3 views in a row bring no progress (phase1).
- The final review needs a fresh view that was already read singly (:197-222).

What the phase1 no-progress stop covers: leaves whose unresolved fields stay unreadable and whose other fields repeat the same keys. On 0015 it stopped after 5 views (34 calls) where main read 9 views (62 calls).

What it does not cover:
- Its 3-view window still costs about 15 agent calls (~135 s) on 0015.
- Any new comparison key counts as progress (:47-48), including new spellings of fields that are already in conflict, which fusion can never resolve. Long address and organisation fields can keep the search going indefinitely.
- It does not reduce joint-review cost.

Phase1's large gains on 0012-0014 came from the initial joint review becoming terminal at view 2. That rests on a single model answer, so it is fragile: when it fails, the leaf falls back to the 0015 path.

Ranked changes:
1. Accept two independent single-frame "other_document_side" claims, so the leaf stops at view 2 without a joint review. Estimated 4-22 calls (about 35-195 s) saved per hard leaf, up to about 35% of wall time on this video.
2. After a non-terminal review, allow a 1-view window and count progress only on unresolved fields that are not in conflict.
3. Stop the frame search once only conflicts remain, then run the final review.
4. Make the joint-review answer compact.

Majority voting would bend README:205 and the existing tests; a fixed per-leaf frame cap would bend README:38. All estimates come from per-leaf totals in comparison.json; no traces were opened.

findings.title: Let two independent single-frame 'other_document_side' claims end the leaf at view 2 without the joint review
findings.claim:
The only route to stop_reason requires_other_document_side today is a joint review. The single-frame schema has no visibility cause, so the pipeline cannot see per frame that a field is on the other side.

Change:
1. Add an optional per-field enum `visibility_cause` to ImageField (values such as other_document_side, occluded, blur_or_small_text, out_of_frame). It is allowed only with status=unreadable and should be a few output tokens.
2. Carry it into views[*] next to complete_page_visible.
3. In requires_other_document_side(), accept an unresolved field when either (a) it has the current joint assessment, or (b) at least 2 views with distinct frame_id, source_sha256 and timestamp_s, each with reading.complete_page_visible=True, mark it unreadable with cause other_document_side.
4. Before `await review_conflicts("initial")`, skip the review when every unresolved field passes (b).
5. Keep every existing guard: no reading ever proposed recognized, not_present or conflict for the field; no conflict fields; no type review pending.
6. Optional, on the agent side: tell the zoom agent to stop zooming for a field once it sets other_document_side.
findings.evidence:
- sever/image_reader.py:159-167: ImageField has only `reason: str | None ... "Brief cause, only for unreadable or not_present"` and no cause enum.
- sever/native_pipeline.py:821-823: `if any(name not in leaf_visibility_assessments for name in unresolved): return False` and `if any(leaf_visibility_assessments[name]["source_reading_count"] != len(readings) ...): return False`.
- These assessments are created only from joint reviews: native_pipeline.py:672-680 `if (field.status == "unreadable" and assessment.get("terminal_for_current_leaf") is True ... and assessment.get("action") == "obtain_other_document_side"`, which uses image_conflicts.py:330-336 `needs_other_side = (... item.visibility_cause == "other_document_side" and item.complete_page_visible ...)`.
- Measured, analysis/ab-speed-20261017/comparison.json (phase1): the six other-side leaves used joint_review calls 0003=5, 0006=5, 0012=7, 0013=4, 0014=6, 0015=6, which is 33 of 39 joint calls.
- Same leaves, field_agent calls: 15/2 views, 12/2, 6/2, 7/2, 11/2, 26/5. The TTN back-side leaves zoom 6-7.5 times per view, against 3-5.5 on clean leaves.
- Joint calls cost roughly 6-13 s each, estimated from leaf model seconds; e.g. 0012 took 95 s for 15 calls with 6 agent calls.
- README:205 itself calls the joint review "модельное разрешение" (model adjudication), not independent agreement.
findings.expected_speed_effect:
Best case on video5 phase1: minus 33 joint calls (about 280 s), plus 0015's views 3-5 and its final review (about 16 agent calls, about 137 s). That is about 1134 s down to about 720 s (-37%), and 75.6 down to about 48 s per sheet.

Per hard leaf: -4 to -7 calls (0012-0014, about 35-60 s) and about -22 calls on 0015 (about 195 s). If the per-frame model flags the other side on only half the leaves, expect about -200 s (-18%).

A side effect not yet checked: fewer agent zooms on TTN back sides (7.5 per view now).
findings.expected_precision_effect:
Neutral on labelled fields: these fields end unreadable today too (confirmed_fields 1/4, 1/4, 0/4, 2/6, 0/4, 2/6, the same in main and phase1).

Risk of recall loss where a joint review would have recovered a value the single reads missed; the guards above limit this. No value is ever confirmed by this rule.
findings.risk:
Business rules: no value is confirmed, two distinct frames are still required, and no previous answer is sent to the model.

It does change a design choice: today only a fresh joint review may declare that this side lacks a field (pipeline version "native-image-joint-leaf-visibility-v1").

Other risks:
- The per-frame model may over-use other_document_side on blurred frames; keep the requirement that the complete page is visible in both frames.
- Changing the schema changes the cached tool-schema prefix once.
- tests/test_native_conflict_pipeline.py expectations about the review happening need updating.
findings.how_to_test:
1. Offline, no model calls: in the phase1 run under /srv/sever/validation/ab-speed-20261017-191924/, open image-readings/page-0003, -0006 and -0012..-0015 .json. Compare views[*].document.fields[name].reason for the fields that ended unresolved with conflict_reviews[*].answer.adjudication.field_reviews[name].model_review.readings[*].visibility_cause. This estimates how often the single-frame reads already describe the other side.
2. Unit tests: two independent views with the claim make the leaf stop at view 2 with conflict_reader never called; a single claim, or any value proposal, still calls it.
3. Server A/B with deploy/ab_speed_test.sh (phase1-speed vs candidate) on 20260818-5_132107.mp4, then tools/compare_runs.py --truth analysis/ground-truth-expanded-provisional.json.
4. Pass targets: joint_review calls on the six leaves 33 down to 10 or fewer; their leaf_seconds sum from about 821 s to 550 s or less; stop_reason unchanged; labelled fields at least 15/22; no field that phase1 confirmed with resolution=fresh_joint_model_review becomes unresolved.

findings.title: After a non-terminal field review, allow one more view instead of three, and count progress only on unresolved, non-conflict fields
findings.claim:
Today, after the initial review fails to settle the leaf, the search waits for 3 consecutive views without progress (phase1), or all views (V7), before the final review.

Change record_progress():
1. Once a kind=fields review has finished unresolved for the current unresolved set, use a window of 1 view; keep 3 before any review.
2. Build _progress_state only from fields whose fused status is unreadable or pending, plus the document type.

New spellings of a field already in conflict cannot change fusion, because conflict is permanent until a joint review. Today they reset the counter.
findings.evidence:
- sever/native_pipeline.py:456-458: `if (no_progress_views is not None and leaf_progress["views_without_progress"] >= no_progress_views): leaf_progress["triggered"] = True`.
- :43-51: proposals come from every reading and every field, `proposals.add((name, "recognized", _field_comparison(name, field.raw_value)))` plus `statuses = tuple(sorted(...))`.
- sever/image_fusion.py:183: `conflict = explicit_conflict or len(values) > 1 or bool(values and absence_frames)`. A second key never disappears.
- Measured: page-0015 phase1 read 5 views (initial review at view 2, three views without progress, then final review), 34 calls, 301 s; 26 agent calls at about 8.8 s each.
- Main vs phase1 confirmed_fields on 0012-0015 are 0/2/0/2 in both runs, while main read 9/20/15/9 views against phase1's 2/2/2/5. The extra views added no confirmations.
findings.expected_speed_effect:
page-0015: views 5 down to 3, about -10 agent calls, about -90 s (-8% of video5 phase1 wall).

It also bounds every leaf whose initial review is non-terminal to 3 views plus 2 reviews. On main's 0013 pattern that is about 15 calls instead of 106.
findings.expected_precision_effect:
Expected neutral on this video, since main's extra views yielded zero confirmed fields.

Slight positive in general: fewer extra reads means fewer confirmed fields flipped into conflict by a later one-glyph variant (image_fusion.py:183). Possible small recall loss where a 4th or 5th view would have supplied the second agreeing frame. Views come ordered by quality (frame_pool.py:138), so later views are usually worse.
findings.risk:
No business rule is bent: nothing gets confirmed and the final review still runs (native_pipeline.py:958-960).

Update tests/test_native_conflict_pipeline.py:357-372 (asserts 5 views) and the _NO_PROGRESS_POLICY metadata.
findings.how_to_test:
1. Offline, deterministic code only: for each leaf of the 11-video V7 batch, run sever.image_fusion.fuse_readings over prefixes of image-readings/<page>.json fusion.readings. Record the view index at which each finally confirmed field first became confirmed, and count fields confirmed only after view (initial-review view + 1). This is the loss bound. Analysis only; outputs are never exported.
2. Then A/B on video5 with deploy/ab_speed_test.sh and compare_runs.
3. Pass targets: page-0015 requests 34 down to 24 or fewer; total requests at most 178; labelled fields at least 15/22.

findings.title: Stop the single-frame search once only conflict fields remain: one fresh view, then the final review
findings.claim:
When stop == "disagreements_preserved" and a fields review has already run unresolved, more single-frame reads cannot resolve the conflict; only a joint review can. They also add new value groups, which the final review must cover with at most 4 frames.

Change:
1. In that state, read at most 1 more view, the next best by quality, so the final review gets its required fresh frame.
2. Then break to the final review.
3. Record a truthful stop label, e.g. conflicts_sent_to_final_review, instead of source_views_exhausted.
4. Optional: let the final review take that fresh frame straight from the pool, using the leaf's shared rotation and a sha256 of the file. This saves the single read too.
findings.evidence:
- sever/native_pipeline.py:919-922: `if stop == "disagreements_preserved": # Unresolved conflicts do not cap the source-frame search. Revisit once at exhaustion with new pixels. stop = None`.
- :606-620: each comparison key becomes its own required group, `alternatives.setdefault(key, set()).update(cited) ... groups.extend(alternatives.values())`.
- :229-245: `choose()` must cover every group within `len(chosen) == 4`; if it cannot, :630-633 marks `blocked_fields ... "Joint review cannot cover every known readable side of this field's dispute"`.
- :217-222: the final review needs a fresh frame from `views`, which today means a frame already read singly.
- :1026-1028: exhaustion labels.
- Main video5 page-0013 ended source_views_exhausted after 20 views, 106 calls, 776 s.
findings.expected_speed_effect:
0 s on video5 phase1, where no leaf ended with an open conflict.

It is a tail guard for address- and organisation-heavy conflict leaves, where variant churn defeats the no-progress counter. On the main-0013 pattern it saves roughly 10-17 views (about 40-65 calls, 250-550 s). It also protects the 2000-call job budget that 20260818-3 hit.
findings.expected_precision_effect:
Positive for the known class 'cross-frame conflicts never resolved': with fewer value groups, the final review can cover every disputed side, so fewer fields end up blocked.

No field can become wrongly confirmed, because resolution still needs two distinct frames inside the joint review (image_conflicts.py:303-318).
findings.risk:
This bends the documented search design (README:205 'продолжается на других пригодных видах без фиксированного числа кадров', and the comment at :920), not the two-frame rule.

tests/test_native_conflict_pipeline.py:80-95 asserts `seen == [all frames]` and must change.

If the optional direct-from-pool frame is used, it must still pass assess_frame_quality, as :844-854 does.
findings.how_to_test:
1. Offline on the V7 11-video artifacts: count conflict_reviews entries with phase=final and blocked_fields. For each conflict field, compare value_groups (fusion.field_confirmations[name].value_groups) with the number of views read.
2. Then A/B on a video with conflict-ending leaves, e.g. 20260818-4_132351.mp4.
3. Measure with compare_runs: requests per leaf, final-review status resolved/unresolved/skipped_incomplete_dispute_coverage, and labelled fields.

findings.title: Make the joint-review answer as compact as the phase1 single-frame answer
findings.claim:
The single-frame schema was compacted in phase1, so evidence_text holds the caption only. The joint-review schema was not: each of up to 4 frames times each field repeats the full value inside evidence_text, and resolution_reason may run to 2000 characters.

Generation is 69% of phase1 model time (61 tok/s).

Change:
1. For recognized/not_present readings, evidence_text becomes caption only; raw_value already carries the value.
2. Keep visible context only for unreadable readings, which the other-side check needs (image_conflicts.py:335 `bool(item.evidence_text.strip())`).
3. Cap resolution_reason at about 300 characters, one sentence.
findings.evidence:
- sever/image_conflicts.py:163: `evidence_text: str = Field(max_length=4000, description="Verbatim role/caption and value from THIS frame, without repairs")`.
- :172: `resolution_reason: str = Field(max_length=2000, ...)`.
- INSTRUCTIONS :64-65: `В evidence_text копируй именно видимую подпись и текст этой строки дословно, включая продолжение адреса`.
- Compare sever/image_reader.py:125-127: `evidence_text quotes only the field's own printed caption ... never the value again`, and :164.
- analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md: 'generation 41,696 tokens in 688 s (61 tok/s) = 69% of model time'.
findings.expected_speed_effect:
Estimate -30 to -50% of joint-review output tokens. With about 39 joint calls at roughly 8 s each on video5, that is about -40 to -80 s (-4 to -7%).

The gain shrinks if finding 1 removes most other-side reviews; conflict reviews (0004, 0005) remain.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Neutral. Values and panel citations are unchanged, and evidence still cites panels that were actually sent (image_conflicts.py:267-276).
findings.risk: Reports lose the duplicated value text in evidence for joint reviews; the raw value stays. The schema hash changes once. tests/test_image_conflicts.py fixtures with long evidence_text may need updating.
findings.how_to_test:
1. Extend tools/compare_runs.py to sum output_tokens per call kind. Rows are already attributed via CALL_KINDS['image_conflicts_observation']='joint_review'.
2. A/B on video5. Pass targets: joint_review output tokens -40%, joint seconds down, labelled fields unchanged, tests/test_image_conflicts.py green.

findings.title: Per-mode request cap for joint reviews: about 5 for unreadable-only or type reviews, 12 kept for real conflicts
findings.claim: Every joint review gets 12 requests and 12 crops. Reviews whose requested fields are all unreadable with no disputed groups mainly have to decide visibility or side; type reviews are similar. Cap both at about 5 requests and 6 crops, and keep 12 where readable sides disagree.
findings.evidence:
- sever/image_conflicts.py:30-31: `MAX_MODEL_REQUESTS = 12`, `MAX_ZOOM_IMAGES = 12`; enforced at :428-429, :463-464 and :527 `UsageLimits(request_limit=MAX_MODEL_REQUESTS)`.
- The cap is hard-coded in the instructions too: :105 `не более 12 запросов` and :140.
- Groups are empty for unreadable-only fields: native_pipeline.py:605 `if groups or document.fields[name].status == "conflict":`.
- Phase1 joint calls per leaf: 0012=7 (one review, 2 views), 0014=6, 0015=6, 0003=5, 0006=5, 0013=4.
findings.expected_speed_effect: About -7 to -9 joint calls on video5 (about -50 to -75 s, -5%). Only reviews running past 5 requests are affected.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Neutral to slightly negative: fewer zooms can turn a terminal other-side verdict into read_more_views, which costs more views. Watch the terminal rate.
findings.risk: A tighter cap may push leaves onto the fallback path, a net loss unless finding 2 is in place. The cap must change together with the 12 written into the instructions.
findings.how_to_test:
1. Offline: from the V7 and phase1 artifacts, take the distribution of conflict_reviews[*].answer.recognition.model_requests (image_conflicts.py:541) by review kind, and the terminal/resolved rate for reviews that used more than 5 requests.
2. A/B on video5: joint calls, number of terminal verdicts, stop_reason per leaf.

findings.title: Remove over-broad blockers that keep requires_other_document_side from firing
findings.claim:
Three guards block the other-side stop for reasons unrelated to the field:
- (a) An assessment is valid only at exactly the reading count of its review. This is redundant with the later scan over all readings, which already rejects any value or blank proposal.
- (b) Any error on any reading blocks the stop, including heading-citation errors that have nothing to do with the field.
- (c) Any failed view blocks it, including a frame that simply used up its 8-request allowance.

Change:
1. Drop (a).
2. Count only errors prefixed '<unresolved field>:'.
3. Treat failed non-persistence attempts like unread frames, which phase1 already accepts for no-progress stops. Keep EvidencePersistenceError blocking.
findings.evidence:
- sever/native_pipeline.py:823: `leaf_visibility_assessments[name]["source_reading_count"] != len(readings)`.
- :827-829: `return not any(reading.errors or any(field.status == "conflict" or (name in unresolved and field.status in {"recognized", "not_present"}) ...`.
- :810: `if (document.document_type == "unknown" or document.errors ...`; fusion copies every reading's errors (image_fusion.py:121).
- :813: `if any(attempt.get("status") in {"failed", "stopped"} for attempt in attempts): return False`.
- Error formats: image_reader.py:376 `"Model document type has no supplied-panel heading evidence"` (no field prefix) and :413 `f"{name}: {rejection}"`.
- Per-view budget errors: image_agent.py:228-229 `raise ViewBudgetExceeded(...)`, caught as a failed attempt at native_pipeline.py:940-941.
findings.expected_speed_effect:
0 on video5 phase1, where all six leaves reached the stop. In V7, main 0013 ended source_views_exhausted after 20 views, consistent with a blocker.

It is a tail guard: an affected leaf saves its remaining views plus the final review (roughly 10-60 calls).
findings.expected_precision_effect: Neutral; the fields stay unreadable. The field-specific readable-proposal guard at :827-829 is kept.
findings.risk: A failed view might have held a readable value, but the phase1 no-progress stop already leaves views unread on the same reasoning. Keep persistence failures blocking, since they are an audit-trail rule.
findings.how_to_test:
1. Offline over the V7 batch image-readings/*.json: find leaves where stop_reason is not requires_other_document_side, every remaining field is unreadable and has a leaf_visibility_assessments entry, and classify which guard failed (document.errors text, attempts[*].status=failed with error_type, or a stale source_reading_count).
2. Add unit tests for each relaxed guard.

findings.title: Align the joint review's 'он же' rule with the single-frame contract
findings.claim:
The joint-review instructions tell the model to keep both real lines when it expands «он же». The single-frame contract forbids returning «он же» as a value.

In phase1 on video5, the only labelled regression (page-0004 consignor_address) happened because two single reads differed by one letter (Кашириных/Каширных). The joint review then returned 'он же; ООО "ФРЭШ-ЭКСПРЕСС", 454004, …'. Joint values replace the fused value, so the joint review created a third boundary.

Change: add to the joint INSTRUCTIONS that raw_value never contains «он же». For он же, raw_value is the seller's own value, and the reference line belongs in evidence_text, as image_reader.py:138-140 says.
findings.evidence:
- sever/image_conflicts.py:61-63: `Ссылка «он же» из СОСЕДНЕЙ строки к этой роли не относится. Раскрывай ссылку только когда она буквально напечатана в собственной строке запрошенного поля; тогда сохрани отдельно обе настоящие строки.`
- sever/image_reader.py:138-140: `If грузоотправитель says «он же», resolve ONLY that explicit reference ... Do not return «он же» itself as a name or address.`
- Joint values replace the fused field: native_pipeline.py:692 `document.fields[name] = field`.
- analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md describes the page-0004 regression.
findings.expected_speed_effect: None.
findings.expected_precision_effect:
Joint-review output becomes consistent with the single-frame contract. On the current provisional labels the gain is +0 or +1 field, because the label holds the postal part only and predates the 11.10 boundary; the label boundary also needs a decision.

It also prevents an 'он же' prefix on any joint-resolved address in the batch.
findings.risk: A prompt change only; the joint prompt's SHA changes. Wording must not push the model to cut the entire printed block, which the 11.10 rule still requires.
findings.how_to_test:
1. Scan the V7 batch and phase1 results.json for recognized fields with resolution fresh_joint_model_review whose raw_value contains 'он же' (case-insensitive).
2. A/B on video5: page-0004 consignor_address must not start with 'он же'; compare_runs labelled fields.

findings.title: Final-review frame selection: maximise fully covered fields instead of all-or-nothing coverage
findings.claim:
_conflict_review_frames merges the dispute groups of all fields into one list. When they cannot all fit into 4 frames, it falls back to the four best-quality frames, so fields that could each have been covered may be blocked.

Change: if the union does not fit, choose the subset of fields that maximises the number fully covered, starting with fields that have the fewest groups. Review those and block the rest. Optionally, a second review covers the remainder.
findings.evidence:
- sever/native_pipeline.py:626: `required_frame_groups=[group for groups in required_groups.values() for group in groups]`.
- :229-245: `choose()` returns None unless every group is covered within 4 frames.
- :251-254: `# If all groups cannot fit ... Returning quality-ranked pixels` then `return candidates[:4]`.
- :630-633: blocked_fields is computed per field against those frames.
findings.expected_speed_effect: Neutral, or +1 review in rare cases.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Positive for 'cross-frame conflicts never resolved' on leaves with two or more disputed fields. Resolution still needs two distinct frames inside the review (image_conflicts.py:303-318).
findings.risk: More complex selection. Must keep the fresh-frame requirement for the final review (:224-226). Extend tests/test_native_conflict_pipeline.py:327 (field stays conflicting when its evidence cannot fit).
findings.how_to_test:
1. Unit test: two conflict fields whose union needs 5 frames, while each needs at most 4.
2. Offline: count conflict_reviews entries with blocked_fields in the V7 batch, and how many of those fields could have been covered on their own.

findings.title: Hard per-leaf frame or call cap (e.g. at most 6 single reads or 40 calls) as a budget backstop
findings.claim: Add a configurable per-leaf ceiling on single reads or calls that ends the search and runs the final review, recording 'leaf_budget_reached'. It bounds the worst case on the main-0013 pattern (106 calls) and protects the 2000-call job budget that made 20260818-3 fail at 54/58 pages.
findings.evidence:
- README.md:38: `Фиксированного ограничения числа кадров на лист нет: остаются пригодность входа и общий бюджет.`
- sever/native_pipeline.py:1031 and :1101 export `"frame_count_limit": None` and `"per_leaf_frame_limit": None`.
- The candidate iterator never ends early: :802-807 (`yield from pool`).
- analysis/monitor-native-v7-state.json: job 20260818-3 `"status": "failed" ... "responses": 2000`.
findings.expected_speed_effect: 0 on video5 phase1 (max 5 views). In V7 terms, -7 to -14 views per extreme leaf (about -35 to -70 calls). Mostly a guarantee on the tail and on whole-job failure.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Avoids losing whole jobs (the 4 unread pages of video 3). Per leaf, a small risk of missing a late confirmation; prefix fusion can measure it offline.
findings.risk: Bends a documented design statement (README:38) and changes the exported limit fields from None. Needs owner or customer agreement.
findings.how_to_test:
1. Offline prefix fusion on the V7 batch, as in finding 2, for caps of 4, 6 and 8 views: count confirmed fields lost.
2. Batch A/B: jobs reaching 2000 requests, total requests, labelled accuracy via compare_runs.

findings.title: Not recommended without customer sign-off: majority of three or more frames with strict digits
findings.claim:
Accepting a value when at least 3 distinct frames agree, the other variants share its digit sequence, and no digits differ would turn some conflicts into values. It explicitly bends README:205 ('большинство кадров не разрешает спор') and two test families.

It would also confirm systematic errors that recur across frames: role confusion (document creator taken as consignor), and repeated glyph misreads such as РИТЕЙЛ read as РИТЕИЛ or 'соор.' read as 'корп.'. Those differ in letters, not digits, so 'digits strict' does not catch them.

On video5 phase1 no leaf ended in conflict, so there is no speed gain there. Evaluate it only offline.
findings.evidence:
- README.md:205: `Значения, различающиеся после сравнения допустимого оформления, сохраняют conflict; большинство кадров не разрешает спор.`
- tests/test_image_fusion.py:235-243: `# A repeated majority cannot hide one genuinely different model proposal.` (f1, f2, f3 with f1 == f3 must give conflict).
- tests/test_image_fusion.py:280-290 `test_numeric_or_script_disagreement_is_not_repaired_or_majority_selected`.
- image_fusion.py:183.
findings.expected_speed_effect: About 0 on video5 phase1. In V7 it could end some conflict leaves earlier, but findings 2-3 do that without bending the rule.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Uncertain to negative for precision of emitted values. Labelled accuracy may rise only where the majority is right; systematic errors would now be emitted as confirmed.
findings.risk: Directly bends README:205 and the corroboration semantics; the customer must agree.
findings.how_to_test: Offline only, never exported: apply the policy to stored fusion.readings in results.json of the 4 labelled videos, score with sever.evaluation against analysis/ground-truth-expanded-provisional.json, and report fields gained vs fields newly wrong.

findings.title: Small presentation-equivalence extensions (ё/е; № prefix; trailing г.) are low value and conflict with tests
findings.claim:
The 'accept the best-quality frame when the other differs only in punctuation' idea is already mostly built in for party names and addresses. What remains strict is deliberate: separators next to digits, a leading '№' on numbers, date forms, and legal-form expansion.

The only gap that matches evaluation is ё/е: evaluation folds it, fusion does not. Folding ё/е in the fusion key cannot lower labelled accuracy.

Treating '№ 2560' as '2560', or '20.08.2026 г.' as '20.08.2026', contradicts explicit test cases. Choosing the raw value from the highest-quality frame within an agreeing group changes presentation only and does not affect labels.
findings.evidence:
- sever/image_fusion.py:39-41: `_literal_comparison` uses NFKC, casefold and whitespace only.
- :53-90: quote, period and separator rules for organisation/address fields.
- sever/normalize.py:41: evaluation does `result.casefold().replace("ё", "е")`.
- tests/test_image_fusion.py:232-233: `("invoice_number", "№ 2560", "2560")`, `("invoice_date", "20.08.2026", "20 августа 2026 г.")` must stay conflict.
- tests/test_image_fusion.py:139: legal-form expansion must stay conflict.
- image_fusion.py:189: `original = next(iter(values.values()))[0]` (the first-read raw value).
findings.expected_speed_effect: Small: each avoided conflict saves one joint review of about 2-4 calls. Frequency unknown.
findings.expected_precision_effect: ё/е: 0 to +, never negative against the current evaluation. The №/г. rules: + on recall, but they contradict tests.
findings.risk: ё/е is a letter difference; it bends README:213 ('сохраняя разные слова') only marginally. The №/г. rules reverse explicit test decisions.
findings.how_to_test: Offline: rerun fuse_readings with the extended key on stored readings from the V7 batch, count conflicts converted to recognized, and score with sever.evaluation.

open_questions: Why did main's initial joint review at view 2 not settle pages 0012-0014, when phase1's did (main read 9/15/20 views)? The next step is to compare conflict_reviews[0].answer.adjudication.field_reviews[*].additional_evidence and the blockers (document.errors, failed attempts) in both runs under /srv/sever/validation/ab-speed-20261017-191924/. If the cause is model nondeterminism rather than a code path, phase1's gain on hard leaves is fragile.

How long do joint-review calls take? The roughly 6-13 s per call used here is estimated from per-leaf totals. compare_runs reads llama.cpp timings per response but does not yet group them by call kind.
On the TTN back-side leaves, do the per-frame `reason` strings already say the field is on the other side? That is the expected hit rate for finding 1; it can be checked without model calls.

Did any of the 6 other-side leaves get a confirmed field from the joint review (resolution=fresh_joint_model_review), or were all confirmations two-frame fusion? If some came from the joint review, finding 1 needs a fallback that still runs the review for those fields.
Should labels follow the 11.10 entire-block address boundary? page-0004 consignor_address is a label-boundary question as much as a model one.
Fields on the other side of a sheet would need front/back pairing across leaves, which is outside this area. README:205 notes a back side with a different number, so automatic merging is risky.

read:segmentation.area: Sheet detection and frame selection (sever/video.py, sever/frame_pool.py, sever/quality.py, sever/evaluation.py matching, analysis/ground-truth-expanded-provisional.json)
read:segmentation.summary: The starting premise is wrong. "8 missed intervals" counts all 88 labelled intervals, not the 20 target intervals. V7 got 14/20 target types right, and evaluation.py:117 only credits a type when the interval was detected, so at most 6 targets can have been missed. Replaying the strict matcher on the V7-era leaves (53 for video 4, 15 for video 5) gives 7 misses: 6 non-target intervals in video 4 and 1 target interval in video 5. Its 7 unmatched predictions equal the 7 that V7 reported. The 8th miss is presumably in video 2, where V7 found 11 leaves for 12 intervals. Today's main and phase1 runs show the same thing on video 5: the only target miss is sample-05-page-005. That miss is a scoring artifact. The leaf was found ([18.93, 21.59], TTN, all fields confirmed), but its primary frame at 21.32 s is 0.15 s past the label's approximate end of 21.17 s. The label's own end range is [20.66, 21.69], and the frame was reviewed as a usable TTN front. So on the labelled data, segmentation costs at most 4 of 44 fields, and those 4 are a matching artifact; it is not the biggest loss. The real segmentation weaknesses are: (1) the primary frame is chosen by a noisy score and lands on the first or last sample of a leaf too often, sometimes right as a page turn starts; (2) the confirming second frame is almost always the very next sample, 0.53 s away and nearly identical; (3) short fragments and repeat showings cost model time (repeat showings are 56% of phase1 wall time on video 5). Phase1 reads exactly 2 views on 14 of 15 leaves, so the primary and first seed chosen in video.py matter more than frame_pool ranking, which ran on only 1 leaf. Glare is not a factor in this footage: the near-white indicator is about 0 on all 174 kept frames of video 4. Everything below can be measured with CPU only: analyze_video plus sever.evaluation.evaluate against the truth file. No model calls are needed, except to confirm the effect of the seed and ranking changes on field precision.

findings.title: Correct the missed-interval metric: 1 of 20 targets missed (not 8), and that miss is a boundary artifact
findings.claim: Report target-only detection separately from all-interval detection, and add a second matching mode that uses the truth's own boundary_uncertainty ranges. Keep the strict mode. In the second mode a truth interval [start_bracket_s[0], end_bracket_s[1]) accepts a prediction whose primary falls inside it, and the matching is a global one-to-one alignment in time order. A simple dynamic program that maximises matches, tie-broken by distance to the interval midpoint, is enough. The current loop matches greedily in truth order, and that would steal matches once the windows overlap. In my replay, greedy matching with brackets moved one miss from interval 012 to 013. Today the dashboards call all-interval detection 'Labelled intervals detected', which is how 8 misses over all intervals became '8 of 20 targets'.
findings.evidence: analysis/monitor-native-v7-state.json:155-162 "correct_labelled_fields": 35 … "correct_target_types": 14, "target_intervals": 20, "missed_intervals": 8, "unmatched_predictions": 7. sever/evaluation.py:111-117 a missed interval gets prediction={} and `type_ok = not failure and prediction.get("document_type") == kind`, so 14 typed targets means at least 14 detected. sever/evaluation.py:203 `"detection": _metric(detected, len(expected)…)` counts all intervals. tools/compare_runs.py:162 `"intervals_detected": _count(report["detection"])`, shown at :242 as "Labelled intervals detected". sever/evaluation.py:108 `if timestamp is not None and start <= timestamp < end:` is a strict window. Replay of the strict matcher on the V7-era leaves (analysis/selected-frame-usability-full.json entries, 53 for video 4 and 15 for video 5): video 4 misses 007, 012, 023, 027, 030 and 032, all non-target; video 5 misses only 005 (TTN, 4 labelled fields); unmatched predictions 6+1=7. analysis/ab-speed-20261017/comparison.json per_interval: sample-05-page-005 has prediction_page_id null in both runs; leaf page-0005 has interval_s [18.93, 21.59], document_type ttn, stop all_required_fields_confirmed. Truth file line 4413 boundary_note: «Автоматический основной кадр 21.324244с выходит за неизменённую границу 21.174306с»; end_bracket_s [20.657856, 21.690756]. selected-frame-usability-full.json clip 5 page-0005 at 21.32 s: decision usable, observed_form "TTN front". With brackets and optimal matching: video 4 misses 6→2 (012 is a blank reverse side; 032 is an appendix continuation merged with 031), video 5 1→0.
findings.expected_speed_effect: None directly. It does keep the team from spending effort on segmentation thresholds that do not move the labelled metric.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Measured labelled-field precision on video 5 rises from 16/22 to up to 20/22, because the 4 fields of sample-05-page-005 become scorable. Its leaf confirmed all 4 TTN fields, and the same document's front scored 4/4 on page-0002; the values themselves were not checked here. V7's 35/44 becomes up to 39/44. Target detection goes from 19/20 to 20/20.
findings.risk: README.md:253 documents strict primary-timestamp one-to-one matching, so publish this as an extra metric rather than silently replacing the headline number. A bracket window can credit a primary that shows the neighbouring sheet. Type and value checks still apply, so this only inflates the score when the neighbour has the same type and values, i.e. a repeat showing. Videos 1 and 2 have no boundary ranges, so they fall back to strict. Labels are not edited, so no business rule is bent.
findings.how_to_test: No model calls. For each run on the server, evaluate(results, truth_video) in strict and bracket modes, then compare details[].detected and unmatched_predictions. Expected: video 5 strict 14/15 vs bracket 15/15 (targets 9/10 vs 10/10). The V7 finish-evaluation.json should show 8 misses split as about 6 non-target in video 4, 1 target in video 5 and 1 in video 2. A segmentation-only check also works: evaluate({'source':{'sha256':v['source_sha256']}, 'pages': json.load(open('video-analysis.json'))['pages']}, v).

findings.title: Pick the primary frame from inner, turn-free samples (the current score is noise and favours leaf edges)
findings.claim: Change the primary score at video.py:478-487. (1) Compute motion against the previous and next samples in time order, including discarded turn samples and samples of the adjacent leaf. Today only same-leaf neighbours are used, so the motion into a page turn is never seen. (2) Multiply by a centrality weight, e.g. w=sqrt(min(1, 2*min(k, n-1-k)/(n-1))), or exclude the first and last sample when n≥3. Apply the same rule to seed eligibility (video.py:489-503). Bump algorithm_version (video.py:414) so cached analyses are rebuilt.
findings.evidence: sever/video.py:482 `neighbors = [j for j in (i - 1, i + 1) if j in group_members]`. :484 `scores[i] = float(np.sqrt(features[i].quality["sharpness_laplacian_variance"] / sharpest) / (1 + 4 * motion))`. :88-94 sharpness is the Laplacian variance over every pixel brighter than 115 in a 384-px thumbnail. In output/accuracy-review/video4-segmentation-observed.json the score spread within a leaf has median 0.039 (scores 0.79-0.85), i.e. noise. In leaves with ≥3 samples, 26 of 51 primaries are the first or last sample, against 19.5 expected if positions were uniform. At least 5 of the 7 V7-era unmatched primaries are first or last samples: video 5 page-0005 at 21.32 (the last sample before the TTN reverse), video 4 page-0007 at 31.99, page-0022 at 82.04, page-0029 at 108.16 (all last) and page-0045 at 159.87 (first). output/accuracy-review/frame-000027.png, the 13.86 s primary of the video 4 TTN-reverse leaf, is the frame just before frame-000028's turn (tests/test_video_accuracy.py:72-82). Visually the sheet is already tilted and curled, with fingers in view, and its Laplacian variance (1580) is higher than the earlier calm samples (1466-1490).
findings.expected_speed_effect: Neutral to slightly faster: fewer first reads of curled or partly covered frames that lead to unreadable fields or conflicts. Not quantified.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Strict matching should recover sample-05-page-005: the leaf's inner samples at about 19.7-20.8 s lie inside [19.11, 21.17). That is +1 target interval and +4 labelled fields under the current headline metric, and fewer primaries that contain the incoming or outgoing sheet. The real reading-accuracy gain is probably small; most of the measured gain is the boundary artifact.
findings.risk: Leaves with 1-2 samples have no inner sample, so keep today's behaviour there. In a very short leaf the central frame can be blurrier; keep sharpness as a factor. No business rule is involved.
findings.how_to_test: CPU only. On the server, run analyze_video(source, fresh_dir) for the 4 labelled videos with the current code (A) and the patched code (B). Score each with evaluate() in strict mode. Report target misses (expected 1→0 on video 5), all-interval misses (expected 8→≤3), unmatched predictions, the share of primaries at the first or last sample (target ≈ Σ2/n, i.e. ≤40% instead of 51%), and the median |primary − truth midpoint|. A full analyze_video of video 4 took about 95 s (analysis/accuracy-speed-v8-progress.json:64).

findings.title: Make the confirming second view independent of the primary, not its closest twin
findings.claim: Choose the first seed as the highest-quality registered same_page sample at least 1.0 s from the primary (or from the other half of the leaf), tie-broken by larger mean_abs_difference. Use edge agreement only as a yes/no gate (same_page), not as a score multiplier. Do the same in frame_pool by putting the unused novelty term into the score and dropping the strength multiplier.
findings.evidence: sever/video.py:496-498 `strength = float(association.get("minimum_edge_agreement", 1.)); eligible.append((scores[i] * strength, i))` rewards similarity to the primary. :502 sorts by -score, then by time proximity. sever/native_pipeline.py:429-432 reads the primary first, then non-primary frames by -relative_selection_score. analysis/ab-speed-20261017/comparison.json leaves: phase1 read exactly 2 views on 14 of 15 leaves, so the first seed is the only second frame behind nearly every 'two distinct source frames agree' confirmation. In video4-segmentation-observed.json, 39 of 54 first seeds are the adjacent 0.53 s sample (median mean_abs_difference to the primary 0.052). sever/frame_pool.py:133 computes `novelty` but never uses it; :135-136 `score = relative_quality * strength`. analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md: on page-0004 the two frame reads already differed by one glyph («Кашириных» vs «Каширных»).
findings.expected_speed_effect: Slightly slower in the worst case: decorrelated frames may expose more disagreements, which trigger joint reviews (+5-20 s on affected leaves). It is neutral when both reads agree.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Fewer wrong values 'confirmed' by two nearly identical frames that repeat the same random misread. This does not fix systematic glyph errors such as Й→И. The effect cannot be measured without model calls; I expect it to be modest.
findings.risk: The two-distinct-frames rule is kept, arguably strengthened. A distant seed in a short leaf may be lower quality, so keep a quality floor of ≥0.9× the primary's sharpness.
findings.how_to_test: Offline, no calls: report the distributions of seed Δt and registered difference before and after on the 4 videos. Retrospective, no new calls, analysis only (not replayed into outputs): in V7 traces of labelled leaves, which read about 4 views per leaf, measure whether field errors coincide more often for view pairs <0.6 s apart than for pairs ≥1 s apart. Then run a model A/B on the 4 labelled videos and compare labelled-field correct counts and joint-review counts.

findings.title: Cut spurious short leaves: confirm 2-sample leaves too, and recognise a covered part of the same sheet
findings.claim: (a) Send 2-sample leaves with weak pair evidence (feature_hull_coverage < .2 or exposure rescue) through _confirm_short_candidates as well; today only singletons are checked. (b) In _regional_edge_agreement, treat a pair as the same sheet partly covered when only the A→B direction is inconsistent and B has fewer than 30% of A's edges in those cells.
