The per-cell counts are already computed. Today the worst direction decides alone, so a hand over part of the same sheet looks like a new sheet. (c) After confirmation, merge a short candidate into a neighbouring leaf whose anchor registers with it (e.g. inliers ≥100 and hull ≥.3) instead of emitting it as its own leaf.
findings.evidence: sever/video.py:291 `if len(group) != 1: kept.append(group); continue` (2-sample leaves skip confirmation). :141-144 `fraction = max(direction["inconsistent_edge_fraction"] …)`, `"partial_page_overlap": fraction >= .18`. :267-272 two consecutive pending samples that match each other open a new leaf. Scoring video4-segmentation-observed.json (an interim v8 segmentation) against the truth: 69 leaves for 53 intervals, 19 unmatched predictions, 13 of them singletons. Five lie inside target intervals: page-0005 in the 004 UPD; page-0008 in the 006 TTN reverse; page-0010, page-0011 and page-0013 in the 008 TTN continuation. analysis/accuracy-speed-v8-progress.json:54-56 "initial_candidate_count": 69, "old_candidate_count": 53, "new_singletons": 15, and 57 leaves before the final hull rule. Phase1 cost per leaf (comparison.md): out-of-scope 3 calls / ~6 s, target leaves with fields on the other side 19-22 calls / ~105 s.
findings.expected_speed_effect: Only where fragments occur. On the interim video 4 segmentation, the 5 target fragments plus 14 non-target fragments would cost about 5×100 + 14×6 ≈ 580 s, roughly 11 s per real interval at phase1 rates. The current code's fragment count is unmeasured.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Labelled-field precision is unchanged, because one-to-one matching ignores extras. Customer-facing precision improves: fewer duplicate or partial records, such as a TTN fragment read as a separate document.
findings.risk: Merging can swallow a genuinely brief different sheet (A, then B briefly, then A). The covered-sheet rule must require that B has no new printed edges in the inconsistent cells. Keep the existing tests (tests/test_video_accuracy.py:22-41, :98-120) passing.
findings.how_to_test: Unit tests: a synthetic page with a smooth skin-coloured blob over 30% should be same_page; the same page with a new printed sheet over 30% should stay partial. Offline on the 4 videos (analyze_video + evaluate): leaves per truth interval, unmatched predictions and fragments inside target intervals should fall, while target detection stays at 20/20 (bracket) or 19-20/20 (strict). Estimate cost as the sum over predicted leaves of the phase1 per-class seconds, with the class read from the truth interval at the primary's timestamp.

findings.title: Detect repeat showings offline (CPU); use them to save reads only after the customer agrees
findings.claim: Add a CPU-only repeat link: register each leaf's primary against the primaries of earlier, non-adjacent leaves and store `repeat_of_candidate` with its evidence on the page. Do not use _pair_evidence for this; its .075 inlier-fraction gate misses real repeats. Use a dedicated rule, e.g. inliers ≥80 and feature coverage ≥.35. With customer approval, a repeat leaf could then be read with one fresh view and confirmed against the original showing's confirmed reading (two distinct, actually-sent frames), or the two showings' frames could be pooled.
findings.evidence: Truth repeat_of links: sample-04 004→001, 005→002, 010→008, 011→009; sample-05 004→001, 005→002, 006→003, 014→012, 015→013. Phase1 seconds on video 5 repeat leaves 0004/0005/0006/0014/0015 = 54.6+59.4+109.1+107.6+301.3 = 632 s of 1134 s (56%) (comparison.json leaves). CPU check with sever.video._pair_evidence on local frames in analysis/sample-0{4,5}/selected-frames: UPD 2560 front vs its repeat → same_page True (259 inliers, coverage .40). UPD 2559 front vs its repeat → False with 99 inliers, coverage .64 and inlier fraction .072, just under the 0.075 gate (video.py:182 `count >= 16 and fraction >= .075 and coverage >= .08`). Different documents on the same template (UPD 2559 vs 2560, TTN 2559 vs 2560, UPD repeat vs repeat) → 42-54 inliers, fraction .031-.039, coverage .25-.28 → False. README.md:38 «двух разных исходных кадров того же листа»; README.md:98 «единица оценки — видимый интервал листа»; the truth's independent_field_review.customer_question asks whether repeat showings should be merged.
findings.expected_speed_effect: Linking alone saves nothing. Reading a repeat with one view instead of 2+ views plus joint review could save an estimated 30-50% of repeat-leaf time; on video 5 in phase1 that is about 190-320 s of 1134 s. This is an estimate.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Agreement across showings uses different hand positions and poses, so errors are less correlated than with adjacent frames. Wrong links are a risk if same-template documents are mislinked; on these 5 pairs the separation margin is about 2× in inliers.
findings.risk: It bends the per-showing leaf unit and the 'same leaf' wording of the two-frame rule (README.md:38, :98). It needs customer approval before any reading changes. Storing link metadata bends nothing. Answers come from the same run, not stored answers from earlier runs, but say so explicitly in the report.
findings.how_to_test: Offline: run the link rule over all leaf-primary pairs of the 4 videos and measure precision and recall against truth repeat_of. Truth labels repeats only on target forms, so review non-target links by eye. Add regression tests from the 5 local frame pairs above. Only after approval, run a model A/B on video 5 for repeat-leaf seconds and labelled fields.

findings.title: Re-rank seeds and pool frames by quality inside the unresolved fields' regions (not glare in this footage)
findings.claim: After each read, re-rank the remaining seeds and pool candidates instead of keeping the fixed frame_pool order. Keep the homography that _registered_pair_evidence already computes. Map each unresolved or conflicting field's Evidence.bbox (normalized to the saved source frame) into each candidate. Score Tenengrad or Laplacian sharpness, saturated-pixel fraction and skin fraction inside that box, on a 1080-px decode for pool frames or a native crop for seeds. Score = local sharpness × (1 − glare) × (1 − skin) × diversity (≥0.5 s from views already read).
findings.evidence: sever/frame_pool.py:128-138: ranking is computed once, from whole-paper sharpness of 384-px JPEG thumbnails (frame_pool.py:69 `scale=384:-2` … `-q:v 5`, a 5.6× downscale of 2160-px frames, too coarse to see glyph blur) times edge agreement. sever/video.py:163 `matrix, inlier_mask = cv2.findHomography(...)` is never returned. sever/video.py:87 drops the top 18% of the frame from features and sharpness. sever/schema.py:21 `bbox: list[float] | None` and sever/image_reader.py:369-370 attach `bbox=panels[identifier]["bbox"]` to every field's evidence. sever/video.py:75 `"glare_confirmed": None`; on all 174 kept frames of video 4, maximum_local_near_white_fraction ≤ 0.00016 and skin fraction exceeds 0.1 on only 4. In phase1 the pool ran on 1 of 15 leaves (page-0015: 5 views, 301 s, 27% of the run); in main on 4 leaves (9-20 views).
findings.expected_speed_effect: Only hard leaves that go past primary and seeds are affected. On video 5 in phase1 that is page-0015 (301 s); a better third view could cut 1-3 views (~60-180 s) there. Elsewhere there is no effect.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Better resolution of one-glyph conflicts and unreadable fields on leaves that need more views. Glare scoring will not help on this footage (indicator ≈0); occlusion scoring will help only a little (4/174 frames).
findings.risk: Extra CPU decode of about 0.1-0.3 s per candidate. A misread bbox steers the ranking wrongly, so fall back to whole-leaf ranking when a field has no bbox. No business rule is bent; the model still reads fresh, actually-sent pixels.
findings.how_to_test: Retrospective, no new calls: on the main A/B run's hard leaves 0012-0015 (9-20 read views each), compute the new score for every read view. Check the ROC AUC for 'this view's field reading agrees with the fused or confirmed value rather than unreadable or conflicting'. Unit tests: add synthetic blur, a saturated blob or a skin blob inside a bbox and assert the candidate is demoted. Then run a model A/B on video 5 for page-0015 seconds and views.

findings.title: Offline segmentation scorer and cached-feature parameter sweep (no model calls)
findings.claim: Add tools/score_segmentation.py. It reads video-analysis.json from analyze_video into a fresh directory, selects the truth video by source_sha256, and reports: strict and bracket detection, all intervals and targets only; unmatched predictions; leaves per truth interval; fragments inside target intervals; truth intervals merged into one prediction; primary first/last-sample rate and |primary − truth midpoint|; whether each labelled field's provenance.timestamp_s falls inside the matched leaf; repeat-link precision and recall; and a phase1 cost proxy. For sweeps, pickle _features for each 0.5 s sample once per video, plus dense-probe thumbnails, and re-run _segment_samples and _confirm_short_candidates with patched thresholds.
findings.evidence: Segmentation is CPU-only: sever/video.py:443-461 (ffmpeg plus OpenCV). sever/evaluation.py:89-114 already scores a pages list with no model results: undetected and unread leaves just lack result. Thresholds to sweep: video.py:154 ratio .72; :182 inliers 16, fraction .075, coverage .08; :188 residual .11; :186-187 exposure rescue .22/.90/.05; :135 cell agreement .55 and count 100; :144 .18; :244 ≥20 keypoints and bright ≥.25; :289 probe radius; :326 hull .2; :332 span .12. The truth gives boundary_uncertainty ranges and fields[].provenance.timestamp_s for every labelled field. analysis/accuracy-speed-v8-progress.json:64 shows a full regroup takes about 95 s on video 4.
findings.expected_speed_effect: Indirect. It lets fragment and merge changes be tuned for leaf count (seconds per sheet) in minutes rather than full model runs.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Indirect. It guards target detection (20/20 bracket) while thresholds change and catches regressions before any model run.
findings.risk: The labels are provisional and coarse: brackets are ±0.5 s for video 5 and ±0.77 s for video 4. Thresholds can over-fit to 4 videos, so hold 1-2 unlabelled videos aside for leaf-count sanity checks.
findings.how_to_test: On the server, where the sources sit in /srv/sever/input, run analyze_video for the 4 labelled videos (CPU), then the scorer. The baseline must reproduce today's numbers: video 5 strict 14/15 with 1 unmatched, video 4 targets 10/10. Confirm the sweep harness reproduces the uncached analyze_video groups exactly for the default thresholds before trusting other settings.

findings.title: Overlap CPU video work with model reading
findings.claim: Start reading leaf 1 while segmentation of later leaves continues, or at least extract full-resolution originals per leaf with a seek, as frame_pool does, instead of a second full decode pass. Prefetch each leaf's frame-pool scan in a worker thread while its primary and seeds are being read.
findings.evidence: sever/video.py:443 is a first full HEVC decode for sampling; :531-533 is a second full decode to write the PNG originals; :300-308 adds an ffmpeg probe per singleton. analysis/accuracy-speed-v8-progress.json:64 "full_video_regroup_seconds": 95 for a 184 s video. sever/native_pipeline.py:415-419 runs `next(iterator)` (the frame-pool ffmpeg scan) on the event-loop thread unless leaf_concurrency>1.
findings.expected_speed_effect: About 1.8-3 s per sheet, 2-4% of phase1's 75.6 s per leaf. Small, but it applies to every video.
findings.expected_precision_effect: None.
findings.risk: Leaves appearing out of order complicate partial reports and checkpoints. The exact source-PTS checks must remain.
findings.how_to_test: Compare the run_started → first page_selected trace interval and total wall time on video 4, with GPU work unchanged.

findings.title: Effective base sampling is 0.533 s; do not move the base to 0.25 s
findings.claim: Keep base segmentation sampling near 0.5 s and rely on the existing dense check for brief showings. If an exact 0.5 s step is wanted, use 0.49 so 30 fps footage steps 15 frames instead of 16. No labelled target interval was lost to sampling.
findings.evidence: sever/video.py:442 `gte(t-prev_selected_t,{effective_interval:.9f})`. In video4-segmentation-observed.json, 345 samples over 183.66 s gives 0.532 s spacing (e.g. 20.26, 20.79, 21.32), with avg_frame_rate 31010625/1033274 ≈ 30.01 fps. The shortest target interval, sample-04-page-011 (1.53 s), was detected in the V7-era leaves. Of the 2 non-target misses that remain under bracket matching, one is a blank reverse side and one is a merge of two look-alike sheets; neither is a sampling loss.
findings.expected_speed_effect: 0.25 s base sampling would roughly double feature extraction and pair comparisons on the CPU (~+95 s on video 4) and add fragment leaves, which cost model time.
findings.expected_precision_effect: No measurable gain on the labelled set.
findings.risk: Very brief, fully covered showings cannot be ruled out; the truth file says the same (inventory_limit).
findings.how_to_test: Use the sweep harness at 0.49, 0.5 and 0.25 s: count leaves, target detection (strict and bracket) and CPU seconds per video.

open_questions: Confirm on the server that /root/sever-validation/native-v7-evaluation/finish-evaluation.json splits the 8 misses as 6 non-target (video 4), 1 target (video 5, sample-05-page-005) and 1 in video 2. I could not read it, since ssh is not allowed.

How many leaves does the current code (algorithm_version 4, with the hull and dense checks) produce on video 4 and on the 7 unlabelled videos? The source videos are not on this machine, so fragments and merges in the current code are unmeasured.
Do the 4 values that page-0005 confirmed in today's runs equal the sample-05-page-005 labels? The comparison.json per-interval rows do not contain them.
Labelling convention: should a blank reverse side (sample-04-page-012 «Чистая оборотная сторона / перелистывание») count as a leaf interval at all? The segmenter drops it by design (video.py:244).
Customer decision on repeat showings (truth customer_question). It decides whether the repeat-link speedup may change reading or only add metadata.

Outside this area but larger than segmentation: TTN commodity continuation pages (sample-05-page-012 and -014, probably video 4's 008 and 010) are typed ТОРГ-12, which costs 4 of the 6 target type errors.

read:serving.area: Inference server configuration and throughput (deploy/sever-model.service, deploy/local-model.conf, deploy/README.md model sections, sever/agents.py request hooks, image encoding in image_agent.py/image_detail.py)
read:serving.summary:
The phase1 branch has in fact already been measured. analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md:22-24 and comparison.md:47 hold llama.cpp timings for 188 calls, and they show that decode dominates. Per call there are 3,403 new input tokens prefilled in 1.45 s (2,340 tok/s, including vision-encoder time), 222 output tokens generated in 3.66 s (61 tok/s), and 0.23 s outside the server timings. That is 69% decode, 27% prefill and 4% other; 68% of input came from the prefix cache. As a sanity check, a 27B at about 6.6 bits per weight is roughly 22-23 GB of weights, so the RTX 5090's ~1.79 TB/s gives a batch-1 decode ceiling of about 78-80 tok/s. The measured 61 tok/s is about 77% of that, so per-call kernel tuning can gain little. The real levers are batched decode across concurrent requests, fewer output tokens, and a model with fewer active parameters.

I simulated concurrency using the measured per-leaf costs. With N slots, prefill runs one request at a time and decode batches. In video order, video 5's leaf phase drops from about 1,007 s to about 730-760 s at N=2 and about 610-650 s at N=4. That is roughly 75.6 to 53-55 s per sheet at N=2, and to 46-48 s at N=4. The limit is the 301 s critical path of page-0015. Across a multi-video batch the throughput bound is about 1.45x at N=2 and about 2x at N=4. Once concurrency is on, prefill becomes the bottleneck, so cache breaks, image token counts and ubatch size start to matter.

I checked llama.cpp behaviour in the local checkout ~/llama.cpp (b7822, Jan 2026). It is not the deployed v0.6.0: the deployed binary accepts --no-reasoning-preserve, which b7822 does not. In b7822, when an mmproj is loaded:
- speculative decoding refuses to start;
- --cache-reuse is disabled;
- the host-RAM prompt cache is disabled;
- context checkpoints are disabled;
- without --kv-unified, --parallel N splits --ctx-size into equal per-slot shares, and a request over its share gets HTTP 400, which this code treats as a fatal stop of the whole batch;
- every image is bilinear-resized into the [min,max] token window, so the 1024 px context image is downscaled and then upscaled again.

The 26.2 GB of VRAM in use (gpu-phase1-speed.csv) points to a small KV cache, possibly a hybrid linear-attention model. If so, any prompt that differs from the cached one before its end forces a full re-prefill.

Recommended order:
1. Analyse the existing trace offline and read the startup log (no model calls needed).
2. Run --parallel 2 then 4 with --kv-unified, a sized context, and requests pinned to slots by id_slot.
3. Keep the tool list stable within a run.
4. Shrink zoom-call output with integer coordinates.
5. Size images to the server's token window.
6. Sweep ubatch size.
7. Treat an A/B against the MoE model as the user's decision.

None of these bends a README business rule. Values stay literal, every call is fresh, two distinct frames are still required, and image sizing makes the evidence images match what the model actually sees.

findings.title: Run 2-4 leaves concurrently on llama-server --parallel N, with --kv-unified, a sized context and slot pinning
findings.claim: Decode is 69% of model time and memory-bound at batch 1 (61 tok/s ≈ 77% of the bandwidth ceiling), so batching 2-4 decoding sequences costs little more per step than 1. Steps: 1) Restart sever-model with `--parallel 2 --kv-unified --ctx-size 131072`, keeping fa on and q8_0 KV. 2) Set HARNESS_LEAF_CONCURRENCY=2, then try 3-4. 3) Pin every request from leaf worker k to slot k by passing model_settings extra_body={'id_slot': k}; this needs a small code change to carry the worker index into AgentConfig. Without --kv-unified each slot gets 65536/N tokens, and a large joint review (4 context images + up to 12 crops of up to 4096 tokens each ≈ 55-60k tokens worst case) gets HTTP 400, which the code treats as fatal and stops the batch. Without pinning, llama.cpp's LCP-similarity slot choice (default threshold 0.1) can hand a new run another leaf's idle slot because the instruction prefix is shared, which destroys that leaf's conversation cache. Simulation from the measured per-leaf costs (prefill 1.45 s exclusive, decode 3.66 s batched, other 0.23 s): video-5 leaf phase about 1,007 s → about 730-760 s at N=2 and about 610-650 s at N=4, i.e. about 75.6 → 53-55 s/sheet (N=2) and about 46-48 s/sheet (N=4). Per-video wall is capped by page-0015 (301 s). A multi-video batch could reach about 1.45x throughput at N=2 and about 2x at N=4. Concurrency also hides the 11.8% of samples where the GPU sat idle.
findings.evidence: deploy/sever-model.service:12 `--ctx-size 65536 --parallel 1 ... --flash-attn on --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0`; sever/agents.py:133 `leaf_concurrency: int = 1  # native_image only`; sever/native_pipeline.py:1066-1090 worker pool `for position, page in queue` (video order); deploy/README.md:586-593 `При --parallel N контекст --ctx-size делится между слотами`; analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md:22-24 `generation 41,696 tokens in 688 s (61 tok/s) = 69% of model time`; gpu-phase1-speed.csv memory 26,180-26,683 of 32,607 MiB, 11.8% of samples at 0% utilisation. llama.cpp b7822: src/llama-context.cpp:173-177 `if (cparams.kv_unified) n_ctx_seq = n_ctx; else n_ctx_seq = n_ctx / n_seq_max`; common/common.h:437 `kv_unified = false`; tools/server/server-common.cpp:48-50 exceed_context_size_error `code = 400`; sever/image_agent.py:348 `fatal = ... status in {400, 401, 402, 403}` → :380-383 FatalProviderError `stop batch`; tools/server/server-context.cpp:932-963 slot chosen by `sim_cur > slot_prompt_similarity` (common.h:527 `0.1f`); server-context.cpp:2996 `task.id_slot = json_value(data, "id_slot", -1)`, :1700-1704 a busy pinned slot defers the task; pydantic_ai/models/openai.py:1214 `extra_body=model_settings.get('extra_body')`. With unified KV, an overflow at n_batch 1 sends 'Context size has been exceeded.' to every processing slot and clears them (server-context.cpp:2638-2668).
findings.expected_speed_effect: -25 to -40% seconds per sheet on video 5 (N=2 to N=4, in video order); about -30 to -50% for multi-video batches, which are throughput-bound
findings.expected_precision_effect: Neutral in expectation. Batched kernels are not bit-identical to batch 1, so temperature-0 readings can change by a glyph and two-frame agreement noise can shift either way; re-score the 22 labels.
findings.risk: VRAM: headroom is about 5.9 GiB. Read the startup line `llama_kv_cache: size = ... MiB`; 131072 cells cost about 2x that. Unified-KV overflow fails every in-flight request (HTTP 500 → failed views; 3 failed leaves in a row stop the batch), so size --ctx-size to the measured peak sum. The shared budget stop cancels sibling leaves (README:592-593). No business rule is bent: calls stay fresh and the two-frame rule is unchanged.
findings.how_to_test: After the README:627-662 idle procedure, restart sever-model with --parallel 2 --kv-unified --ctx-size 131072. Check /props total_slots=2, /slots n_ctx, and peak memory in nvidia-smi. Run deploy/ab_speed_test.sh with REF_A=phase1-speed REF_B=phase1-speed LEAF_CONCURRENCY_B=2: the A run uses concurrency 1 on the same server and serves as the control (script lines 20, 48-51, 129-130). Compare wall time, seconds per leaf, labelled 15/22, and grep the server log for 'selected slot by LCP similarity' with f_keep<0.5 (slot steals) and 'Context size has been exceeded'. Repeat with N=3 and N=4.

findings.title: Measure first, offline: per-call timing split, cache continuity, peak context, and the server's model/vision facts
findings.claim:
The existing phase1 trace (/srv/sever/validation/ab-speed-20261017-191924/phase1-speed/trace.jsonl) already holds per-response server_timings, cache_read_tokens and response_parts, but tools/compare_runs.py only sums them. Before changing flags, compute these from that trace (no model calls):
(1) Per call kind (orientation/triage/field_agent/joint_review): n, p50/p95/max of prompt_n, cache_n, predicted_n, prompt_ms, predicted_ms, and elapsed minus server time.
(2) Cache continuity per run: for consecutive responses, ratio = cache_n / (prev.cache_n + prev.prompt_n + prev.predicted_n). A ratio of about 1 is a clean continuation; about (prev.cache_n+prev.prompt_n)/expected means the re-rendered assistant turn did not match what the model generated; 0 means the cache was cleared.
(3) cache_n of the first request of every run, i.e. whether the about 7-8k-token instruction and schema prefix is ever reused across runs.
(4) max(cache_n+prompt_n+predicted_n) per kind, which sizes --ctx-size for --parallel.
(5) Output tokens by tool name (zoom_regions, zoom_source, submit_reading, submit_conflict_review, text parts).
Also grep the sever-model startup and runtime journal for: the architecture line; `llama_kv_cache: size` / recurrent memory (hybrid or not); `image_min_pixels` / `image_max_pixels` (exact vision token window); `failed to truncate tokens ... clearing the memory` and `forcing full prompt re-processing` (full re-prefills); `speculative` / `cache_reuse` / `prompt cache` warnings.
findings.evidence: sever/agents.py:182-184 keeps llama.cpp `timings`; :188-189 keys `cache_n, prompt_n, prompt_ms, ... predicted_ms`; :576-582 trace row with `cache_read_tokens`, `elapsed_seconds`, `server_timings`, `response_parts`; tools/compare_runs.py:84-87 and :106-107 only accumulate totals (`timings.update(...)`, `totals["server_timings"]`); analysis/ab-speed-20261017/comparison.md:47 shows totals only. llama.cpp b7822 log sources: tools/mtmd/clip.cpp:1263-1267 prints `image_min_pixels` / `image_max_pixels (custom value)`; tools/server/server-context.cpp:2437 `failed to truncate tokens with position >= %d - clearing the memory`; :2384 `forcing full prompt re-processing`; :962 `selected slot by LCP similarity`. The KV estimate (26,180 MiB idle) suggests about 2-2.5 GiB of KV at 65536 cells, consistent with a hybrid model; to be confirmed.
findings.expected_speed_effect: None directly; it settles which of the cache, context and output findings are worth doing and sizes --ctx-size for concurrency
findings.expected_precision_effect: None
findings.risk: None. Read-only analysis of existing artefacts; ground truth is not involved.
findings.how_to_test: Extend tools/compare_runs.py, or write a separate script, to emit per-kind percentiles, the continuity ratio histogram, first-in-run cache_n, peak context per kind, and output tokens per tool name from the trace above. Then run `journalctl -u sever-model | grep -E 'arch|kv_cache|recurrent|image_(min|max)_pixels|truncate|full prompt re-processing|speculative|cache_reuse|prompt cache'`.

findings.title: Stop hiding zoom tools mid-run: the changed tool list breaks the prefix cache for the final submit request
findings.claim: prepare_zoom removes zoom_source/zoom_regions from the request once 8 crops are used, or from the 7th request on. A single zoom_regions call may return all 8 crops, so the request that follows is often the one with hidden tools. Qwen chat templates render the tool list inside the first system turn, before every image, so this request differs from the cached prompt at the tool block. llama.cpp must then re-prefill the submit_reading schema (about 14.8k chars), the context image and all crops: about 10-20k tokens, roughly 4-9 s at 2,340 tok/s, instead of a few hundred tokens. For a hybrid model with mmproj (b7822) a mismatch before the cached end clears the whole slot, so the instructions are re-prefilled too. Fix: keep the tools listed for the whole run and rely on the in-tool decline that already exists (returns 'zoom_limit_reached', no image). Hide them only on the last allowed request (requests_started >= MAX-1) to protect the 8-request cap. Apply the same change to image_conflicts.
findings.evidence: sever/image_agent.py:256-265 `if (source.zoom_count >= MAX_ZOOM_IMAGES or deps.requests_started >= MAX_MODEL_REQUESTS - 1 ...): return None`; :267 and :301 `@agent.tool_plain(sequential=True, retries=1, prepare=prepare_zoom)`; :302 zoom_regions `max_length=8`; :278-289 existing decline `No additional image supplied: crop allowance exhausted`; sever/image_conflicts.py:461-466 same hiding with MAX_ZOOM_IMAGES=12 (:31). Schema size measured by importing the module: _NativeReadingResponse JSON schema 14,779 chars; INSTRUCTIONS 8,983 + ZOOM_INSTRUCTIONS 2,023 chars. llama.cpp b7822 tools/server/server-context.cpp:2220 `n_past = slot.prompt.tokens.get_common_prefix(input_tokens)`; :2298 checkpoints `disallow with mtmd contexts for now`; :2434-2441 a failed truncate clears the memory.
findings.expected_speed_effect: Unknown frequency until measured. If about 1 in 3 frame reads hits it, about 3-8% less model time at N=1 and more at N≥2, where prefill is the bottleneck.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Neutral. The model already receives the 'submit now' text after the limit.
findings.risk: The model may call zoom again after the crop limit: one extra short request (it gets text only). If that happens on the 8th request, ViewBudgetExceeded loses the frame, so keep hiding on the last request. No business rule touched.
findings.how_to_test: In the phase1 trace, mark field_agent/joint_review requests issued after a proof with panel zoom_08 (or zoom_12), or at page_request ≥7. Compare their cache_n/prompt_n with the continuity ratio from the measurement finding. After the change, check that those requests show cache_n ≈ previous total, and compare prompt_ms per run and labelled fields on video 5.

findings.title: Emit crop rectangles as integer [x1,y1,x2,y2] in 0-1000 instead of keyed floats in [0,1]
findings.claim: Each output token costs about 16.4 ms (61 tok/s), and decode is 69% of model time. Qwen tokenizers split digits one per token, so a keyed float rectangle such as {"left":0.125,...} costs about 35-40 tokens, and an integer array [125,40,880,95] about 15-17. An 8-region zoom_regions call would drop from about 300 to about 130 output tokens, roughly 2.8 s saved per such call. Qwen-VL models from Qwen3-VL on use relative 0-1000 integer boxes as their native grounding format, which may also place crops better and so reduce follow-up zooms. Integer arguments also avoid float re-serialisation (0.10 → 0.1) when the server re-renders the tool call into history, a possible break in cache continuity. Convert back to normalised floats inside the tool, so proofs and coordinate_system stay unchanged.
findings.evidence: sever/image_agent.py:36 `Coordinate = Annotated[float, Field(ge=0, le=1, ...)]`; :55-60 CropRegion left/top/right/bottom floats; :75-76 `normalized left, top, right, bottom in [0, 1]`; :180-189 zoom() scales floats to pixels; :302 up to 8 regions per call; sever/image_conflicts.py:147 `_FrameCropRegion` (same pattern, up to 12 regions, :500). analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md:23 decode 61 tok/s = 69%.
findings.expected_speed_effect: Depends on how much of the output goes to zoom arguments (measure by tool name first). If it is about 30-40% of output, about 10-15% less decode time, roughly -7 to -10% of model time.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Possibly + through better crop placement if the model's grounding convention is 0-1000. Unverified for Qwen3.8; neutral otherwise.
findings.risk: A changed tool contract changes the prompt hash, so a new batch is required. If the model was trained with another box convention, crop accuracy could drop, so A/B it. No business rule touched.
findings.how_to_test: From the measurement finding, sum predicted_n and argument length for zoom_regions/zoom_source calls. Then run an A/B on video 5 comparing output tokens per field_agent call, crops per read, how often the model re-zooms the same field, seconds per leaf, and labelled 15/22.

findings.title: Send the context, orientation and triage images at the server's token window, not 1024 px that the server then bilinear-upscales
findings.claim: With --image-min-tokens 1024, llama.cpp resizes every Qwen-VL image with BILINEAR into the [min_pixels, max_pixels] window. The client first LANCZOS-shrinks the 2160x3840 frame to 576x1024 (589,824 px). That is below 1024 tokens' worth of pixels (1,048,576 px at 32-px tokens, 802,816 at 28-px), so the server upscales it about 1.17-1.33x. The model sees an interpolated, blurred context at the same token cost it would pay for real pixels. Fix: downscale the source directly to the window, e.g. long edge about 1376 for 32-px tokens or about 1200 for 28-px, using the image_min_pixels value from the startup log. Likewise pre-resize crops that fall outside the window with LANCZOS on the client, so the stored panel is exactly what the model sees. Today the crop proof records `resize: none` / `native_source_detail: true` and the instructions promise 'without magnification', yet the server magnifies small crops and shrinks crops above 4096 tokens. This helps the triage heading (out-of-scope forms recorded with their literal heading), orientation, and crop targeting on the context image.
findings.evidence: sever/image_agent.py:140-146 `if context: uploaded.thumbnail((1024, 1024), Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)` then JPEG q95; :63-64 `reduced to a 1024-pixel long edge`; :77-78 `lossless native crops, without magnification or invented pixels`; :170-173 prep `"resize": "LANCZOS" if context else "none", "native_source_detail": not context`; sever/image_detail.py:86-90 four 1024-px orientation thumbnails; sever/image_triage.py:134 triage sends only that context JPEG; deploy/sever-model.service:12 `--image-min-tokens 1024 --image-max-tokens 4096`. llama.cpp b7822 tools/mtmd/clip.cpp:1160-1171 `Qwen-VL models require at minimum 1024 image tokens to function correctly on grounding tasks`; :2834-2843 `calc_size_preserved_ratio(..., params.patch_size * 2, image_min_pixels, image_max_pixels)` then `RESIZE_ALGO_BILINEAR`; :2357-2361 upscale branch when below min_pixels.
findings.expected_speed_effect: Neutral, with the same token count. Possibly slightly faster if better context reading reduces re-zooms.
findings.expected_precision_effect: + small to moderate on triage and type headings and on crop placement. Glyph-level effect on crops is small (LANCZOS instead of bilinear).
findings.risk: Changes the instruction text and prompt hash, so a new batch is required. JPEG payload grows by about 1.8x, which is negligible on loopback. Strengthens rather than bends the 'evidence must cite actually-sent images' rule, because the stored panel then equals what the model sees.
findings.how_to_test: Read image_min_pixels / image_max_pixels from the sever-model log. Confirm on one triage call that prompt_n drops by about 0 tokens (same budget). Run an A/B on video 5 and the other 3 labelled videos: out-of-scope rejection 5/5 with literal headings, orientation agreement between frames, labelled fields, crops per read.

findings.title: A/B the already-installed Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (MoE) against the dense 27B on the current pipeline: the user decides
findings.claim: The current pipeline is decode-bound (69%). An A3B MoE reads only about 3B active parameters per token, so on this GPU it should decode about 2.5-3x faster (assumption: 150-200 tok/s) and also prefill faster. Estimate: about 5.3 s → 2-2.5 s per call. The old trial (156.8 s vs 231.2 s, both 9/10 accepted fields) used the earlier OCR-guided pipeline and counted accepted fields, not measured accuracy. The model choice was the user's, so this is an experiment to put to them, not a default change.
findings.evidence: deploy/README.md:241-242 `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q6 | 9/10 | 156,83 с` vs `Qwen3.8-27B Q6 | 9/10 | 231,19 с`; :244 `Это счётчики принятых полей, не независимо измеренная точность`; :166 `По выбору пользователя используется плотная Qwen3.8-27B Q6`; :260 `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q6 сохранена для исторического сравнения`; analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md:22-24 decode = 69%.
findings.expected_speed_effect: Estimated -45 to -60% model time per sheet if calls per sheet stay the same. More reads, if accuracy drops, would offset this.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Unknown, possibly negative on glyph and role errors. Must be measured on all 44 labelled fields.
findings.risk: VRAM: about 29 GB at Q6 likely rules out --parallel >1, and Q5 would be needed for concurrency. Glyph-level OCR may degrade. Changes the batch fingerprint (README:458). No business rule bent, but it reverses an explicit user choice.
findings.how_to_test: With the user's consent, follow the README:627-662 idle swap and run phase1-speed on video 5, then on the other 3 labelled videos. Compare with tools/compare_runs.py against today's 27B phase1 run (15/22), including predicted_per_second and prompt_per_second from server_timings.

findings.title: Raise --ubatch-size to 1024-2048: prefill becomes the bottleneck once decode is batched
findings.claim: No -b/-ub flags are set, so llama.cpp defaults apply: n_batch 2048, n_ubatch 512. Measured prefill is 2,340 tok/s including vision encoding. On a dense 27B a larger physical batch usually lifts prompt throughput by about 10-25%. At N=1 prefill is 27% of model time, so the gain is about 3-5%. In the N=4 simulation, prefill is more than half of GPU-busy time, so the gain rises to about 6-12%.
findings.evidence: deploy/sever-model.service:12 (no -b/-ub); llama.cpp b7822 common/common.h:322-323 `n_batch = 2048` / `n_ubatch = 512`; analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md:22-23 `prefill 639,726 new input tokens in 273 s (2,340 tok/s)`.
findings.expected_speed_effect: -3 to -5% model time at N=1; -6 to -12% at N=3-4
findings.expected_precision_effect: None (tiny numeric differences only)
findings.risk: Larger CUDA compute buffer (see `compute buffer size` in the log) competes with the KV needed for --parallel N inside about 5.9 GiB of headroom. A larger prefill chunk slows other slots' decode steps more under concurrency. No business rule touched.
findings.how_to_test: While sever-model is stopped (idle procedure), run `llama-bench -m $MODEL_PATH -fa 1 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -p 4096 -n 0 -ub 512,1024,2048`. Then restart with the best -ub and compare prompt_per_second in server_timings and peak memory on an A/B run.

findings.title: Cap output tokens per call kind at about 2x the observed maximum instead of 8192 for agent and joint-review calls
findings.claim: Field-agent and joint-review runs allow 8192 output tokens. At 61 tok/s one runaway greedy answer costs about 134 s, about 1.8 phase1 leaves. The 222-token mean says nothing about the tail. Orientation (128) and triage (96) are already capped. Once the measurement finding gives max/p99 predicted_n per kind, set the cap for field_agent and joint_review (e.g. 2048-3072, above the observed max). Note that the code default (2200) differs from the deployed env (8192).
findings.evidence: deploy/local-provider.env.example:7 `HARNESS_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=8192`; sever/cli.py:27 and sever/api.py:157 default `"2200"`; sever/image_agent.py:328 `"max_tokens": effective.max_output_tokens`; sever/image_conflicts.py:528 same; sever/image_orientation.py:28 `ORIENTATION_OUTPUT_LIMIT = 128`; sever/image_triage.py:31 `TRIAGE_OUTPUT_LIMIT = 96`.
findings.expected_speed_effect: Only tail latency: 0 if no call exceeds about 2k tokens today; up to minutes per affected leaf otherwise
findings.expected_precision_effect: Neutral if the cap stays above the observed max. A cap that is too low truncates a legitimate long address block and loses the frame.
findings.risk: Truncation leads to a schema failure and a failed view. Long ENTIRE-address values (UPD consignee_address) set the floor. No business rule bent.
findings.how_to_test: From the phase1 trace: histogram of predicted_n for field_agent / joint_review, max and p99, and leaf time with and without the top-1% calls. Set the cap at about 2x the max and re-run video 5.

findings.title: If the model is hybrid, shrink the static prefix (instructions plus about 14.8k-char schema): it is re-prefilled on every run
findings.claim: In b7822 with an mmproj loaded, the host-RAM prompt cache and context checkpoints are both off. For a hybrid or recurrent model, any prompt that differs from the cached one before its end clears the slot. Each new frame read's first request shares the instruction and schema prefix with the previous run but differs at the image, so for such a model the about 7-8k-token prefix (8,983 + 2,023 chars of instructions + 14,779 chars of JSON schema) is processed in full on every run. Removing schema fields the model is told to omit and the per-variant duplication could save about 2-3k tokens per run. With roughly 40 runs per video, that is about 100k tokens, or about 40 s per video at N=1. If the measurement finding shows cross-run reuse works (an attention-only model, or v0.6.0 has mtmd caching), drop this finding.
findings.evidence: llama.cpp b7822 tools/server/server-context.cpp:1007-1008 `// TODO: mtmd does not support prompt cache` / `update_cache && (ret->mctx == nullptr)`; :2298 `disallow with mtmd contexts for now`; :2434-2441 a failed truncate clears the memory; sever/image_reader.py:163 `confidence ... description="Omit"`, :211 `type_confidence ... description="Omit"`, :167 `reason`; sizes measured by import: INSTRUCTIONS 8,983, ZOOM_INSTRUCTIONS 2,023, schema 14,779 chars; GPU idle memory 26,180 MiB suggests a small KV (hybrid-like).
findings.expected_speed_effect: Conditional: about -3 to -5% model time at N=1 and more at N≥2, only if first-in-run cache_n ≈ 0
findings.expected_precision_effect: Uncertain. Schema wording steers role and address boundaries, so labelled A/B is required.
findings.risk: Prompt and schema edits can shift role and address readings (known error classes). This overlaps the reading-schema area. No business rule bent if the literal and evidence fields remain.
findings.how_to_test: The measurement finding settles it: architecture from the log, plus first-in-run cache_n for field_agent and joint_review. If the condition holds, A/B a trimmed schema on video 5 for prompt_n per run and labelled fields.

findings.title: Read a leaf's first two frames concurrently to shorten the critical path
findings.claim: Confirmation always needs two distinct frames, both for fields and for out-of-scope, yet frames are read strictly one after another. After the leaf's single orientation call, launch the primary and the best extra frame together, including triage. This halves the minimum latency of clean leaves and gives the hardest leaf (page-0015, 301 s, which caps per-video wall time at N≥3) two-way parallelism. It improves latency, not throughput, so do it after leaf concurrency.
findings.evidence: sever/native_pipeline.py:862 `answer = await read(frame, ...)` inside the sequential per-frame loop; :1066-1090 concurrency exists only across leaves; sever/zoom_image_reader.py:41-61 orientation is decided once and reused for later views; analysis/ab-speed-20261017/comparison.md page-0015 `34 | 301.33`; simulation: at N=4 the leaf phase ends when page-0015 ends (about 310 s of about 610-650 s).
findings.expected_speed_effect: -10 to -20% per-video wall at N≥2 (critical path); about 0 for batch throughput
findings.expected_precision_effect: Neutral. The same frames are read, but the order of arrival can change which extra frames are later chosen.
findings.risk: The no-progress counter, triage short-circuit and fusion order assume sequential reads. One wasted read when the first frame alone would have stopped the leaf (rare, since two frames are needed). No business rule bent.
findings.how_to_test: Implement behind a flag. On video 5 with --parallel 4, compare per-leaf seconds (compare_runs leaf table), total requests, stop reasons and labelled fields against leaf-only concurrency.

findings.title: Do not spend time on speculative decoding, --cache-reuse, --cache-ram, lower --image-min-tokens or f16 KV
findings.claim: With an mmproj loaded, b7822 refuses to start with a draft model and disables --cache-reuse; it also disables cache reuse for memory that cannot shift (hybrid). The RAM prompt cache is skipped for mtmd. Lowering --image-min-tokens triggers llama.cpp's explicit Qwen-VL grounding warning, and the zoom agent depends on grounding to choose crops. f16 KV doubles the KV bytes read per decode step at 10-40k contexts and eats the VRAM needed for slots. Keep --flash-attn on, which q8_0 V cache needs. Verify each point against the deployed binary, which is newer than b7822: run `llama-server --help` and read the startup log.
findings.evidence: llama.cpp b7822 tools/server/server-context.cpp:717-720 `cache_reuse is not supported by multimodal, it will be disabled`; :722-725 `err: speculative decode is not supported by multimodal` / `return false`; :733-736 `cache_reuse is not supported by this context`; :1007-1008 mtmd skips the prompt cache; tools/mtmd/clip.cpp:1167-1171 `Qwen-VL models require at minimum 1024 image tokens ... grounding`; deploy/sever-model.service:12 already uses `--flash-attn on --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 --image-min-tokens 1024`; the deployed flag `--no-reasoning-preserve` does not exist in b7822 common/arg.cpp (grep finds only --reasoning-format/--reasoning-budget), so the versions differ.
findings.expected_speed_effect: None (avoids wasted experiments)
findings.expected_precision_effect: Avoids a likely loss from lowering image-min-tokens
findings.risk: v0.6.0 may have added mtmd support for one of these. If its log shows speculative or mtmd prompt caching accepted, revisit: JSON-heavy 222-token outputs would suit speculation.
findings.how_to_test: `/opt/sever-tsl/llama.cpp/build/bin/llama-server --help | grep -Ei 'spec|draft|cache-ram|kv-unified|checkpoint'`, and grep the sever-model journal for the warnings quoted above.

open_questions: Is Qwen3.8-27B a hybrid (linear-attention) model or full attention? Check the startup log's architecture and KV/recurrent lines. This decides whether cross-run prefix reuse is possible at all and how many KV cells --parallel N can afford.

Does the deployed llama.cpp v0.6.0 still disable the RAM prompt cache, context checkpoints, speculative decoding and --cache-reuse when an mmproj is loaded? Every llama.cpp claim here was checked in the local b7822 checkout (~/llama.cpp).
What exact image_min_pixels / image_max_pixels does the server log print (vision patch size 14 or 16)? This sets the right context-image size.
What are the peak tokens per request (cache_n + prompt_n + predicted_n) for joint_review and field_agent in the phase1 trace? This sizes --ctx-size for --kv-unified with N slots.
Is 'seconds per sheet' meant as single-video latency (bounded by the hardest leaf) or as batch throughput across the 11 videos? Concurrency helps the second much more.
Is run-to-run non-bit-reproducibility under batched decode acceptable for the customer's acceptance protocol?
Does the user want the MoE model (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B) re-evaluated, given that the dense 27B was their explicit choice?

read:reading.area: Per-frame reading step: sever/image_agent.py, image_reader.py, image_detail.py, zoom_image_reader.py, image_orientation.py, image_triage.py (with the image-token behaviour of deploy/sever-model.service)
read:reading.summary:
The frame-reading step is limited mostly by decoding, not by input size. On the 2026-10-17 server A/B (analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md:23), phase1-speed spent 69% of model time generating text at 61 tok/s, and prefill ran at 2,340 tok/s with 68% of input coming from the prefix cache. The field agent made 115 calls over about 25 views, roughly 4.6 requests and 21-23 s per view.

Token costs below come from running the Qwen3.5 tokenizer found on this Mac (vocabulary of 248,044) over the real prompts. I assume Qwen3.8 uses the same family tokenizer; one trace check would confirm it.
- The text prefix is about 6.7k tokens: instructions 2,639, submit_reading tool schema as actually sent 3,567, the two zoom tools 466. Text runs about 4 characters per token, so the chars/1.5 rule (agents.py:539) overestimates it about 2.5 times.
- Images go through llama.cpp's Qwen-VL resizing (32 px per token, kept between 1,024 and 4,096 tokens). The 576x1024 overview is enlarged to 768x1376, which costs 1,032 tokens but adds no detail. Each zoom crop costs at least about 1,024 tokens, and small crops are enlarged 1.5-2.4 times. The whole frame at the 4,096-token cap arrives at only 71% of native resolution.

Recommendations, ranked:
1. **Read each frame in one request.** Send two overlapping full-width native bands of the upright sheet up front (about 3.6-4.0k tokens each, sized so the server does not resize them). Allow at most one zoom round, only for lines with uncertain characters. Expected: 21-23 s per view down to about 10-16 s.
2. **Shorten the final answer**, since decoding dominates. Example UPD answer: 620 tokens, about 450 after trimming.
3. **Check whether each view's first request misses the prefix cache.** The model looks like a hybrid-attention type, for which llama.cpp only reuses a prefix from saved checkpoints. If it misses, that is up to about 74 s per video.
4. **Stop the per-frame schema from offering a "conflict" status.** One such answer permanently blocks two-frame confirmation of that field.
5. **Size the overview to what the server actually uses and crop it to the sheet.** Free extra resolution.

Smaller or negative results:
- Splitting form identification into its own call with a form-specific schema gains little or nothing on speed, and reusing one frame's type for the next frame bends the two-frame rule. Trimming the shared schema is better.
- Orientation is already one call per leaf, so at most about 20 s per video is left to save. The sheet outline cannot tell orientation.
- Grammar-constrained decoding runs near the GPU's memory-bandwidth limit, so it is not a material slowdown.
- Perspective correction is not worth it: the sheet touches the frame edge in nearly every frame.

None of these were measured, and labelled precision has to be checked by A/B on video 5 (22 labels, baseline 15/22) before anything ships.

findings.title: Replace the 1024-px-overview + up-to-8-crop zoom loop with one request carrying two native bands of the sheet (at most one zoom round)
findings.claim: Change read_frame_agent's first message from one 1024-px JPEG to the upright sheet split into 2 full-width horizontal bands. Use the sheet bounding box (frame['quality']['paper_geometry']['quadrilateral_normalized'] + 3% margin) when it exists, else the whole upright frame. Bands overlap by at least 25% of band height so no address block is cut, and are pre-sized with Lanczos to 32-px multiples within 4,194,304 px so llama.cpp does not resize them again. Examples: portrait 2160x2240 bands become 1984x2080 = 4,030 tokens at 0.92 of native; a sheet-box band of 1840x2000 becomes 1856x1984 = 3,596 tokens at native; a landscape 3840x1300 band becomes 3488x1184 = 4,033 tokens at 0.91. Optionally keep a 768x1376 overview (1,032 tokens). Set MAX_MODEL_REQUESTS=2 so prepare_zoom offers zoom_regions only on request 1 and only submit_reading on request 2, and set tool_choice to 'required'. Instruct: submit immediately unless a specific character is uncertain, then zoom those lines once. Register bands through _Source.panel(context=False) with ids b1/b2 and a separate counter, so they do not use up the crop allowance. Each request is about 6.7k text + 7.2-9.1k image tokens = 14-16k, well under ctx 65,536. Today the model starts from about 27% of native linear resolution (illegible small text), so it must zoom 3-7 times. Every zoom adds a tool-call decode (about 50-160 tokens) and a round trip that re-sends every earlier image. Bands give it about 92-100% of native resolution from the start. Do NOT derive frame-2 crops from frame-1 evidence boxes: identical answer-driven crops would correlate errors (e.g. the same truncated address on both frames) and would condition one frame's reading on a stored answer.
findings.evidence: sever/image_agent.py:33-35 "MAX_MODEL_REQUESTS = 8 / MAX_ZOOM_IMAGES = 8"; image_agent.py:140-146 "uploaded.thumbnail((1024, 1024)...)" for the context, PNG for crops; image_agent.py:176-177 zoom_count increments for every non-context panel; image_agent.py:256-265 prepare_zoom returns None when "deps.requests_started >= MAX_MODEL_REQUESTS - 1"; image_agent.py:325-329 "tool_choice": "auto"; image_agent.py:76-77 tells the model crops come "without magnification", but llama.cpp bicubic-enlarges any crop under 1,048,576 px (a 1944x231 line crop becomes 2976x384 = 1,116 tokens, 1.53x). One-call reading with a custom panel preparer already exists: image_reader.py:435-447 (read_frame(..., panel_preparer=...), request_limit=1 at :510), and image_detail.py:133-141 prepare_detail_panels (context + overlapping 2x2 native quarters; quarters split lines left/right, bands do not). Measured: analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md:19 "field agent 115" calls, :23 "generation ... (61 tok/s) = 69% of model time", prefill 2,340 tok/s; comparison.json per leaf: page-0002 about 13 s per view (3 calls), page-0001 about 24 s per view (5.5 calls). Resize rule: llama.cpp tools/mtmd/mtmd-image.cpp smart-resize "else if (opts.min_pixels > 0 && h_bar * w_bar < opts.min_pixels)" enlarges, aligned to patch_size*n_merge; the local Qwen3.5 config gives patch_size 16, spatial_merge_size 2 (32 px per token); deploy/sever-model.service:12 "--image-min-tokens 1024 --image-max-tokens 4096".
findings.expected_speed_effect: Field-agent time per view drops from about 21-23 s (4.6 calls) to about 10-16 s: 3.1-3.9 s to prefill the bands at 2,340 tok/s, plus 0-2.9 s if the text prefix misses the cache, plus 6.6-10.2 s to decode a 400-620-token answer at 61 tok/s. That is about 175-325 s saved on video 5 (15-29% of the 1,134 s wall; about 64-60 s per sheet instead of 75.6). Each view also becomes one independent request, so the two mandatory views of a leaf could later be decoded together under --parallel 2.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Uncertain, so it must be A/B'd. Likely better on role confusion and address-block boundaries, because each field's caption and whole block are always visible together. Possibly worse on single-glyph errors (РИТЕЙЛ/РИТЕИЛ, соор./корп.): band x-height is about 12-16 px versus 1.5-2.4x server enlargement for small crops. The one allowed zoom round is the mitigation. More uniform framing across frames should raise two-view agreement, which is what ends hard leaves and avoids joint reviews.
findings.risk: Business rules: evidence cites actually-sent images (bands are sent and recorded with transforms), values stay literal, and no answers are reused, so it complies. The address rule depends on band overlap being at least the tallest block. If both frames cut a block at the same place, they could falsely agree, so keep overlap at 25% or more; handheld motion also shifts boundaries between frames. Context: about 16k tokens per request fits ctx 65,536, but would exceed a 16,384-token slot if leaf concurrency used --parallel 4 without unified KV. The sheet box comes from a 384-px thumbnail thresholded at gray>140 and can clip dark or occluded edges, so fall back to the whole frame when no quadrilateral exists.
findings.how_to_test: Branch from phase1-speed. Run deploy/ab_speed_test.sh with REF_A=phase1-speed, REF_B=<branch>, VIDEO=/srv/sever/input/20260818-5_132107.mp4, then tools/compare_runs.py with --truth analysis/ground-truth-expanded-provisional.json. Pass criteria: field_agent calls per view ≤1.3 (now 4.6), field-agent model seconds per view, labelled fields ≥15/22, and two-view agreement rate (share of fields where the first two views give the same _field_comparison key, from results.json image_recognition.views). Also test variants: bands without the overview; one sheet-box image at 4,096 tokens (about 0.81 of native); 3 native bands (about 10k tokens). Before that, a cheap per-image probe: run tools/read_zoom_images.py on the 6 images in /srv/sever/validation/accuracy-speed-v8-20261011/input-images and compare per-image proposals with analysis/accuracy-speed-v8-pixel-review.json.

findings.title: Shorten the final submit_reading answer: decoding is 69% of model time
findings.claim: Generation runs at 61 tok/s, so every output token costs about 16 ms. A realistic UPD final answer counted with the Qwen tokenizer is 620 tokens. Values are only 152 of those, field captions 62 and the heading 67; the remaining ~340 are keys, punctuation, default values and panel ids. Changes, none of which alter any value: (1) remove confidence and type_confidence from the model-facing schema; their only description is "Omit". (2) Make explicit_blank and reason absent unless used, and tell the model to omit them; 13 tokens per field when emitted, 67 tokens on the UPD example. (3) Use short panel ids: 'zoom_02_r90' is 9 tokens and 'z2' is 4. The _r{rotation} suffix is the same for every panel of a frame, and answers cite 2-4 panels per field. (4) Ask for observed_form only for unknown; for supported forms it repeats heading_text (17 tokens). (5) Limit heading_text to the own title line and the form code or ОКУД, without the full постановление caption (29 tokens). (6) Set tool_choice='required' so no free-text preamble is ever generated. Expected about 620 → 430-480 tokens per UPD answer. The ImageField models are shared with the joint review, so it shrinks too.
findings.evidence: analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md:23 "generation 41,696 tokens in 688 s (61 tok/s) = 69% of model time"; :18 "Output tokens per request | 236 | 222"; sever/image_reader.py:163 "confidence: ... description=\"Omit\""; image_reader.py:166-167 explicit_blank/reason defaults; image_reader.py:211 type_confidence "Omit"; image_reader.py:212-214 observed_form/visible_text/heading_text all required for every form; image_reader.py:117-120 asks for the "approval/regulatory caption"; image_agent.py:149 identifier f"zoom_{n:02d}_r{self.rotation}"; image_agent.py:329 "tool_choice": "auto"; image_conflicts.py:24-25 imports UPDFields/TORGFields/TTNFields/TRNFields; agents.py:580-582 the trace stores response_parts for every response, so emitted keys and text are visible.
findings.expected_speed_effect: About 2-3 s less decode per final answer (140-190 tokens at 61 tok/s). Across about 25 field-agent finals plus the joint reviews on video 5, about 60-100 s (5-9% of wall). More if the trace shows text preambles.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Neutral if captions (evidence_text) and the ОКУД code are kept. Captions act as role grounding and should not be removed.
findings.risk: Shortening the heading must not drop the ТОРГ-12 or ОКУД identifier that separates torg12 from a generic Товарная накладная (image_reader.py:117-120). Renaming panel ids must keep proof['panels'] keys and the _validate_reading lookups (image_reader.py:361-370) consistent. Changes the response schema hash and version strings (image_reader.py:32-33), so run a new A/B rather than comparing against old runs.
findings.how_to_test: No new calls needed first. In /srv/sever/validation/ab-speed-20261017-191924/phase1-speed/trace.jsonl, attribute model_response_received rows to call kinds as tools/compare_runs.py does (CALL_KINDS). Sum server_timings.predicted_n per kind, and per response part (ToolCallPart tool_name zoom_regions / zoom_source / submit_reading). Count TextPart occurrences and how often explicit_blank:false, reason:null and confidence appear in submit_reading args. Then A/B the change on video 5: predicted_n per submit_reading, wall time, and labelled 15/22 unchanged.

findings.title: Check whether each view's first request misses the prefix cache (hybrid model + one slot) and shrink what a miss costs
findings.claim: The per-view text prefix (instructions + tools) is about 6.7k tokens. With --parallel 1, the slot is overwritten between views by orientation, triage and joint-review prompts that use other system prompts. The model also looks hybrid-attention: 26.2-26.7 GB in use at ctx 65,536 with about 22-23 GB of Q6 weights leaves room for a KV cache on only a fraction of layers. For such models llama.cpp reuses a prefix only from a saved context checkpoint, so each view's first request probably re-prefills the whole 6.7k text. Within one view, reuse clearly works: 68% of input comes from the cache. If all 25 views miss, that is 25 × 6.7k ≈ 168k of the 640k prefilled tokens (26%), about 72 s per video. Fixes inside this area: shrink the prefix (drop the two 'Omit' fields; deduplicate rules repeated between INSTRUCTIONS and schema descriptions, e.g. the full-address-block rule appears 3 times in INSTRUCTIONS plus 2 field descriptions, and «он же» 2 times plus 1). Measured: removing confidence fields alone takes the schema from 3,435 to 3,161 tokens; descriptions total 1,163 tokens. Target about 5k. Server side: pin field-agent requests to their own slot (--parallel 2 plus the llama.cpp id_slot request field via extra_body), or tune the checkpoint and cache-ram settings so a checkpoint sits at the end of the system prompt.
findings.evidence: sever/zoom_image_reader.py:49-50 (orientation call), :72-73 (triage call), :86-87 (field agent): three different system prompts in a row per view; deploy/sever-model.service:12 "--parallel 1 ... --ctx-size 65536"; analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md:20 "GPU memory 26,180–26,683 MiB", :23 "68% of input tokens came from the prefix cache"; image_reader.py:54-56, 59-68, 132-135 and 175, 177 (address rule five times), 44-50, 137-140, 174 («он же»). Token counts from the local Qwen3.5 tokenizer: INSTRUCTIONS+ZOOM_INSTRUCTIONS 2,639; wire tool schemas 4,033 (submit_reading 3,567). External: https://particula.tech/blog/prompt-reprocessing-swa-hybrid-models-kv-cache (llama.cpp reuses a prefix only if it can roll back; recurrent/SWA layers need checkpoints; "forcing full prompt re-processing due to lack of cache data"; --checkpoint-min-step default 8192).
findings.expected_speed_effect: If misses are confirmed: about 70 s per video (about 6% of wall) recoverable with slot pinning or checkpoints, or about 25 s from cutting the prefix 6.7k → 5k. If there are no misses, the gain from trimming is negligible.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Neutral for slot pinning. Deduplicating rules carries a small risk: the repetitions were added to fix observed errors (README.md:166-176 in deploy describe the «он же» rule history), so drop only exact duplicates and A/B.
findings.risk: --parallel 2 halves the context per slot (32,768) unless KV is unified, and multi-frame joint reviews may not fit. Checkpoint flag names differ by llama.cpp build (the server runs tag v0.6.0), so check llama-server --help first. Removing duplicate rule text may reverse fixes that only work because of the repetition.
findings.how_to_test: In the phase1-speed trace, take each image_agent run's first model_response_received (the one following model_request_started with page_request==1 after an image_agent_observation row). Read server_timings.cache_n and prompt_n. A cache_n far below about 6,700 confirms the miss. Compare with page_request ≥2 rows. Optionally run llama-server once with -lv 4 and look for 'forcing full prompt re-processing'.

findings.title: Remove 'conflict' from the per-frame field status: one such answer permanently blocks two-frame confirmation
findings.claim: The per-frame schema lets the model return status 'conflict' for a field it sees in one image. _validate_reading keeps such a field unchanged when raw_value is null. Fusion then treats any per-frame 'conflict' with evidence as an explicit disagreement, so that field can never become recognized by two agreeing frames on this leaf. The leaf keeps reading views and triggers joint reviews (the stop rule needs recognized/not_present). A single frame cannot hold a cross-frame conflict. Use Literal['recognized','not_present','unreadable'] for the per-frame ImageField; fusion and joint review still own 'conflict'. Bonus: the schema loses one enum value and the model loses a confusing option.
findings.evidence: sever/image_reader.py:162 "status: FieldStatus"; sever/schema.py:7 "FieldStatus = Literal[\"recognized\", \"not_present\", \"unreadable\", \"conflict\"]"; image_reader.py:407-411 (an unresolved field with raw_value None keeps proposal.status); sever/image_fusion.py:181-185 "elif field.status == \"conflict\" and _frames(field.evidence): explicit_conflict = True ... conflict = explicit_conflict or ..."; sever/native_pipeline.py:160-165 stop requires recognized/not_present; INSTRUCTIONS (image_reader.py:36-156) never define a per-frame use of conflict.
findings.expected_speed_effect: Zero if the model never emits it. Where it does, each affected leaf avoids extra views and a joint review (about 5-7 calls, roughly 30-60 s).
findings.expected_precision_effect: Neutral to positive: fields that two frames would agree on stop being locked in conflict.
findings.risk: Joint review imports the same field models (image_conflicts.py:24-25, 33). Give the per-frame reader its own ImageField variant, or check that joint review does not rely on emitting 'conflict'. Changes the schema version.
findings.how_to_test: Count fields with status 'conflict' in single-view readings (image_recognition.views[*] → recognition.reading fields) in the phase1-speed and main results.json for video 5, and in the 11-video V7 batch. If any exist, A/B on video 5 and report joint_review calls and confirmed fields for the leaves concerned.

findings.title: Size every overview image to what llama.cpp actually feeds the model, and crop it to the sheet
findings.claim: The 1024-px-long-edge overview (576x1024, 589,824 px) is below the server's 1,024-token floor (1,048,576 px). llama.cpp bicubic-enlarges it to 768x1376 and charges 1,032 tokens without adding information. Send a Lanczos 768x1376 (or 1376x768) image straight from the native frame instead: same tokens, 1.33x more real linear detail. Additionally crop to the sheet bounding box when video.py produced a quadrilateral. Local data has a quadrilateral in 13/22 (video 5 sample) and 68/198 (video 4) frames, with a median bounding-box share of 0.79 and 0.73, which gives a further 1.12-1.17x linear detail. This applies to the field-agent overview, to orientation's four rotations and to triage, whose heading literal decides the out-of-scope short-circuit. Note: the outline is computed in video.py on 384-px thumbnails, not in quality.py.
findings.evidence: sever/image_agent.py:140-141 "uploaded.thumbnail((1024, 1024), Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)"; sever/image_detail.py:87-88 same for orientation; sever/image_triage.py:89 "source.panel((0, 0, *source.upright_size), context=True)"; deploy/sever-model.service:12 "--image-min-tokens 1024"; smart-resize gives 576x1024 → 768x1376 = 24x43 = 1,032 tokens; sever/video.py:45-70 (largest bright contour, approxPolyDP, "quadrilateral_normalized"), video.py:442 "scale=384:-2", frame_pool.py:25-28 (384-px features); sever/quality.py:143 "no OCR/model or paper-outline rule runs"; local stats from analysis/video5-local-ocr-prewarm.json and output/accuracy-review/video4-segmentation-observed.json.
findings.expected_speed_effect: No extra tokens. Small indirect gains: fewer re-zooms in the current agent, more triage short-circuits on out-of-scope leaves. Probably under 3% of wall.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Small gain: headings and captions sharper in the overview, which helps form choice, crop choice and literal out-of-scope headings.
findings.risk: A box from a gray>140 threshold mask can clip shadowed or hand-covered edges, so add a margin and fall back to the full frame. Panel bbox and transform must describe the crop (_source_transform already handles arbitrary boxes, image_reader.py:269-283). If the server's llama.cpp v0.6.0 does not enlarge to min_pixels, the gain is real detail at +456 tokens instead of free.
findings.how_to_test: First confirm the token math from the existing phase1 trace: for triage responses, prompt_n + cache_n should be about 1.37k (about 340 text + 1,032 image) if the image is enlarged, and about 0.9k if not. Then A/B on video 5: labelled 15/22, triage short-circuit count (out_of_scope_form_confirmed with 3 calls per leaf), and field-agent calls per view.

findings.title: Do not split form identification into a separate call with a form-specific schema; trim the shared union instead
findings.claim: The union schema as sent is 3,567 tokens. UPD|Unknown alone would be about 1.4k (974 + 387), and UPD-only instructions about half of 2,639, so a split saves about 3k prefix tokens per request. But that prefix is either cached (then no gain) or re-prefilled once per view (then about 1.3 s per view). Producing the type guess costs a triage-sized call of about 1.2 s per frame. Net speed is roughly zero. If instead the first frame's type is reused to narrow the second frame's schema, frame 2 can no longer disagree on type. That bends the two-distinct-frames rule (the type is still 'confirmed' but no longer independently) and silences the disagreeing_document_readings stop. Ordering is already right: in the discriminated union the model writes observed_form and heading_text before document_type and then fields, so identification already precedes extraction within one generation. Only reconsider if trace errors turn out to be cross-form rule confusion, and then derive each frame's narrowed schema from that frame's own triage, always keeping UnknownReading.
findings.evidence: Measured with the Qwen tokenizer: union wire schema 3,567 tokens; UPDReading 974 and UnknownReading 387 (titles and confidence stripped). sever/image_reader.py:209-216 (_Reading fields, then document_type and fields in subclasses at :219-243), :246-248 discriminated union; sever/native_pipeline.py:168-170 "if len(supported) > 1: return \"disagreeing_document_readings\""; triage cost from comparison.json (out-of-scope leaf: 1 orientation + 2 triage = 4.5-4.7 s); sever/zoom_image_reader.py:70 triage runs only until "full_read_required"; README.md:38 type and fields need two different source frames.
findings.expected_speed_effect: About zero to −2% wall (gain only when the prefix misses the cache, offset by the extra call).
findings.expected_precision_effect: Small possible gain from fewer cross-form rules in context. A real precision risk if frame 2 inherits frame 1's type (correlated type errors).
findings.risk: Weakens the independence behind two-frame type confirmation unless the narrowing is per frame. Every narrowed schema must keep UnknownReading so out-of-scope forms are still recorded with their heading.
findings.how_to_test: From the phase1 trace and results.json, classify field errors on the 22 labels (role confusion, boundary, glyph, wrong form). Only if wrong-form or cross-form rule errors dominate, prototype a per-frame narrowed schema behind a flag and A/B on video 5, reporting disagreeing_document_readings occurrences and labelled precision.

findings.title: Orientation: little left to save; the sheet outline cannot decide it, but a 1-image composite or merging with triage can trim it
findings.claim: Orientation is now one call per leaf: 15 calls on video 5, each sending four 1,032-token images plus about 300 text tokens (about 4.4k), about 2.1-2.3 s per call. The sheet outline gives only the sheet's aspect, and the sheet touches the frame edge in 22/22 and 197/198 sampled frames, so it cannot tell 0 from 180 degrees or whether text runs along the long axis (UPD and ТОРГ-12 are landscape forms, ТТН and ТрН portrait). Cheap options: (a) tile the four rotations, each about 512 px long edge, into one image of about 1088x1088 (1,156 tokens instead of 4,128); (b) on a leaf's first view, return rotation and triage scope plus heading in the same call, saving one call per leaf; (c) a horizontal-versus-vertical text-line projection profile on the native grayscale image to fix the axis, leaving the model only 0/180 or 90/270.
findings.evidence: sever/image_orientation.py:75-81 four context rotations, :28 "ORIENTATION_OUTPUT_LIMIT = 128", :29-38 instructions (185 tokens); sever/image_detail.py:75-88 each rotation is a 1024-px thumbnail, so 1,032 tokens after smart-resize; sever/zoom_image_reader.py:41-61 leaf reuse, :99-104 orientation dropped and redone after an insufficient_evidence result; analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md:19 "orientation 15, triage 19"; analysis/accuracy-speed-v8-latency-followup.json "orientation_seconds": 27.65 for 12 requests; video.py:57-61 clipped_edges marks full_page False.
findings.expected_speed_effect: Option (a): about 1.3 s per leaf, about 20 s per video (about 1.7%). Option (b): about 1 s per leaf. Combined, under 3% of wall.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Neutral if orientation accuracy holds. Lower-resolution rotations could mis-orient, but the existing drop-and-retry bounds the damage.
findings.risk: Orientation evidence is not field evidence, so no business rule is touched. A combined orientation+triage answer must still yield a literal heading for out-of-scope records.
findings.how_to_test: On the phase1 video-5 run, read the 15 orientation decisions as a reference. Run the composite variant over the same saved frames as a fresh diagnostic (new calls, no reuse) and count disagreements; then A/B wall time on video 5. Also check how many leaves on the 11 videos needed a fresh orientation after leaf_orientation_dropped.

findings.title: Grammar-constrained tool/JSON decoding is not a material slowdown; do not spend effort there unless the trace shows it
findings.claim: Measured generation is 61 tok/s. A dense 27B Q6 model reads about 22-23 GB of weights per token, and the RTX 5090 moves about 1.79 TB/s, so the ceiling is about 78-81 tok/s. 61 tok/s is about 75-80% of that, a normal llama.cpp efficiency, which leaves at most about 10% for grammar overhead. Tool calls use a grammar that switches on at the tool call (tool_choice auto); NativeOutput calls use response_format json_schema. Optional micro-cut: maxLength and maxItems add 203 schema tokens (3,161 → 2,958) and many repetition rules to the grammar. Keep them, because they cap runaway strings that would otherwise fail validation after up to 8,192 tokens. The real decode lever is fewer output tokens (finding 2) or faster decoding (batched slots, or the MoE model that was 156.8 s vs 231.2 s), which is outside this area.
findings.evidence: analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md:23 "generation 41,696 tokens in 688 s (61 tok/s)"; README.md:6 model "Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q6_K_M"; sever/image_agent.py:252 ToolOutput(..., strict=False) and :329 tool_choice auto; sever/image_orientation.py:135 and image_triage.py:130 NativeOutput(..., strict=False); sever/image_reader.py:161-167, 212-215 maxLength 1200/600/240/500/1000/1000; deploy/sever-model.service:12 "--jinja".
findings.expected_speed_effect: Under 10% of decode at most; probably a few percent. Dropping maxLength: negligible.
findings.expected_precision_effect: None.
findings.risk: Removing maxLength could let a looping generation run to 8,192 tokens (about 2 minutes) before validation fails.
findings.how_to_test: Extend tools/compare_runs.py to group server_timings by call kind and compute predicted_n/predicted_ms. Compare orientation/triage (json_schema), zoom tool calls and submit_reading on the existing phase1 trace. For a clean number, send one identical image+prompt to llama-server three times as fresh diagnostic calls (plain text, response_format json_schema, tools) and compare timings.predicted_per_second.

findings.title: Skip perspective warp/deskew; at most crop to the sheet box
findings.claim: A perspective warp would need four reliable corners. The outline comes from a 384-px thumbnail and touches the image edge in nearly every frame (22/22 and 197/198), and four-corner quadrilaterals exist in only 34-59% of frames. Opposite-edge skew is modest (median perspective_indicator 0.10-0.13, p90 0.16-0.19), which Qwen-VL tolerates. A warp also resamples every glyph, and provenance would need a full projective inverse: _inverse_affine assumes an affine last row. Recommend the bounding-box crop from the overview finding and no geometric warp.
findings.evidence: sever/video.py:52-70 (contour area > .18, approxPolyDP, clipped_edges, perspective_indicator = 1 - min(ratios)); local stats from analysis/video5-local-ocr-prewarm.json (n=22: quad 13, clipped 22, perspective median 0.13) and output/accuracy-review/video4-segmentation-observed.json (n=198: quad 68, clipped 197, median 0.099, p90 0.188); sever/image_reader.py:262-266 _inverse_affine uses only the 2x3 part; image_agent.py:76-77 promises the model "no ... invented pixels".
findings.expected_speed_effect: None.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Avoids a likely loss: interpolated glyphs and mis-warped clipped sheets.
findings.risk: None for the recommendation itself.
findings.how_to_test: Compute quadrilateral, clipped-edge and perspective statistics from the analysis.json manifests of all 11 server videos. Warp only becomes worth trying if most frames have unclipped 4-corner outlines with perspective_indicator > 0.2.

open_questions: Confirm Qwen3.8 vision geometry (patch 16, merge 2, hence 32 px per token) and the hybrid-attention architecture from the GGUF/mmproj metadata or the llama-server start-up log. The token math here uses the local Qwen3.5 config and tokenizer.

Does the server's llama.cpp build (tag v0.6.0) enlarge images up to --image-min-tokens and resample with antialiasing like current master (tools/mtmd/mtmd-image.cpp)? The triage prompt_n check in the overview finding answers this.

Which checkpoint and cache-ram flags exist in that build, and is a checkpoint created at the system-prompt/user boundary? This decides whether the prefix-cache fix needs server flags or only a shorter prompt.
Joint review (image_conflicts.py: 39 calls, likely about a third of model time) has the same zoom-loop pattern; would per-frame bands for up to 4 frames (about 32k image tokens) fit and help?

Since each view would be a single request, should native_pipeline issue the two mandatory views of a leaf at once under --parallel 2? Decoding is bandwidth-bound, so batching 2 streams should give about 1.6-1.9x throughput; per-slot context would halve.

Precision evidence is thin: 22 labels on video 5 (95% CI about 50-87%), and the consignor_address label follows the pre-11.10 field boundary. Should band/zoom variants be judged on single-image proposals of all 44 labelled fields too, not only fused results?
Output-token split by call kind and tool name, and how often per-frame 'conflict' status or free-text preambles occur, are unknown until the existing phase1 trace on /srv/sever is queried.
Model choice (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B decodes far faster per token) is the largest remaining decode lever but is outside this area and changes the comparison baseline.

research:vlm-general.topic: Open-weight VLMs for literal Russian (Cyrillic) document OCR and field extraction that fit one RTX 5090 (32 GB), as of October 2026
research:vlm-general.summary:
What the two model names are: "Qwen3.8-27B" is Alibaba's dense 27B multimodal model, released 2026-08-14 under Apache-2.0. It has 64 layers in a hybrid layout: 48 Gated DeltaNet (linear attention) layers and 16 full-attention layers, plus a 27-layer vision encoder. "Qwen3.6-35B-A3B" is the April 2026 mixture-of-experts sibling: 35B parameters in total, about 3B used per token, 40 layers (30 linear, 10 full attention), Apache-2.0. The Qwen3.8 open release so far is only 27B (plus a 2.4T-A95B model). Smaller siblings are Qwen3.6-27B (2026-04-22) and Qwen3.5-27B, 35B-A3B, 9B, 4B, 2B and 0.8B (Feb–Mar 2026), all vision-language and 201 languages. They replace Qwen3-VL (2B/4B/8B/32B/30B-A3B, Oct 2025).

Best Russian-specific evidence: MWS Vision Bench (MTS AI). It has 800 images of real Russian office documents, with OCR and JSON key-information-extraction (KIE) tasks, and was updated 2026-07-23. Private test scores (overall / OCR / KIE):
- Qwen3.6-27B: 0.692 / 0.861 / 0.893
- Qwen3.6-35B-A3B: 0.691 / 0.847 / 0.840
- Qwen3.8-27B: 0.687 / 0.797 / 0.807
- Qwen3.5-35B-A3B: 0.664 / 0.808 / 0.847
- Qwen3.5-27B: 0.648
- Qwen3.5-9B: 0.624
- Gemma 4 31B: 0.613 / 0.734 / 0.793
- Qwen3-VL-8B: 0.578
- Mistral Small 3.2 24B: 0.577
- Qwen3-VL-32B: 0.576

The OCRBench v2 private leaderboard (2026.09, English average) agrees: Qwen3.6-27B 68.3, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 65.5, Qwen3.8-27B 63.5, GLM-4.6V-Flash 59.0. So the current production model, Qwen3.8-27B, is better on agentic benchmarks but looks worse than Qwen3.6 at literal Russian OCR and extraction. Its one clear advantage is grounding (MWS 0.223 vs 0.062 for Qwen3.6-27B), which may matter for the zoom_regions tool.

Other families checked and ruled out:
- InternVL3.5: no 3.6 or 4 exists. Russian appears only in multilingual VQA scores, and the older InternVL2-76B scored 13.18 on CC-OCR Russian.
- GLM-4.6V-Flash 9B: card lists only Chinese and English.
