- MiniCPM-V 4.5 (8B) and the 1B 4.6: rank low on OCRBench v2.
- Kimi-VL-A3B: 2025 model, no newer small release found.
- Molmo 2: English only, no OCR scores.
- Mistral Small 3.2: about 0.58 on MWS.
- Too big for 32 GB: Mistral Small 4 (119B-A6.5B), Llama 4 Scout (109B, and Russian is not listed), GLM-4.6V 106B, Qwen3.8-2.4T.
- Gemma 3 is superseded by Gemma 4 (OmniDocBench edit distance 0.365 vs 0.131).
- No open-weight Russian VLM was found: GigaChat open releases are text-only.

Recommended benchmark set:
1. Qwen3.6-27B: same architecture as the current model, drop-in on the existing llama.cpp setup.
2. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B: about 3B active parameters, so much faster prompt processing. The project's own trial measured 156.8 s vs 231.2 s on one clip.
3. Qwen3.8-27B: current baseline, kept as the control.
4. Gemma 4 31B: the only competitive non-Qwen family, with official ggml-org GGUFs.
5. Optional: Qwen3.5-9B or 4B as a fast helper for orientation and triage.

Serving caveat: llama.cpp prefix-cache restore for hybrid DeltaNet models has an open complaint. Issue #22384 was closed the same day as "fix incorrect", and a June–Aug 2026 forum thread reports full re-processing of the prompt. A community model card reports 93–99% prefix-cache hits for Qwen3.8-27B in vLLM 0.30/0.31 (--enable-prefix-caching plus --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16), which also opens the way to --parallel leaf concurrency.

Limits: none of these benchmarks tests phone photos of УПД/ТОРГ-12/ТТН/ТрН forms. MWS does not say whether thinking was on, which settings were used, or at what precision models ran. All numbers are vendor or leaderboard claims; only the project's own 44 labelled fields can decide.

findings.title: Benchmark Qwen3.6-27B as a drop-in replacement for Qwen3.8-27B (same architecture, better Russian OCR and extraction)
findings.claim: Swap only the GGUF and mmproj on the existing llama-server, then re-run the labelled videos. Qwen3.6-27B has the same structure as Qwen3.8-27B (64 layers, 16 full-attention layers, mmproj about 0.93 GB), so speed and VRAM should be nearly the same. On the only Russian-document benchmark found, it beats Qwen3.8-27B on literal OCR (0.861 vs 0.797) and on JSON extraction (0.893 vs 0.807). OCRBench v2 private English shows the same order (68.3 vs 63.5). Qwen3.8's gains are in agentic and GUI tasks (OSWorld 84.3 vs 63.9), which this pipeline does not need. The glyph errors (РИТЕЙЛ->РИТЕИЛ, соор.->корп.) and address-block errors are exactly the OCR and extraction axes where Qwen3.6 leads.
findings.evidence: https://github.com/mts-ai/MWS-Vision-Bench, test set: "Qwen3.6-27B | 0.692 | 0.861 | 0.753 | 0.062 | 0.893" vs "Qwen3.8-27B | 0.687 | 0.797 | 0.738 | 0.223 | 0.807" (columns: Overall, OCR, Structured, Grounding, KIE). https://99franklin.github.io/ocrbench_v2/ (2026.09): Qwen3.6-27B EN 68.3 (rank 5) vs Qwen3.8-27B EN 63.5 (rank 11). https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B: OSWorld-Verified 84.3 vs 63.9 for Qwen3.6-27B; OmniDocBench 1.5 91.1 vs 89.4. Architecture: Qwen3.8-27B config.json: 64 layers, full_attention_interval 4, 4 KV heads, head_dim 256. Qwen3.6-27B card: 64 layers, hybrid Gated DeltaNet / Gated Attention. GGUF: https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.6-27B-GGUF has Q6_K 22.5 GB and mmproj-F16 928 MB.
findings.expected_speed_effect: About neutral, since architecture and quantized size are the same (Q6_K 22.5 GB vs UD-Q6_K 22 GB). Fewer cross-frame conflicts would shorten the joint-review and extra-frame loops on hard leaves, but that is unproven.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Likely gain on literal Cyrillic glyphs and JSON field extraction (benchmark gaps of +0.06 on OCR and +0.09 on KIE). Possible loss on box placement (grounding 0.062 vs 0.223), which could hurt zoom_regions crop selection.
findings.risk: MWS does not say whether thinking was on or which precision was used. The production pipeline runs with thinking disabled at temperature 0 and Q6, so benchmark gaps may not carry over. The grounding gap could make crop requests miss the field, adding calls. The chat template or tool-call format may differ slightly from Qwen3.8 (Qwen3.6 uses the qwen3_coder XML tool format), so verify that submit_reading parses. Business rules are unaffected. Labels are provisional (44 fields).
findings.how_to_test: Run the existing server A/B script on the 4 labelled videos plus video 20260818-5_132107.mp4, with phase1-speed code fixed and only the model path changed. Compare labelled-field accuracy (baseline 35/44), target types (14/20), the count of 'conflict' fields after fusion, the number of crops requested per leaf, model requests per leaf and wall time from the per-call timing log. Separately count glyph-level mismatches on ИНН/КПП and org names.

findings.title: Benchmark Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (MoE) for speed: workload is prompt-processing-bound
findings.claim: Model calls are 90% of wall time, and each call reads about 11.4k input tokens and writes about 236. So the cost is processing the input, which scales with the parameters used per token: about 3B for this MoE model vs 27B for the dense one. The project's own one-clip trial already showed 156.8 s vs 231.2 s with the same 9/10 fields. On the Russian benchmark it ties Qwen3.6-27B overall (0.691 vs 0.692) and beats Qwen3.8-27B on OCR (0.847 vs 0.797) and KIE (0.840 vs 0.807). Its cache for full-attention layers is tiny (10 such layers with 2 KV heads, about 10 KB per token at q8_0), which leaves room for --parallel slots.
findings.evidence: https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B: "35B total, 3B activated", 40 layers, 256 experts (8 routed + 1 shared), OmniDocBench1.5 89.9, CC-OCR 81.9, Apache-2.0, vLLM>=0.19.0, SGLang>=0.5.10. https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B comparison table: OCRBench 90.0 (35B-A3B) vs 89.4 (27B). https://github.com/mts-ai/MWS-Vision-Bench test: "Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | 0.691 | 0.847 | 0.755 | 0.094 | 0.840". config.json: num_key_value_heads 2, head_dim 256, 10 full-attention layers. https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF: UD-Q4_K_XL 22.4 GB, UD-Q5_K_M 26.5 GB, UD-Q6_K 29.3 GB, mmproj-F16 899 MB.
findings.expected_speed_effect: Large. Expect roughly 1.3–2x lower model time per call, consistent with the 156.8 vs 231.2 s trial. More if --parallel 2–4 is enabled for the phase1 leaf concurrency, since the cache costs only about 0.2 GB per 16k-token slot.
findings.expected_precision_effect: About equal to Qwen3.6-27B on Russian benchmarks and better than the current Qwen3.8-27B on OCR and KIE. MoE models can be more sensitive to quantization; at Q4 it may lose glyph accuracy.
findings.risk: Q6_K (29.3 GB) plus mmproj and vision compute buffers is tight on 32 GB with --image-max-tokens 4096; Q5_K_M (26.5 GB) is the safer ceiling. The single-clip trial is not significant. MoE routing is deterministic at temperature 0, but llama.cpp batch-size effects can still change outputs between parallel and serial runs, so check reproducibility. Same grounding weakness as Qwen3.6-27B (0.094).
findings.how_to_test: Same A/B as above with UD-Q5_K_M and then UD-Q4_K_XL. Record peak memory from nvidia-smi, input tokens per second from the per-call timing log, and accuracy on the 44 labelled fields. Then repeat with llama-server --parallel 2 and phase1 leaf concurrency on, and compare wall time on video 5 (baseline 2665 s main / phase1 measured).

findings.title: Check prefix-cache reuse for hybrid DeltaNet models on llama.cpp; vLLM is the fallback
findings.claim: All Qwen3.5/3.6/3.8 models are hybrid recurrent/attention models. llama.cpp cannot cut a recurrent state back to an arbitrary point; it can only restore saved snapshots, and users report full re-processing of the prompt when those restores fail. With about 24k characters of instructions and schema per call, plus 73% of input tokens coming from the prefix cache in the V7 batch, any regression here directly multiplies prompt-processing time. vLLM 0.30/0.31 reportedly reaches 93–99% prefix-cache hits on Qwen3.8-27B. Its Blackwell-native NVFP4 or INT4 builds keep the vision tower in BF16 and fit in 32 GB with room for several parallel sequences.
findings.evidence: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/22384: "server: fix context checkpoint restore for hybrid/recurrent models (DeltaNet/Mamba)", closed 2026-04-26 by ggerganov with "The fix is incorrect"; the reporter says full reprocessing persists in b8943. https://www.v2ex.com/t/1219800 (2026-06-12 to 08-03): Qwen3.6-27B, a ~19K-token prompt checked against checkpoints at 39K–71K was rejected and "reprocessed from BOS". https://friendli.ai/models/Twu31/Qwen3.8-27B-AWQ-INT4-MTP-LowLatency: vLLM flags "--enable-prefix-caching --prefix-match-unit 16 --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16", hit rate "about 99%" with MTP off and "93–98% (vLLM 0.29)" with MTP K=2, weights about 18.2 GB, vision tower kept in BF16. https://huggingface.co/HivenetQuant/Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4 (vision encoder BF16).
findings.expected_speed_effect: If llama.cpp is currently losing cached prefixes between calls on the same leaf, vLLM could cut prompt-processing time substantially. Batching across leaves would add on top. Zero gain if llama.cpp is already reusing prefixes.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Neutral by itself. 4-bit NVFP4 or AWQ weights may lose some glyph accuracy compared with Q6 GGUF; the vision tower stays BF16.
findings.risk: vLLM on sm_120 needs a CUDA 12.8/13 build, and community recipes mention CUDA-graph crash workarounds (vllm#40807). Quantized builds are community-made, with no independent vision accuracy numbers. A second serving stack means a new systemd unit; the managed proxy and network setup must not be touched. Outputs at temperature 0 are not bit-identical between stacks, so they need a fresh label check. Stored answers are never replayed, so every comparison means re-running the model.
findings.how_to_test: First check llama.cpp itself. The phase1 per-call usage counters log cached prompt tokens against total prompt tokens; compute that ratio per call within a single leaf conversation and across leaves on video 5. If within-leaf reuse is well below (prompt length minus new turn), stand up vLLM with Qwen3.6-27B or Qwen3.8-27B in INT4/NVFP4 and repeat the run. Compare prompt-processing seconds per call and cache-hit counts at equal accuracy.

findings.title: Keep Qwen3.8-27B as the control and check whether its grounding edge matters for zoom_regions
findings.claim: Qwen3.8-27B is the only open Qwen with meaningful grounding on Russian documents (0.223 vs 0.062–0.099 for Qwen3.6). If zoom_regions depends on model-emitted box coordinates landing on the right field, a Qwen3.6 swap could request worse crops and need more turns. Measure crop usefulness, not just final accuracy, before choosing.
findings.evidence: https://github.com/mts-ai/MWS-Vision-Bench test grounding column: Qwen3.8-27B 0.223, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 0.094, Qwen3.6-27B 0.062, Qwen3.5-27B 0.073, Gemma 4 31B 0.043. https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B: OmniDocBench 1.5 91.1 (vs 89.4 Qwen3.6-27B).
findings.expected_speed_effect: Indirect. Better crops mean fewer zoom calls per leaf; the hard leaves currently take 44–106 calls.
findings.expected_precision_effect: May offset part of Qwen3.6's OCR advantage if crops miss fields.
findings.risk: The MWS grounding task (locating text on a page) may not match how image_agent asks for regions. The low grounding scores could be prompt-format issues rather than ability.
findings.how_to_test: From the A/B runs, log each zoom_regions call's boxes and whether the next turn's answer used text from that crop (field value found in the crop's OCR). Compare crops per confirmed field and the zoom-loop share of calls between Qwen3.8-27B, Qwen3.6-27B and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B.

findings.title: Add Gemma 4 31B as the single non-Qwen control; expect lower Russian OCR
findings.claim: Gemma 4 is the only non-Qwen family that fits 32 GB, has official ggml-org GGUFs, built-in tool use and an Apache-2.0 license, and is close to Qwen on document parsing. It scores clearly lower on Russian OCR (0.734 vs 0.861), so treat it as a check on whether errors are Qwen-specific, not as an expected winner. Its image budget tops out at 1120 tokens, versus up to 4096 in the current setup, so it depends more on the native-resolution crops.
findings.evidence: https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-31B-it: 30.7B dense, 256K context, Apache 2.0, visual token budget "70, 140, 280, 560, or 1120 tokens", "Native support for structured tool use", OmniDocBench 1.5 edit distance 0.131 (Gemma 3 27B: 0.365 per https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it). https://github.com/mts-ai/MWS-Vision-Bench test: "Gemma 4 31B IT | 0.613 | 0.734 | 0.700 | 0.043 | 0.793". https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/docs/multimodal.md lists "gemma-4-31B-it-GGUF". https://huggingface.co/unsloth/gemma-4-31B-it-GGUF: Q5_K_M 21.7 GB, mmproj-F16 1.2 GB.
findings.expected_speed_effect: Probably slower than Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (dense 31B), but fewer image tokens per image (at most 1120) cut prompt size.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Likely lower on Cyrillic OCR per MWS; possibly different and complementary error types.
findings.risk: Sliding-window attention: reusing the prompt cache in llama.cpp may need --swa-full, which at 16k context adds about 7 GB of cache (50 local layers x 16 KV heads x 256 dims), squeezing Q6. Different tool-call and template format. Recommended sampling is temperature 1.0; behaviour at temperature 0 is untested.
findings.how_to_test: Same labelled-video A/B with Q5_K_M and image tokens set to the maximum (1120). Compare field accuracy and tool-call parse failures.

findings.title: Optional: offload orientation and triage to Qwen3.5-4B or 9B
findings.claim: Orientation is 75 of 424 calls on video 5, and each sends four rotated 1024-px images. That is a coarse vision task a 4B–9B model of the same family can likely handle. Next to Qwen3.6-35B-A3B at Q4 (about 25 GB), a Qwen3.5-4B Q8 plus mmproj (about 5 GB, estimate) could fit on the same 32 GB card as a second llama-server.
findings.evidence: https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B: 201 languages, OCRBench 89.2 (9B) / 85.0 (4B), OmniDocBench1.5 87.7 / 86.2, Apache-2.0. https://github.com/mts-ai/MWS-Vision-Bench test: Qwen3.5-9B 0.624 overall, Qwen3.5-4B 0.602. https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3.8 README: Qwen3.5-9B/4B/2B/0.8B released 2026-03-02.
findings.expected_speed_effect: Orientation and triage calls could run several times faster (estimate, not measured), saving part of the about 18% of calls they make up.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Neutral if orientation accuracy holds; a wrong rotation would hurt every later read of that leaf.
findings.risk: Two servers on one GPU compete for memory and compute. The 26 GB used by the current 27B Q6 setup leaves no room, so this only works with the MoE at Q4 or with vLLM. The out-of-scope triage decision must still record the heading literally (business rule), so a weaker model could mislabel forms.
findings.how_to_test: Offline, replay the orientation prompts from the timing log for all leaves of the 11-video batch through Qwen3.5-4B and 9B. Measure agreement with the current orientation choice and seconds per call before wiring it in.

findings.title: Do not spend benchmark time on the other families listed in the task
findings.claim: Each fails on size, Russian evidence or document strength. InternVL3.5 is the latest InternVL (no 3.6 or 4 found); its Russian evidence covers multilingual question-answering only, and the family was historically very weak on Russian OCR. GLM-4.6V-Flash lists only Chinese and English. MiniCPM-V 4.5/4.6, Kimi-VL-A3B (2025) and Ministral 3 rank low on OCRBench v2. Molmo 2 is English-only with no OCR scores. Mistral Small 3.2 sits about 0.11 below Qwen3.6 on MWS. Mistral Small 4 (119B), Llama 4 Scout (109B) and GLM-4.6V (106B) do not fit in 32 GB at a usable quantization. Qwen3-VL is superseded by Qwen3.5/3.6. Specialist OCR models such as PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 have no tool calling, no free-form extraction, and their card does not mention Russian.
findings.evidence: https://github.com/OpenGVLab/InternVL: latest news 2025/08/30, InternVL3.5 1B–241B-A28B. https://arxiv.org/html/2508.18265 Table 8: InternVL3.5-30B-A3B Multilingual MMBench ru 83.5. Table 4: OCRBench 880. https://arxiv.org/html/2412.02210 Table 3: CC-OCR Russian: InternVL2-76B 13.18 vs Qwen2-VL-72B 65.94. https://99franklin.github.io/ocrbench_v2/: InternVL3.5-14B EN 47.1; GLM-4.6V-Flash EN 59.0; MiniCPM-V-4.5 ZH 58.8; Kimi-VL-A3B ZH 54.1; Ministral-3-14B EN 43.3. https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-4.6V-Flash: languages Chinese and English, MIT. https://huggingface.co/allenai/Molmo2-8B: English only, no OCR numbers. https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603: "119B total, with 6.5B activated", Russian not listed. https://huggingface.co/meta-llama/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct: 109B total, Russian not listed. MWS test: Mistral Small 3.2 0.577, Qwen3-VL-8B 0.578, Qwen3-VL-32B 0.576. https://huggingface.co/PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR-VL-1.6: no KIE, fixed task prompts.
findings.expected_speed_effect: Saves benchmarking time on the server.
findings.expected_precision_effect: None directly; keeps effort on likely winners.
findings.risk: InternVL3.5-30B-A3B was never run on MWS or OCRBench v2 2026.09, so its Russian document OCR is unmeasured rather than shown to be bad. It is a reasonable 6th candidate if time allows (community GGUF at https://huggingface.co/bartowski/OpenGVLab_InternVL3_5-14B-GGUF).
findings.how_to_test: None needed. If desired, run InternVL3.5-30B-A3B on the public MWS validation split (https://huggingface.co/datasets/MTSAIR/MWS-Vision-Bench) with the repo's vLLM runner and compare its OCR and KIE scores with the Qwen3.6 rows.

research:cloud-baseline.topic: Frontier hosted vs strongest open models on document-OCR benchmarks (OmniDocBench, OCRBench v2, olmOCR-bench) and Russian/multilingual OCR splits, as a ceiling estimate and a downsizing check for the local Qwen pipeline
research:cloud-baseline.summary:
1) Frontier hosted models are not at the top of the public OCR benchmarks in 2026. On OmniDocBench they trail small specialist parsers. PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 paper, v1.6: PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 96.33, Gemini 3 Pro 92.91, Gemini 3 Flash 92.62, GPT-5.2 86.59. Nanonets' own v1.5 run: Gemini-3-Flash 90.1, Gemini-3-Pro 88.8, GPT-5.2 88.0, Claude Sonnet 4.6 86.9, GPT-5.4 85.3. Qwen's self-reported v1.5: Qwen3.8-27B 91.1, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 89.9, Qwen3.5-27B 88.9, Qwen3.5-9B 87.7. On the official OCRBench v2 board (2026.09, private English set), Qwen3.6-27B scores 68.3, Qwen3.8-27B 63.5, Gemini 3 Pro Preview 63.4, Qwen3.5-9B 58.7 and GPT-5 55.5; the top entry is SEEU DOC at 76.2. On olmOCR-bench, open specialists lead: Chandra OCR 2 85.8–85.9, dots.mocr 83.9, olmOCR-2 82.4. Nanonets' runs put the hosted models below them: GPT-5.4 81.0, Gemini 3 Pro 77.7, Claude Opus/Sonnet 4.6 about 74. I found no vendor-published speed figures on these benchmarks. Vendors mostly do not self-report OCR numbers; the exception is Google's Gemini 3 Pro card, OmniDocBench 1.5 edit distance 0.115 vs 0.145 for Sonnet 4.5 and 0.147 for GPT-5.1. These benchmarks are mostly English/Chinese digital PDFs, and self-reported and vendor-run numbers disagree by up to about 11 points. For example, Qwen3.5-9B is 87.7 self-reported vs 76.7 in Nanonets' run.

2) Russian. No open model family publishes a 27B-vs-8B Russian OCR split.
- Qwen cards give only the CC-OCR aggregate. CC-OCR's multilingual track includes Russian, but it is 140 of 150 scene images per language. Qwen3.5-27B scores 81.0 vs 79.3 for Qwen3.5-9B. The Qwen3-VL report shows its 39-language results only as a figure.
- PaddleOCR-VL publishes a Cyrillic edit-distance column, and Datalab publishes a per-language table with a ru row.
- The only benchmark with Russian business documents, a JSON key-information-extraction (KIE) task, and Qwen 27B/9B alongside frontier models is the third-party MWS Vision Bench (GitHub, updated through July 2026). On its private test set:

| Model | KIE | Image→text |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.6-27B | 0.893 | 0.861 |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | 0.840 | 0.847 |
| Qwen3.5-27B | 0.833 | 0.737 |
| Qwen3.8-27B (deployed) | 0.807 | 0.797 |
| Qwen3.5-9B | 0.789 | 0.772 |
| Qwen3-VL-8B | 0.592 | 0.779 |

Best hosted KIE scores on the test set: Cotype Pro 3 0.906, Gemini 3.5 Flash 0.882, GPT-5.6 Sol 0.862. On the validation set, Claude Opus 5.5 scores 0.896 and Gemini 3.6 Flash 0.903. MDPBench (photographed multilingual documents, RU column): Qwen3-VL-8B 61.9 and Qwen3.5-9B 60.3, vs Gemini 3 Pro 85.5 and PaddleOCR-VL-1.5 86.0.

3) Ceiling. On Russian KIE, the best local 27B-class Qwen is within about 0–9 points of hosted frontier models. Hosted models lead clearly only on grounding (0.6–0.7 vs 0.06–0.24). A model swap would therefore not fix the project's biggest loss, which is segmentation (8 of 20 target intervals missed).

4) Downsizing. An 8–9B model would lose noticeably on Russian KIE: 4–10 points vs the 27B-class models, about 30 points for Qwen3-VL-8B, and it is weak on photographed Russian pages. There is also no Qwen3.6 or Qwen3.8 9B. For speed, the better route is the Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MoE. Generation is 69% of model time at 61 tok/s on phase1-speed, and the MoE scores at or above Qwen3.8-27B on Russian text reading and KIE.

5) Qwen3.6-27B reads Russian text better than the deployed Qwen3.8-27B, but Qwen3.8 is clearly better at grounding (0.223 vs 0.062). The zoom_regions tool depends on grounding, so this needs a server A/B test, not a straight swap.

findings.title: Ceiling estimate: on Russian KIE, local 27B-class Qwen is already close to hosted frontier models; segmentation, not the reader model, is the main loss
findings.claim: Treat the reader model as near-ceiling for field reading and put accuracy effort into interval segmentation and other-side handling. On the only Russian business-document KIE benchmark (MWS Vision Bench), hosted frontier models score 0.86–0.91 on the private test set. The best local 27B-class Qwen (Qwen3.6-27B) scores 0.893, and the deployed Qwen3.8-27B 0.807. Hosted models lead clearly only on grounding (GPT-5.6 Sol 0.623 vs Qwen3.8-27B 0.223) and overall score. Even a hosted frontier model would add at most about 5–9 points on field reading. It would not recover the 8 of 20 target intervals that segmentation misses, which is the largest measured loss.
findings.evidence: https://github.com/mts-ai/MWS-Vision-Bench, private test set (Overall / img→text / KIE / Grounding): GPT-5.6 Sol 0.789 / 0.836 / 0.862 / 0.623; Cotype Pro 3 0.747 / 0.859 / 0.906 / 0.437; Claude Sonnet 5 0.738 / 0.842 / 0.830 / 0.374; Gemini 3.5 Flash 0.672 / 0.789 / 0.882 / 0.050; Qwen3.6-27B 0.692 / 0.861 / 0.893 / 0.062; Qwen3.8-27B 0.687 / 0.797 / 0.807 / 0.223. Validation set: Claude Opus 5.5 KIE 0.896; Gemini 3.6 Flash KIE 0.903; GPT-6.1 Sol overall 0.822. The page gives no KIE formula, only that metrics are 'adapted from OCRBench v2 with Russian optimizations'. Project facts: '8/20 target intervals MISSED by segmentation (biggest loss)'. analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md: 'labelled intervals detected 14/15 both'.
findings.expected_speed_effect: None directly. It argues against spending GPU or latency budget on larger or hosted readers.
findings.expected_precision_effect: A frontier reader would add at most about 5–9 points on field-level KIE (benchmark proxy) and nothing on missed intervals.
findings.risk: MWS is a third-party benchmark. Inference settings (temperature, thinking, image size) are not stated, and the KIE metric is unspecified. Its documents (scans, tables, handwriting, personal documents) are not handheld video frames of УПД/ТОРГ-12/ТТН/ТрН. Hosted models are out of scope for the product anyway.
findings.how_to_test: Split the 9 wrong of 44 labelled fields by error class (missed interval, other side, role, address boundary, glyph) from the existing evaluation output. Only the glyph and role classes are reader-model-limited; count them to bound the possible gain from any model swap.

findings.title: A/B Qwen3.6-27B against the deployed Qwen3.8-27B: better Russian text reading and KIE, much weaker grounding
findings.claim: Run a model-only A/B on the server: same git ref, same flags, same quant level, swapping MODEL_PATH/MMPROJ_PATH to Qwen3.6-27B. Two independent boards show Qwen3.6-27B ahead of Qwen3.8-27B on OCR-style reading. MWS Russian: img→text 0.861 vs 0.797 (test) and 0.863 vs 0.800 (validation); KIE 0.893 vs 0.807 (test) and 0.833 vs 0.812 (validation). OCRBench v2 English 68.3 vs 63.5 (Extraction subscore 92.8 vs 90.4), Chinese 58.7 vs 56.9. Qwen3.8-27B is better at grounding: MWS 0.223 vs 0.062 (test), and OCRBench v2 English Recognition 75.5 vs 71.1. Qwen's own OmniDocBench 1.5 table shows 91.1 vs 89.4. The pipeline's zoom_regions/zoom_source tools need correct coordinates, so the result is not predictable from benchmarks alone. Both models are the same size and hybrid layout, so speed should be roughly equal.
findings.evidence: https://github.com/mts-ai/MWS-Vision-Bench test rows: 'Qwen3.8-27B | 0.687 | 0.797 | 0.738 | 0.223 | 0.807 | 0.873' and 'Qwen3.6-27B | 0.692 | 0.861 | 0.753 | 0.062 | 0.893 | 0.889'. https://99franklin.github.io/ocrbench_v2/ 2026.09 English: Qwen3.6-27B Average 68.3, Recognition 71.1, Extraction 92.8; Qwen3.8-27B Average 63.5, Recognition 75.5, Extraction 90.4. https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B: OmniDocBench 1.5 91.1 (3.8-27B) vs 89.4 (3.6-27B), plus agentic gains such as OSWorld-Verified 84.3 vs 63.9. deploy/sever-model.service: '--model ${MODEL_PATH} --mmproj ${MMPROJ_PATH}'.
findings.expected_speed_effect: About neutral per call (same 27B dense hybrid size). Fewer conflict and joint-review calls are possible if glyph reads agree more often across frames.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Possibly a few points better on glyph and literal-text errors; possibly worse crop placement on hard leaves. The net effect is unknown.
findings.risk: Qwen3.6 and Qwen3.8 need different mmproj files (Unsloth notes Qwen3.6 mmproj is not interchangeable with 3.5). Prompt behaviour and tool-call formatting may differ. With 22–44 labels, a few-field difference is inside the 95% interval (README: 'the 95% interval of either score spans roughly 50–87%').
findings.how_to_test: On the server, run the phase1-speed ref twice on 20260818-5_132107.mp4 and the other labelled videos, once per MODEL_PATH, with no overlapping jobs. Compare the runs with tools/compare_runs.py: labelled fields, conflicts per leaf, joint_review calls, and how often zoom_regions crops miss the target field (inspect the trace).

findings.title: Use the Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MoE, not an 8B model, as the speed option: the pipeline is decode-bound and the MoE does not lose on Russian reading
findings.claim: Generation is 69% of model time at 61 tok/s on the 27B dense model. A 3B-active MoE attacks exactly that. Benchmarks do not show it reading Russian worse than Qwen3.8-27B. MWS test: img→text 0.847 vs 0.797, KIE 0.840 vs 0.807, overall 0.691 vs 0.687. OCRBench v2 English 65.5 vs 63.5. OmniDocBench 1.5 89.9 vs 91.1. It is weaker at grounding (0.094 vs 0.223), which matters for zoom_regions. The project's own earlier one-clip trial already showed the same 9/10 fields in 156.8 s vs 231.2 s. Unsloth reports MTP decode of about 220–240 tok/s for 35B-A3B vs 140–160 tok/s for the 27B on an RTX 6000-class GPU.
findings.evidence: analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md: 'generation 41,696 tokens in 688 s (61 tok/s) = 69% of model time'. https://github.com/mts-ai/MWS-Vision-Bench test: 'Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | 0.691 | 0.847 | 0.755 | 0.094 | 0.840 | 0.920'. https://99franklin.github.io/ocrbench_v2/: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B English 65.5. https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B: OmniDocBench1.5 89.9, CC-OCR 81.9. https://unsloth.ai/docs/models/qwen3.6: '35B-A3B at 240 tokens/s on an RTX 6000', 27B '160 tokens/s'; memory table 35B-A3B 6-bit 30 GB, 4-bit 23 GB; 27B 6-bit 24 GB.
findings.expected_speed_effect: Likely 1.5–3x faster decode per call; the earlier trial measured 0.68x the time for one clip. Prefill is also cheaper. The measured gain will depend on the quant level and on whether more calls are needed.
findings.expected_precision_effect: About neutral to slightly better on literal Russian text (benchmark proxy); risk of worse crop localization.
findings.risk: At Q6 (about 30 GB total per Unsloth), headroom on the 32 GB RTX 5090 with mmproj and q8_0 KV at ctx 65536 is about 1–2 GB, which blocks --parallel N leaf concurrency. Q5_K_M or UD-Q4_K_XL (about 23 GB) is safer, but MoE quantization quality needs checking. Unsloth warns against CUDA 13.2 ('gibberish outputs'). Grounding is weaker than Qwen3.8-27B.
findings.how_to_test: Same model-only A/B as for Qwen3.6-27B: run phase1-speed with MODEL_PATH set to Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q6_K and then UD-Q4_K_XL on the labelled videos. Record llama.cpp timings (generation tok/s, prefill tok/s), nvidia-smi peak memory, calls per leaf, and labelled accuracy via tools/compare_runs.py.

findings.title: Do not downsize to an 8–9B model: it loses 4–10 KIE points on Russian documents and much more on photographed Russian pages
findings.claim: Qwen's own cards suggest the 9B loses little: Qwen3.5-27B vs Qwen3.5-9B is OmniDocBench1.5 88.9 vs 87.7, CC-OCR 81.0 vs 79.3, OCRBench 89.4 vs 89.2. Those numbers are not Russian and not photographed. On Russian business documents (MWS test), KIE is 0.833 for Qwen3.5-27B, 0.789 for Qwen3.5-9B and 0.893 for Qwen3.6-27B. Qwen3-VL-8B scores 0.592 vs 0.671 for Qwen3-VL-32B. On photographed multilingual documents (MDPBench RU), Qwen3-VL-8B scores 61.9 and Qwen3.5-9B 60.3, vs 85.5 for Gemini 3 Pro and 86.0 for PaddleOCR-VL-1.5. CC-OCR V2 says Qwen3.5-9B's performance 'decreases noticeably on ... Russian'. Qwen3.8 has no 9B (the collection lists only 27B and 2.4T-A95B), so a small model would also be an older generation.
findings.evidence: https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-27B and https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B (vision tables). https://github.com/mts-ai/MWS-Vision-Bench test: 'Qwen3.5-9B | 0.624 | 0.772 | 0.638 | 0.072 | 0.789 | 0.850', 'Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct | 0.578 | 0.779 | 0.692 | 0.073 | 0.592 | 0.754'. https://arxiv.org/html/2603.28130v1 Table 2 RU column: Qwen3-VL-Instruct-8b 61.9, Qwen3.5-Instruct-9B 60.3, Gemini-3-pro-preview 85.5, PaddleOCR-VL-1.5 86.0. https://arxiv.org/html/2605.03903 Appendix A.4 (Qwen3.5-9B drops on Russian). https://huggingface.co/collections/Qwen/qwen38.
findings.expected_speed_effect: A 9B dense model would decode about 2–3x faster than the 27B. The 35B-A3B gives similar decode speed without the accuracy loss.
findings.expected_precision_effect: About -4 to -10 KIE points vs the 27B-class models on Russian documents (benchmark proxy). Worse on photographed or angled pages, which is this product's input.
findings.risk: Plain image→text on MWS is not worse for Qwen3.5-9B (0.772 vs 0.737 for Qwen3.5-27B), so a 9B might be acceptable for the one-call out-of-scope triage only. That would need its own test and a second model resident in VRAM.
findings.how_to_test: Optional and cheap: run triage-only calls with Qwen3.5-9B on the 5 out-of-scope and 10 in-scope leaves of video 5 and compare the accept/reject decisions with the current model. Do not test it as the field reader unless the 35B-A3B fails.

findings.title: Small specialist OCR parsers match Gemini 3 Pro on photographed Russian text; use them at most as a glyph cross-check, not as the field reader
findings.claim: PaddleOCR-VL-1.5 (0.9B) has the highest RU score on MDPBench (86.0, vs 85.5 for Gemini 3 Pro). On real-world photographed and scanned pages it beats every general model listed: Real5-OmniDocBench 92.05 vs Gemini-3 Pro 89.24, Qwen3-VL-235B 88.90 and GPT-5.2 78.66. PaddleOCR-VL publishes a Cyrillic edit distance of 0.109 vs 0.220 for Qwen2.5-VL-72B. Datalab's Chandra 2 table gives 85.5% for ru, vs 82.8% for Gemini 2.5 Flash and 72.2% for GPT-5 Mini. These models output page Markdown, not role-labelled fields. They could at most serve as an extra literal transcript to flag glyph conflicts such as «Кашириных» vs «Каширных» before a joint review. The field value and its two-frame confirmation must still come from the VLM readings.
findings.evidence: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.28130v1 Table 2 (PaddleOCR-VL-1.5 RU 86.0, Photo. 75.2). https://arxiv.org/html/2606.03264 Table 3 (Real5-OmniDocBench: PaddleOCR-VL-1.5 92.05, PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 93.19, Gemini-3 Pro 89.24, GPT-5.2 78.66). https://arxiv.org/html/2510.14528 Table 6(a) Cyrillic. https://github.com/datalab-to/chandra ('ru 88.8% 85.5% 88.7% 82.8% 72.2%'). analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md (the one-glyph «Кашириных» vs «Каширных» conflict).
findings.expected_speed_effect: Uncertain. A 0.9B parser is fast, but it adds a second model and service. It saves time only if it replaces joint-review calls.
findings.expected_precision_effect: May reduce glyph-noise conflicts. It cannot fix role or address-boundary errors.
findings.risk: Business rules: stored answers are never replayed, values must be literal, and confirmation needs two distinct source frames from the field reader. An OCR transcript must never fill or repair a value. Serving is mainly vLLM/SGLang for these models. Chandra's weights use a modified OpenRAIL-M license with a revenue cap. A second resident model eats into VRAM.
findings.how_to_test: Offline only: run PaddleOCR-VL-1.5 on the saved full-resolution primary and seed frames of the 4 hard leaves. Check whether its transcript contains the labelled literal for the conflict and glyph-error fields, and how often it disagrees with the label.

findings.title: Public OCR benchmarks cannot settle model choice at this label size; grow the labelled set first
findings.claim:
OmniDocBench is near saturation (open models above 94% on v1.5) and is mostly digital English/Chinese pages. olmOCR-bench is English PDF unit tests. OCRBench v2 covers only English and Chinese. Different groups get very different numbers for the same model on the same benchmark:
- Qwen3.5-9B on OmniDocBench 1.5: 87.7 self-reported vs 76.7 in Nanonets' run.
- GPT-5.4: 85.3 (Nanonets) vs 89.1 (another aggregator).
- Gemini 3 Pro: 90.33 (Codesota) vs 88.8 (Nanonets).
The gaps that matter here are 4–9 KIE points on Russian documents, which is 2–4 of 44 labelled fields and inside the noise. The model decision needs more customer-approved labels on the real form types.
findings.evidence: https://www.llamaindex.ai/blog/omnidocbench-is-saturated-what-s-next-for-ocr-benchmarks (GLM-OCR 94.6%, PaddleOCR-VL-1.5 above 94%; small, narrow dataset). https://benchmarking.nanonets.com/benchmarks/omnidocbench (Qwen3.5-9B 76.7, GPT-5.4 85.3, Gemini-3-Pro 88.8). https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B (OmniDocBench1.5 87.7). https://www.codesota.com/ocr/benchmark/omnidocbench (Gemini 3 Pro 90.33). analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md ('with 22 labels the 95% interval of either score spans roughly 50–87%').
findings.expected_speed_effect: None.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Makes a 4–9 point model difference measurable (about 150+ labelled fields are needed to resolve ±5 points).
findings.risk: Labels are provisional and the address-boundary convention changed on 11.10. Labelling cost and customer acceptance are pending.
findings.how_to_test: Label all 19 fields on every in-scope sheet of the 11 V7 videos (273 sheets in the batch) under the current address-block rule. Then rerun both model A/B candidates and report per-class accuracy with confidence intervals.

findings.title: Decode-side speedup available on the current model: llama.cpp MTP speculative decoding for Qwen3.6/3.8 hybrids
findings.claim: Generation is the dominant cost, and Qwen3.8-27B is trained with MTP. llama.cpp has merged MTP speculative decoding; Unsloth reports about 1.4x for dense and 1.15–1.2x for MoE at 2 draft tokens, with 'no change in accuracy'. Greedy speculative decoding should give the same output as plain greedy decoding at temperature 0. Check whether an MTP-enabled GGUF of Qwen3.8-27B exists and works with --mmproj.
findings.evidence: https://unsloth.ai/docs/models/qwen3.6: 'llama.cpp has merged MTP support', flags '--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 2', 'Average speedup is about 1.4x for dense models', acceptance drops from 83% to 50% with 4 draft tokens; the 35B-A3B MTP example includes --mmproj, the 27B example does not. https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B: 'MTP (Multi-Token Prediction): trained with multiple steps'. analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md: 69% of model time in generation.
findings.expected_speed_effect: About 1.3–1.4x faster generation on the dense 27B, so roughly 20–25% less model time per sheet if acceptance holds on short JSON and tool-call outputs.
findings.expected_precision_effect: None expected at temperature 0 (lossless greedy speculation); verify that the outputs are byte-identical.
findings.risk: Needs an MTP-enabled GGUF for the exact model, plus a newer llama.cpp build (PR #22673 or later) and about 1 GB more VRAM. Compatibility with vision input and prompt caching for this hybrid architecture is unverified. Speculation can interact with tool-call grammar parsing.
findings.how_to_test: Restart llama-server with the MTP flags on a staging port. Replay the same leaf's requests and compare response bytes and llama.cpp timings (predicted_per_second, draft acceptance) against the current server.

findings.title: Russian-specific failure mode: Cyrillic/Latin lookalike letters can pass two-frame fusion unnoticed
findings.claim: MDPBench reports that on Russian documents models 'frequently suffer from visual confusion'; the search summary of the same paper names Cyrillic/Latin lookalike letters as the main failure, but that wording was not in the fetched text. image_fusion._literal_comparison uses NFKC+casefold, which does not map Latin С/Р/О/А/Е/К to their Cyrillic forms. Two frames that both return a Latin lookalike would agree and be confirmed. A check that flags (never rewrites) mixed-script words in Cyrillic fields as 'unreadable/conflict' for joint review would follow the literal-value rule.
findings.evidence: https://arxiv.org/html/2603.28130v1 ('For Russian documents, models frequently suffer from visual confusion'). sever/image_fusion.py lines ~38-41: 'return " ".join(unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", value).casefold().split())'. grep found no homoglyph or mixed-script check in sever/*.py; the only related comment is in vision.py ('A Latin/Cyrillic prefix difference never authorizes rewriting the actual script').
findings.expected_speed_effect: Negligible. It may add a joint-review call on flagged fields.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Small. It catches silent script errors in confirmed fields, if any exist; the frequency in this data is unknown.
findings.risk: Legitimate Latin text occurs in values (brand names, 'LLC', vehicle plates, e-mail addresses), so the check needs a token-level rule and an allow-list. It must only flag and never repair, per the business rules.
findings.how_to_test: Scan the existing results.json files of all V7 and phase1 runs for words in organization or address fields that mix Cyrillic and Latin letters, and count them before writing any code.

candidates.name: Qwen3.6-27B
candidates.params_or_size: 27B dense, hybrid Gated DeltaNet + gated attention (same family as Qwen3.5-27B), vision encoder

research:ocr-specialist.topic: Dedicated document-OCR / document-parsing models (Oct 2026) as a replacement for, or a stage before, the general VLM in the Север pipeline: Russian printed forms photographed by phone, 19 literal fields, evidence boxes required, one RTX 5090.
research:ocr-specialist.summary:
No public benchmark measures what Север needs: field-level literal accuracy on Russian forms photographed by phone. Three proxies come closest:
- **MDPBench** (Mar 2026): 17 languages including RU, with photographed copies of each page.
- **GlotOCR Bench** (Apr 2026): Cyrillic sentences, rendered rather than photographed, scored as the share read with ≤5% character errors.
- **Real5-OmniDocBench** (Jan–Mar 2026): photographed and warped pages, but in Chinese and English.

These proxies rank the models differently, so leaderboard scores cannot pick the model.

**Strongest local candidates for Cyrillic on photos, with usable boxes:**
- **PaddleOCR-VL-1.5/1.6** (0.9B, Apache-2.0). Russian is explicitly listed. It scores Real5 93.19 (1.6), MDPBench RU 76.0 (1.5) and GlotOCR Cyrillic 78.0. It returns per-line 4-point boxes (`Spotting:`) and block bboxes, and runs in llama.cpp since Feb 2026, without the layout stage.
- **dots.ocr / dots.mocr** (3B, MIT). GlotOCR Cyrillic 86.0/83.5 and MDPBench RU 66.8/71.2. It returns one layout JSON with a bbox per block and can read a given bbox. It runs in llama.cpp since Apr 2026.
- **HunyuanOCR-1.5** (1B, Tencent community licence). GlotOCR Cyrillic 86.8 (version not stated) and MDPBench RU 67.4. It has text spotting with coordinates and llama.cpp plus DFlash speculative decoding.
- **MonkeyOCRv2-B** (0.7B, Apache-2.0). MDPBench RU 80.1 and Photo 81.7, but MDPBench comes from the same lab, and it has no documented boxes.
- **Chandra-2** (5B). Russian 85.5% on Datalab's own benchmark and MDPBench RU 74.0, but the weights licence is restrictive and boxes are not documented.

**Weak on Cyrillic or photos:**
- GLM-OCR: GlotOCR Cyrillic 26.2.
- DeepSeek-OCR-2: Real5 73.01, skew 61.28, Cyrillic 57.8.
- MinerU2.5: MDPBench RU 8.6 (Pro 62.6).
- Nanonets-OCR2: RU 45.5.
- LightOnOCR-2: RU 54.3. LightOnOCR-3 makes no Russian claim.
- Granite-Docling: no Russian.
- OvisOCR2 and TeleOCR: top OmniDocBench v1.6 scores (96.58 / 96.87), but zh/en only and no line boxes.
- Even Gemini-3-pro reaches only 84.9 RU on MDPBench.
- Look-alike Latin letters replacing Cyrillic is a documented failure. PaddleOCR-VL turned МОСКВА into MOCKBA, and Cyrillic script accuracy ranges 94.2–99.2%. This clashes with the rule that values must be literal.

**Should a two-stage design (specialist OCR, then an LLM mapping text to fields) replace the zoom agent?**
- **Speed:** it is likely a large gain. Today a sheet costs about 34 calls of about 5.7 s each. Two-stage is one OCR pass per frame plus one text-only mapping call. I estimate roughly 3–5x on clean leaves. This is not measured.
- **Accuracy:** unknown, and it risks more role and address-boundary errors once the page layout is reduced to text.
- **History:** the repo's earlier OCR-gated mode (`ocr_guided`) once returned "unknown" for every leaf (README:80).

**Recommendation:** use OCR before the VLM (a hybrid), not instead of it.
- A small OCR model on a second llama-server supplies line boxes, orientation, form heading and out-of-scope triage.
- Its boxes guide the zoom crops and its region IDs become evidence.
- The VLM stays as fallback for conflicts.
- The first step is an offline test of how often the OCR output contains the labelled values: S–M effort, using frames already saved on the server.

All 5090 speed figures here are estimates. Published speeds are from A100/H100 GPUs.

findings.title: Run an offline OCR test on saved frames before changing the design; shortlist PaddleOCR-VL-1.5/1.6, dots.ocr/dots.mocr, HunyuanOCR-1.5, MonkeyOCRv2-B, plus PP-OCRv5 as a baseline
findings.claim:
Public proxies disagree on Cyrillic. HunyuanOCR scores 86.8 on GlotOCR Cyrillic but only 52.2 (v1.0) / 67.4 (v1.5) MDPBench RU. GLM-OCR scores 94.62 on OmniDocBench v1.5 but 26.2 on GlotOCR Cyrillic. MonkeyOCRv2 leads MDPBench RU (80.1), but MDPBench comes from the same lab. So the only valid way to choose is to measure on the project's own frames. Shortlist:
- PaddleOCR-VL-1.5 and 1.6: line-level boxes, Russian explicitly listed, best Real5 photo robustness.
- dots.ocr and dots.mocr: block bbox JSON, best open GlotOCR Cyrillic, can read a given bbox.
- HunyuanOCR-1.5: text spotting with coordinates, llama.cpp with DFlash.
- MonkeyOCRv2-B: best MDPBench RU and Photo.
- PP-OCRv5 eslav (classic line detector plus recognizer): baseline that gives line polygons.
Optional: Chandra-2, only if its licence is acceptable.
Exclude:
- GLM-OCR: Cyrillic Acc@5 26.2.
- DeepSeek-OCR-2: Real5 skew 61.28, warping 66.53, Cyrillic 57.8.
- MinerU2.5: MDPBench RU 8.6; Pro 62.6, zh/en only.
- Granite-Docling: no Russian.
- Nanonets-OCR2: RU 45.5, no boxes.
- olmOCR-2: English, no boxes.
- OvisOCR2 and TeleOCR: zh/en, no text-line boxes.
findings.evidence:
Proxy scores (Russian/Cyrillic and photo robustness):
- https://arxiv.org/html/2603.28130 (MDPBench Table 2, RU is the 19th value; I checked the column order against the Latin and non-Latin averages): dots.ocr 66.8, dots.mocr 71.2, PaddleOCR-VL 56.9, HunyuanOCR 52.2, olmOCR2 65.8, GLM-OCR 64.2, DeepSeek-OCR 36.2, MinerU-2.5-VLM 8.6, Gemini-3-pro 84.9.
- https://huggingface.co/datasets/Delores-Lin/MDPBench: PaddleOCR-VL-1.5 RU 76.0, 1.6 70.7, chandra-ocr-2 74.0, MonkeyOCRv2-B 80.1, HunyuanOCR-1.5 67.4, LightOnOCR-2-1B 54.3.
- https://arxiv.org/html/2604.12978 (GlotOCR Tables 5/6, Cyrillic Acc@5 / script accuracy): dots.ocr 86.0/99.2, HunyuanOCR 86.8/98.5, dots.mocr 83.5/99.2, PaddleOCR-VL-1.5 78.0/97.8, GLM-OCR 26.2/98.2, DeepSeek-OCR-2 57.8/94.2.
- https://huggingface.co/datasets/PaddlePaddle/Real5-OmniDocBench: PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 overall 93.19 (skew 92.66), dots.ocr 86.38, DeepSeek-OCR 2 73.01.
- https://huggingface.co/zenosai/MonkeyOCRv2-B-Parsing: RU among its 17 languages, MDPBench RU 80.1. The authors are from HUST (Yuliang Liu); the MDPBench repo is Yuliang-Liu/MultimodalOCR.
From the repo:
- analysis/ground-truth-expanded-provisional.json: the 44 labelled fields.
- README.md:203: evidence today = coordinates of the sent image or crop, `region_index=null`.
findings.expected_speed_effect: None on production. This is offline evaluation. Estimated cost: about 30–60 frames × 6 models × a few seconds each, so well under an hour of GPU time.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Indirect. It sets an upper bound on accuracy before any redesign. If no OCR model has the exact labelled literal for most fields on two distinct frames, the two-stage design is ruled out cheaply.
findings.risk:
- The labels are provisional and few (44 fields), so the test has little statistical power.
- The test competes with production for the GPU, so run it under the existing shared inference lock.
- Chandra-2 weights forbid competitive commercial use (https://huggingface.co/datalab-to/chandra-ocr-2).
- HunyuanOCR uses the Tencent Hunyuan Community License; check its territory clause.
- Re-running OCR on stored frames is evaluation only. It must not become a cached production answer, because stored model answers are never replayed.
findings.how_to_test:
1. Take the saved full-resolution primary and seed PNGs for the labelled sheets of the 4 videos, plus all 15 leaves of video 20260818-5 from the 2026-10-17 run directory.
2. Run each candidate once per frame:
   - PaddleOCR-VL `Spotting:` and `OCR:` on layout blocks.
   - dots.ocr `prompt_layout_all_en`.
   - HunyuanOCR spotting.
   - MonkeyOCRv2 parsing.
   - PP-OCRv5 eslav.
   Use a second llama-server on port 8091, or the PaddleOCR vLLM sm120 container, at temperature 0.
3. Record per frame: wall seconds, output tokens and peak VRAM (nvidia-smi).
4. Score per labelled field:
   - (a) exact literal hit: the ground-truth value appears inside one block or line after the same presentation normalization `image_fusion.fuse_readings` uses.
   - (b) the hit holds on at least 2 distinct frames.
   - (c) the box overlaps the hand-marked field area.
   - (d) number of tokens mixing Latin and Cyrillic letters.
5. Report the hit rate separately for the УПД, ТОРГ-12, ТТН and ТрН address blocks.

findings.title: Use OCR before the VLM (hybrid), not instead of it: OCR line boxes become zoom proposals and evidence, VLM stays as fallback
findings.claim:
Add an OCR step per selected frame, using the winner of the bake-off. Its text lines and boxes, with stable IDs, are transformed into source-frame coordinates the same way `_source_transform` does for crops. They are passed to `read_frame_agent` alongside the 1024 px context image. Then:
- In the first request the agent can ask `zoom_regions` for every label anchor it needs (Продавец, Грузоотправитель, ИНН/КПП, address blocks) in one go, instead of finding them over several requests.
- Fields whose literal is already readable in OCR lines get a region ID as evidence. These are real text locations, where today evidence boxes only bound the uploaded panels.
- The VLM stays the decision maker for form type, roles and blank fields. This avoids the failure of the old OCR-gated mode, where an OCR gate yielded `unknown` with zero reads.
findings.evidence:
From the repo:
- sever/image_agent.py:34-35: `MAX_MODEL_REQUESTS = 8`, `MAX_ZOOM_IMAGES = 8`.
- sever/image_agent.py:141: `uploaded.thumbnail((1024, 1024), ...)`.
- sever/image_reader.py:420: "Evidence boxes delimit uploaded panels in the saved source frame, not measured word locations."
- README.md:203: `ocr_guided` kept links to real OCR regions; `native_image` keeps `region_index=null`.
- README.md:80: the v6.1 full run of the old mode was stopped; every candidate got `unknown` and there were zero image reading calls.
- sever/image_reader.py:1: the reader is described as running without an OCR classification gate.
- sever/ocr.py:56-72: the existing Apple Vision regions already carry `bbox` and `region_index`.
From the web:
- PaddleOCR-VL-1.5 Spotting emits text plus 8 `<LOC_0..1000>` tokens per line, as a 4-point quadrilateral: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21957
- dots.ocr emits JSON with a bbox `[x1,y1,x2,y2]`, a category and text per element: https://huggingface.co/rednote-hilab/dots.ocr
findings.expected_speed_effect: Estimate, not measured. Field-agent calls were 294 of 424 on video 5. If OCR anchors let most frames finish in 2–3 agent requests instead of up to 8, field-agent time could fall by about 30–50%. The OCR step adds about 1–5 s per frame. That figure comes from A100 batch-1 measurements of 0.6–1.1 s per page (https://habr.com/ru/companies/mts_ai/articles/1065182/); dense УПД pages will produce more tokens.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Likely positive for role confusion and address-block boundaries, because the agent sees explicit label lines and their geometry. Neutral to slightly positive for glyph errors, because crops can be centred on the actual line. Evidence quality improves: real line boxes in place of panel boxes.
findings.risk:
- Adding OCR text to the prompt may lead the VLM to copy OCR errors (anchoring), e.g. Latin look-alikes or a dropped Й. Mark the OCR text as hints only, and require the final literal to come from a zoom crop.
- More input tokens per call (about 1–3k).
- OCR boxes are themselves model predictions. Reject a box whose crop OCR does not re-read to the same string.
- The business rule still needs two distinct frames, and OCR from the same frame is not an independent confirmation.
findings.how_to_test:
1. Implement behind a flag, e.g. `HARNESS_OCR_HINTS`.
2. Run `deploy/ab_speed_test.sh` on video 20260818-5 with and without the flag on phase1-speed.
3. Compare with `tools/compare_runs.py`: requests per leaf, seconds per leaf (from page_selected events), stop reasons.
4. Score the 44 labelled fields with `deploy/evaluate_server_results.py`.
5. Accept if fields correct is ≥ the current 35/44 and field-agent requests fall by ≥30%.

findings.title: Two-stage replacement (OCR text and boxes, then a text-only LLM fills the 19 fields): big speed upside, unproven accuracy, keep it as an experiment
findings.claim:
A full replacement would be:
- one OCR pass per frame, keeping only non-table layout blocks so the large goods table is not decoded;
- one text-only call with the existing `submit_reading` tool and compact schema, whose inputs are lines with region IDs and coordinates;
- confirmation on 2 frames, as today.
This removes the image tokens from LLM calls (about 11.4k input tokens per call today) and the zoom loop. The text stage could use the current 27B or the faster Qwen3.6-35B-A3B already tried. The accuracy risks are the reasons to run it only as an A/B arm:
- Role mapping on УПД and ТТН depends on the visual table structure.
- Errors carry over from the OCR stage.
- OCR models are tuned for page-to-markdown, not literal key-value extraction.
- No controlled 2026 study comparing two-stage and end-to-end extraction on forms was found.
findings.evidence:
Measured today (task facts): ~11.4k input and ~236 output tokens per call, ~5.7 s per call, ~34 calls and 174 s per sheet on V7.
- README.md:78: in the earlier trial the 35B-A3B gave the same 9/10 fields in 156.83 s vs 231.19 s for the 27B.
- sever/image_agent.py:252: `output_type=ToolOutput(_NativeReadingResponse, name="submit_reading", strict=False)`. The structured-output path can be reused for text input.
- Speeds on other GPUs, batch 1 on A100 (https://habr.com/ru/companies/mts_ai/articles/1065182/, Jul 2026): PaddleOCR-VL 98.7 pages/min on vLLM, dots.ocr 61.6, DeepSeek-OCR 56.3.
- LightOnOCR-3-1B single-page latency 2.7 s on H100: https://huggingface.co/blog/lightonai/lightonocr-3
- Even Gemini-3-pro reaches only 84.9 RU (page-level edit-distance score) on MDPBench (https://arxiv.org/html/2603.28130), so OCR text will contain errors on photographed pages.
findings.expected_speed_effect: Estimate, not measured. About 1–5 s of OCR plus one 5–8 s text call per frame, and 2 frames per leaf, gives about 15–25 s per clean leaf vs 52–76 s measured. For the 4 hard leaves (72% of calls), the effect depends on whether OCR output agrees across frames more often than VLM readings do; unknown.
findings.expected_precision_effect:
Uncertain, could go either way:
- Probably better on glyph consistency if the OCR model is strong on Cyrillic.
- Probably worse on role and address boundaries unless boxes and reading order are kept in the prompt.
- New error class: OCR hallucinating fluent text (GlotOCR reports that models produce fluent text in a familiar script rather than admit they cannot read).
findings.risk:
- Repeats the failure of the old OCR-first mode (README.md:80) if OCR classification is allowed to gate reading.
- Literal values could pass through OCR normalisation (markdown, merged lines, quote changes).
- OCR output must be produced fresh each job, never cached across jobs, under the no-replay rule.
- The 'address = entire printed block' rule depends on block segmentation. PP-DocLayout or dots layout blocks may split or merge the org/РЦ/ИНН-КПП lines.
findings.how_to_test:
1. Build an offline harness: OCR JSON from the bake-off goes into one text-only `submit_reading` call per frame, then the existing `fuse_readings` across 2 frames.
2. Run it on the 4 labelled videos with the 27B and the 35B-A3B.
3. Compare fields correct (of 44), type correct (of 20) and seconds per leaf against the phase1-speed A/B baseline from 2026-10-17.
4. Add error-class tallies: role confusion, address boundary, glyph.

findings.title: Replace the orientation and out-of-scope triage VLM calls with OCR signals that already exist in the repo
findings.evidence:
From the repo:
- sever/image_orientation.py:1-4: the orientation call is described as an isolated fresh choice of source-image orientation, using four rotated context images.
- sever/ocr.py:188: `def _orientation_score(result: dict, pixel_size: tuple[int, int]) -> dict:` ("Prefer horizontal text and headers above footers").
- sever/ocr.py:27-30: the `_DOCUMENT_TITLE` regex already matches ТОВАРНО-ТРАНСПОРТНАЯ НАКЛАДНАЯ, ТОВАРНАЯ НАКЛАДНАЯ, СЧЁТ-ФАКТУРА, УНИВЕРСАЛЬНЫЙ ПЕРЕДАТОЧНЫЙ ДОКУМЕНТ.
- sever/zoom_image_reader.py:8-10: imports `choose_reading_rotation` and `triage_frame`.
Measured today: orientation 75 of 424 calls on main; 5 out-of-scope leaves at 7–8 calls and 23–40 s each.
From the web:
- PP-OCRv5 eslav recognizer: 81.6% line accuracy on 7,031 ru/be/uk text images; outputs `dt_polys` and `rec_boxes`: https://www.paddleocr.ai/main/en/version3.x/algorithm/PP-OCRv5/PP-OCRv5_multi_languages.html
- The PaddleOCR-VL pipeline has `use_doc_orientation_classify` and `use_doc_unwarping`: https://www.paddleocr.ai/main/en/version3.x/pipeline_usage/PaddleOCR-VL.html
findings.expected_speed_effect: Estimate. On main, about 75 × 5.7 s ≈ 430 s of 2665 s went to orientation. Phase1's once-per-leaf orientation already cuts most of that, leaving about 15–20 calls (~85–115 s). OCR orientation and triage would remove those plus about 100–180 s of out-of-scope leaf time, for about 7–11% of the video-5 wall time. OCR itself costs about 0.1–1 s per frame.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Neutral if fallback is strict. Positive for the out-of-scope rule, because the heading literal comes with a real box from two frames.
findings.risk:
- A wrong rotation (180° on forms with symmetric layout) poisons all later reads.
- An OCR scope gate is exactly what failed in v6.1 (README.md:80). Allow only the 'skip VLM for confirmed out-of-scope' direction, never 'skip VLM because OCR saw nothing'.
- Tesseract or Apple Vision quality on phone frames may be what made the old mode weak; use the bake-off winner instead.
findings.how_to_test:
1. On the saved frames of all 15 video-5 leaves, compare the OCR orientation choice against the VLM orientation recorded in trace.jsonl, measuring agreement.
2. Compare OCR heading against the confirmed `observed_form` for the 5 out-of-scope leaves.
3. Then run the A/B with `deploy/ab_speed_test.sh` and count orientation and triage requests and seconds per leaf with `tools/compare_runs.py`.

findings.title: Add a deterministic check for mixed Latin/Cyrillic letters and for И/Й, Е/Ё differences between readers (flag only, never repair)
findings.claim:
Look-alike Latin letters inside Cyrillic words are a documented failure of specialist OCR models, and models can drop diacritics (РИТЕЙЛ read as РИТЕИЛ is one of the error classes seen here). The check would:
- flag any recognized literal that mixes Latin and Cyrillic letters inside one word;
- flag cases where two readers (VLM vs OCR, or two frames) differ only in И/Й, Е/Ё or Latin/Cyrillic look-alike pairs.
A flagged value is marked as needing a higher-resolution zoom or left as a conflict, with no value repair. This fits the literal-value rule and applies even without any OCR model.
findings.evidence:
- https://habr.com/ru/articles/966846/ (Nov 2025): PaddleOCR-VL 0.9B replaced Cyrillic with look-alike Latin on a clean printed Russian page (МОСКВА → MOCKBA).
- https://arxiv.org/html/2604.12978: Cyrillic script accuracy ranges 94.2% (DeepSeek-OCR-2), 95.5% (LightOnOCR-2), 97.8% (PaddleOCR-VL-1.5), 99.2% (dots.ocr). Latin is the second most frequent output script for Cyrillic input.
- sever/image_fusion.py:148: the fusion method compares Unicode, case and whitespace with presentation equivalences, and the method text reads `no OCR, semantic repair or expected values`.
- Task facts: glyph error РИТЕЙЛ→РИТЕИЛ observed.
findings.expected_speed_effect: Negligible cost (string checks). It may add a few targeted zooms on flagged fields.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Positive. It catches a class of silent literal errors before they reach two-frame confirmation. It is especially needed if any OCR stage is introduced.
findings.risk:
- Legitimate mixed-script values exist (Latin brand names, e.g. 'ООО "X5 Retail"', model codes). Limit the check to letters inside one word, and exempt words that are all Latin.
- Must not change values, per the literal rule.
findings.how_to_test:
1. Run the checker over all recognized literals of the V7 full batch (273 sheets) and the 2026-10-17 runs.
2. Count flags and manually check them against the ground truth.
3. For the 9 known wrong labelled fields, check how many would have been flagged.

findings.title: Serve the OCR model as a second llama-server on the same RTX 5090; prefer a 0.7–1B model so it fits next to the 27B
findings.evidence:
From the repo:
- deploy/sever-model.service:12: `llama-server ... --ctx-size 65536 --parallel 1 ... --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 --image-min-tokens 1024 --image-max-tokens 4096`.
llama.cpp support:
- https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/docs/multimodal.md lists OCR models PaddleOCR-VL #18825, GLM-OCR #19677, Deepseek-OCR #17400, Dots.OCR #17575, HunyuanOCR #21395.
- https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/18825: layout not included; `<__media__>` marker; one image per request.
- https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/17575: merged 2026-04-09.
- https://huggingface.co/blog/ggml-org/using-ocr-models-with-llama-cpp (Apr 10, 2026): PaddleOCR-VL may have degraded performance; most GGUFs default to Q8_0.
- https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/HunyuanOCR/blob/main/docs/llama_cpp.md: llama.cpp ≥ b11103 with DFlash, decode 84.6→167.1 tok/s on Apple M5 Pro; outputs byte-identical on 26 samples.
Blackwell support:
- https://www.paddleocr.ai/v3.5.0/en/version3.x/pipeline_usage/PaddleOCR-VL-NVIDIA-Blackwell.html
- https://www.paddleocr.ai/main/en/version3.x/pipeline_usage/PaddleOCR-VL.html: SGLang and FastDeploy need compute capability 8.0 to below 12.0.
findings.expected_speed_effect: Small OCR models decode fast, so OCR adds about 1–5 s per frame (estimate). A separate server allows OCR of the next frame to overlap with the 27B call, but both share one GPU, so the overlap is partial.
findings.expected_precision_effect: The llama.cpp build of PaddleOCR-VL may be less accurate than the official pipeline, so measure both in the bake-off. Use F16 or Q8, not lower.
findings.risk:
- VRAM pressure with the 27B at 65k context, risking out-of-memory under load.
- A new systemd unit and model hashes must be recorded with results, since deploy/README.md:274-276 says changing these parameters changes the comparison conditions.
- GPU contention can slow the 27B calls.
findings.how_to_test:
1. Start `llama-server -hf ggml-org/<ocr-model>-GGUF:Q8_0 --port 8091 -c 16384` next to the running service.
2. Record `nvidia-smi` peak memory during a video-5 run with both active.
3. Run OCR on 30 saved frames: measure seconds per frame and output tokens.
4. Compare text against the same model in the official PaddleOCR or vLLM pipeline on the same frames (character error rate between the two).

findings.title: Use a small OCR model as the reader for crops the VLM has chosen (literal second reading at low cost), not as an independent confirmation
findings.claim: dots.ocr can transcribe a given bbox (`prompt_grounding_ocr` with `--bbox`). PaddleOCR-VL's native mode is `OCR:` on a cropped block. In the zoom loop, once the VLM has placed a box, the same native-resolution crop could be read by the OCR model (sub-second, estimated). Agreement lets the VLM submit sooner; disagreement only in the И/Й or look-alike sets raises a targeted re-zoom. This needs a business-rule ruling: a second engine on the same crop must not count toward the two-distinct-frames confirmation.
findings.evidence:
- https://huggingface.co/rednote-hilab/dots.ocr: prompt modes include `prompt_grounding_ocr` (parse a given bbox, used with `--bbox`).
- https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/18825: PaddleOCR-VL is trained on the `OCR:` prompt; the author recommends layout detection first, then recognizing regions separately.
- sever/image_reader.py:2-4: "Evidence here is a model's literal transcription of supplied pixels, not an independent OCR observation."
- sever/image_fusion.py:109: "Two distinct image views must support the type and each recognized field."
findings.expected_speed_effect: Unclear. It may shorten agent loops on hard leaves (44–106 calls), or add overhead if disagreements trigger more zooms. Each OCR crop read is estimated well under 1 s for a 0.3–1.5B decoder.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Potentially positive on glyph errors and frame-to-frame conflicts. Negative if the VLM learns to defer to a weaker OCR reading.
findings.risk:
- Business-rule conflict if same-view OCR agreement is treated as corroboration.
- Two models with the same blind spot (e.g. a dropped Й) agreeing can make an error look certain.
findings.how_to_test:
1. Offline: for every zoom crop already saved in the 2026-10-17 video-5 traces (crops are stored with SHA), run PaddleOCR-VL `OCR:` and dots.ocr grounding.
2. Compute exact agreement with the VLM's literal and with ground truth on the labelled fields.
3. Proceed only if OCR-VLM disagreement predicts VLM error (precision ≥0.5).

findings.title: Possible help for missed intervals (the biggest loss): use OCR text fingerprints to split leaves that image registration merged
findings.claim: Segmentation missed 8 of 20 target intervals, the largest accuracy loss. If misses come from merged leaves (two similar sheets that ORB+RANSAC registers as one), a fast line OCR on about 1080 px samples could add a leaf-change signal at negligible VLM cost. The signal is a change in heading text, document number or top-block lines. This is speculative and outside the core OCR-model question. It depends on the failure mode of the misses, which needs checking first.
findings.evidence:
From the repo:
- sever/video.py:405: paper and text orientation is handled separately by `sever.ocr.read_image`, so the video stage already sits next to an OCR entry point.
- sever/ocr.py:286: `_header_line_boxes` already extracts header lines with boxes.
Task facts: 8/20 target intervals missed; thumbnails are sampled at 384 px every 0.5 s (too small for OCR, so this would need a larger sample).
From the web:
- PP-OCRv5 eslav line recognizer at 81.6% line accuracy: https://www.paddleocr.ai/main/en/version3.x/algorithm/PP-OCRv5/PP-OCRv5_multi_languages.html
findings.expected_speed_effect: Adds a few seconds per video (about 145 samples for a 72.8 s clip) of OCR. No change to VLM calls unless new leaves are recovered, which add reads.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Could recover some of the 8 missed target intervals if they are merges; no effect if they are blur or too-short drop-outs.
findings.risk:
- Creates false splits when OCR text flickers between frames of the same sheet. Require a stable new heading over ≥2 samples.
- Extra decode cost at 1080 px sampling.
findings.how_to_test:
1. First classify the 8 missed intervals in the labelled videos as merged with a neighbouring leaf, never stable, or rejected by the quality gate.
2. Only for the 'merged' ones, run PP-OCRv5 eslav on 1080 px samples across the merged span and check whether heading or number text changes at the true boundary.
