research:russian-ocr.topic: Cyrillic/Russian OCR quality of VLMs and OCR models (2025-2026): benchmarks, failure modes, best open models, and llama.cpp + Qwen community reports, applied to the Север pipeline
research:russian-ocr.summary:
No public benchmark matches the task (phone-video frames of Russian shipping forms, field-level literal values). The closest Russian-specific benchmark is MWS Vision Bench from MTS AI: Russian business documents, an OCRBench-v2-style scorer, and a leaderboard updated in 2026. It is the one source here that scores the exact model in use. In the README I downloaded and checked, Qwen3.8-27B scores BELOW both Qwen3.6 open models on plain Russian OCR and JSON key-information extraction (KIE), but well ABOVE them on grounding. Validation img->text is 0.800 vs 0.863 (Qwen3.6-27B) and 0.859 (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B). Validation KIE is 0.812 vs 0.833 and 0.822. Test KIE is 0.807 vs 0.893 and 0.840. Grounding is 0.236 vs 0.071 and 0.099. This, plus the project's own one-clip trial (35B-A3B got the same 9/10 fields in 156.8 s vs 231.2 s), is the strongest evidence-based lever here.

Multilingual benchmarks consistently rank Russian/Cyrillic among the weaker scripts for open models:
- CC-OCR multilingual (F1): Qwen2.5-VL-72B 71.09, Gemini-1.5-Pro 69.99, Qwen3.5-9B 78.97 (ScriptMoE paper, Sept 2026). CC-OCR V2 says Qwen3.5-9B "decreases noticeably" on Russian.
- MDPBench (Mar 2026): open models drop 17.8% on photographed documents and 14.0% on non-Latin scripts. Russian text edit distance on digital-born pages: dots.mocr 0.030, Gemini-3-pro 0.031, PaddleOCR-VL-1.5 0.033, Qwen3-VL-8B 0.039.
- GlotOCR (Apr 2026) and MORE (Jul 2026): HunyuanOCR, dots.ocr/dots.mocr and PaddleOCR-VL are the strongest small open OCR models on Cyrillic.

Documented Cyrillic failure modes:
- (a) Cyrillic letters decoded as visually identical Latin ones. MDPBench names this as the Russian failure, and the ScriptMoE paper attributes the Russian gap to Cyrillic-Latin confusion. Habr (Nov 2025) shows PaddleOCR-VL writing a Russian city name in Latin.
- (b) Rewriting rare or odd strings into more plausible forms. The FaithC4 paper (Sept 2026) reports a 31% rewrite rate on scrambled words for Qwen3-VL-4B. A literal-transcription instruction cuts this by only 30-50%. Content AI reports the same tendency on Russian documents. This matches the project's "соор." -> "корп." error.
- (c) Look-alike substitutions and hallucinated text under seals or stamps (CC-OCR V2).
- (d) Loss of diacritic-like marks (MDPBench, shown for Hindi). Plausibly the same mechanism as Й -> И, but no source quantifies Й/И or ё/е for Russian.

Russian industry evidence on the target forms (Content AI, Habr; synthetic near-ideal documents; PTR = share of documents with every field fully correct):
- УПД: VLM-only 4%, IDP-only 2.67%, hybrid IDP+VLM 36.67%.
- ТОРГ-12: best cloud VLM about 41%, hybrid 80%.
These forms are hard everywhere, which is consistent with 4 hard leaves using 72% of the calls.

llama.cpp community evidence is thin. No Cyrillic-specific llama.cpp issue was found. The only related report is issue #22785 (May 2026, unconfirmed, closed as not planned): Qwen-VL fine-grained OCR got worse in llama-server than in llama-cli on the same build. One informal guide says a BF16 projector reads fine text better.

No source found for Telegram summaries, RuDocs, or a Sber/GigaChat Russian OCR benchmark. MERA Multi has no OCR-specific task, OCRBench v2 is bilingual (English/Chinese), and MMDocBench appears to be English-only.

GLM-5.3-Flash has good grounding on MWS (0.603) but is a 320B MoE and does not fit on the RTX 5090. Cotype Light 3 scores well on MWS (KIE 0.873), but no open weights could be confirmed.

findings.title: A/B Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Qwen3.6-27B against the current Qwen3.8-27B on Russian field reading
findings.claim: Swap the reader model in a controlled A/B before more prompt or agent tuning. On the only Russian business-document benchmark that includes all three models (MWS Vision Bench), Qwen3.8-27B is worse at plain Russian OCR and JSON key-information extraction (KIE) than both Qwen3.6 models. It is better only at grounding. The project's own one-clip trial already showed 35B-A3B (MoE, about 3B active) at the same 9/10 fields with 32% less time. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B is the best first candidate: likely faster per call, with Russian OCR at least as good. Qwen3.6-27B is the accuracy-first candidate: it has the best test KIE (0.893) and fits easily at Q6.
findings.evidence:
MWS Vision Bench README (downloaded and checked: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mts-ai/MWS-Vision-Bench/main/README.md, from https://github.com/mts-ai/MWS-Vision-Bench). Validation rows, 'Overall | img→text | img→markdown | Grounding | KIE (JSON) | VQA':
- Qwen3.6-35B-A3B: '0.694 | 0.859 | 0.784 | 0.099 | 0.822 | 0.904'
- Qwen3.6-27B: '0.691 | 0.863 | 0.768 | 0.071 | 0.833 | 0.919'
- Qwen3.8-27B: '0.688 | 0.800 | 0.758 | 0.236 | 0.812 | 0.836'
Test rows:
- Qwen3.6-27B: '0.692 | 0.861 | 0.753 | 0.062 | 0.893 | 0.889'
- Qwen3.6-35B-A3B: '0.691 | 0.847 | 0.755 | 0.094 | 0.840 | 0.920'
- Qwen3.8-27B: '0.687 | 0.797 | 0.738 | 0.223 | 0.807 | 0.873'
KIE is scored as an F1 of fully matching key-value pairs (https://habr.com/ru/companies/mts_ai/articles/953292/). Qwen3.6-27B model card: CC-OCR 81.2 (27B) and 81.9 (35B-A3B), OCRBench 89.4 and 90.0 (https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B). Project facts: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q6 got 9/10 fields in 156.8 s vs 231.2 s for the 27B dense; deploy/README.md:260 keeps 35B-A3B 'для исторического сравнения'.
findings.expected_speed_effect: 35B-A3B: the project's own trial measured -32% wall time (156.8 vs 231.2 s). With about 3B active parameters, per-call prefill and decode should drop sharply. Model time is 90% of wall and about 11.4k input tokens per call, so this is the main speed lever. The gain could shrink if weaker grounding causes extra zoom rounds. Qwen3.6-27B: about the same speed as Qwen3.8-27B (same dense size).
findings.expected_precision_effect: From MWS deltas only: +0.06 img->text and +0.01 to +0.09 KIE F1 on Russian documents. How much carries over to the 44 labelled fields is unknown. Grounding is 2-3x worse, which may misplace zoom crops (zoom_regions relies on model-chosen rectangles) and could offset the reading gain.
findings.risk: MWS inference settings (precision, thinking on or off, image resolution) are not published, and its documents (contracts, tables, handwriting) differ from phone-video УПД/ТТН frames. UD-Q6_K for 35B-A3B is a 30 GB file (https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MTP-GGUF), which is very tight on 32 GB with mmproj and KV cache. UD-Q5_K_M (27.1 GB) or Qwen3.6-27B Q6_K (21-22.4 GB) is safer. The prompts were tuned on Qwen3.8 and may need re-tuning. Only 44 provisional labels, so a 1-2 field difference is noise. Business rules are unaffected.
findings.how_to_test: Use deploy/ab_speed_test.sh with only MODEL_PATH, MMPROJ_PATH and MODEL_ALIAS swapped. Run video 20260818-5 plus the 3 other labelled videos. Compare against the provisional ground truth: labelled fields correct (baseline 35/44), target types (14/20), fully right sheets (4/8), number of conflict and unreadable fields. Also compare wall time, model requests per leaf (baseline 424 on video 5), and the share of zoom crops whose panel is later cited as evidence (a proxy for grounding quality).

findings.title: Check that the local llama-server Q6 stack is not losing Russian OCR quality (MWS subset plus golden crops)
findings.claim: Measure the production serving stack itself on Russian text. Run the MWS Vision Bench validation img->text (144 items) and KIE (119 items) subsets through the llama-server OpenAI-compatible endpoint, with the production flags (Q6 GGUF, current mmproj, --image-min-tokens 1024 --image-max-tokens 4096, q8_0 KV, thinking off). Compare the result with the published Qwen3.8-27B validation scores (0.800 img->text, 0.812 KIE). Also send about 20 native PNG crops from the labelled set, with known literal text, through llama-server and through a BF16 reference (vLLM or transformers), and compare exact-match rates. Confirm that MMPROJ_PATH is an F16 or BF16 projector, not a Q8 one. A material shortfall points to loss from quantization, the projector, or llama-server preprocessing, not from the model.
findings.evidence: llama.cpp issue #22785 (May 2026, labelled bug-unconfirmed, closed as stale): the server misreads fine OCR detail since b8545 while llama-cli on the same build is fine; the projector is qwen3vl_merger; the maintainer calls the suspected commit unrelated (https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/22785). MindStudio guide (30 Aug 2026, informal): 'with a BF16 projector giving noticeably better image understanding than lower-precision variants'; it also says reading small text degrades more under quantization than scene understanding does (https://www.mindstudio.ai/blog/how-to-run-qwen-vision-models-locally/). The MWS runner supports OpenAI-compatible and vLLM endpoints, and task counts are on https://huggingface.co/datasets/MTSAIR/MWS-Vision-Bench. deploy/sever-model.service:12 shows the production flags, and the mmproj precision is not visible in the repo (paths are in /etc/sever-tsl/local-model.env).
findings.expected_speed_effect: None directly (diagnostic only). If a stack loss is found and fixed, fewer cross-frame conflicts should mean fewer extra frames and joint-review calls.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Unknown until measured. If img->text comes out well below 0.80, recovering it could be the largest single precision gain, since glyph errors (РИТЕИЛ, корп./соор.) are among the known error classes.
findings.risk: The production --image-max-tokens 4096 caps full-page resolution, so full-page img->text will read low compared with the reference for reasons that do not affect the zoom pipeline. Run once with production flags and once with a higher cap to separate the effects. The MWS runner may need a small adapter for llama-server. Benchmark documents differ from the domain. This uses model calls on the server and must not interfere with the production lock.
findings.how_to_test: (1) Record the llama.cpp build hash and the mmproj file name and precision. (2) Run the MWS validation img->text and KIE subsets against 127.0.0.1:8090 and compare with 0.800 and 0.812. (3) Golden crops: take the evidence crops cited for the 35 correct and 9 wrong labelled fields, read each with a fixed literal-transcription prompt on llama-server and on a BF16 reference, and compare exact match per crop. (4) If the gap exceeds a few points, repeat with an F16/BF16 mmproj and with a llama.cpp build at or before b8533.

findings.title: Handle Cyrillic/Latin homoglyphs explicitly: script hint plus mixed-script flag (never rewrite)
findings.claim:
The documented Russian failure of current VLMs is emitting Latin letters that look identical to Cyrillic ones (А/A, В/B, Е/E, К/K, М/M, Н/H, О/O, Р/P, С/C, Т/T, У/Y, Х/X). The fusion comparison key uses only NFKC plus casefold. NFKC does not fold cross-script confusables, so a homoglyph in one frame turns a visually identical reading into a 'conflict', which sends extra frames or joint review. A homoglyph that occurs in both frames gets confirmed as a wrong-codepoint value. Proposals:
- (a) Add one explicit line to INSTRUCTIONS: printed Russian words must be written in Cyrillic, with Latin only where Latin is actually printed (e-mail, Latin brand names).
- (b) Add a deterministic mixed-script detector: a token containing both Latin and Cyrillic letters makes the field unconfirmable, with reason 'mixed Latin/Cyrillic script'. Never transliterate or repair.
- (c) Optionally, a homoglyph-folded key used only to label a conflict as 'script-only', so joint review gets a precise question.
findings.evidence: MDPBench (arXiv 2603.28130, Mar 2026), Russian failure analysis: models 'erroneously decoding Cyrillic characters that are visually identical to Latin letters' (https://arxiv.org/html/2603.28130v1). ScriptMoE paper (arXiv 2609.24058): 'The Russian gap stems from Cyrillic-Latin character confusion' (https://arxiv.org/html/2609.24058). GlotOCR Bench: script hinting helps, 'Cyrillic and Thai also benefit notably, suggesting that character ambiguity is a non-negligible factor' (https://arxiv.org/html/2604.12978). Habr (16 Nov 2025): PaddleOCR-VL wrote a Russian city name in Latin lookalikes (https://habr.com/ru/articles/966846/). OKO project (Qwen3-VL 8B on Russian vehicle documents) has to normalize Latin/Cyrillic before comparison (https://github.com/honeyjostar/oko). Code: sever/image_fusion.py:39-41 `def _literal_comparison(value)` is `" ".join(unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", value).casefold().split())`, which has no confusable handling. sever/image_reader.py INSTRUCTIONS contain no script instruction (grep for 'кирил|latin|латин' finds nothing). The provisional ground-truth values contain no mixed-script tokens (checked locally).
findings.expected_speed_effect: (a) neutral. (b) neutral to slightly slower, since flagged fields go to review. (c) could cut joint-review requests (55 on video 5) if a meaningful share of conflicts is script-only. The count is unknown and must be measured first.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Prevents confirming wrong-codepoint values, which fail exact-match KIE and any downstream 1C or registry lookup. Should reduce spurious conflicts if the hint works (GlotOCR shows script hints help Cyrillic). Size unknown.
findings.risk: Business rule 'values must be literal': (b) only lowers status and never changes a value, so it is safe. (c) must never select or alter a value: agreement still needs two frames with identical codepoints, unless the customer explicitly accepts glyph-identical equivalence. Legitimate mixed tokens (Latin brand names inside Cyrillic org names, e.g. ООО «X5 ...») need an allowance for tokens printed wholly in Latin, applied per token, not per field.
findings.how_to_test: Analysis only, no model calls and no replay into outputs. Scan the stored readings and fusion records of the V7 batch (273 sheets) and the phase1 runs for tokens mixing Latin and Cyrillic letters. Count (i) conflicts whose values differ only by homoglyph substitution and (ii) confirmed values containing Latin homoglyphs. Then A/B the one-line script hint on video 5 and the labelled set, comparing mixed-script token counts, conflict counts and joint-review requests.

findings.title: Use a specialized literal OCR model as a veto on the cited crop (against 'plausible rewriting')
findings.claim: VLMs rewrite rare, odd or perturbed strings into more plausible forms, and prompt instructions reduce this only partly. The current prompt already says 'Read abbreviations character by character...do not expand or repair', yet 'соор.' was still read as the more frequent 'корп.'. Add a small, fast OCR-specialized model (HunyuanOCR-1.5 1B, PaddleOCR-VL-1.5 0.9B or dots.mocr 3B, all strong on Cyrillic) that transcribes only the native crop the VLM cites as evidence for a party-name or address field. Use it strictly as a veto: if the OCR text of that crop does not contain the VLM's raw_value under the same presentation normalization (_field_comparison), that frame does not count toward confirmation. It never supplies or repairs a value, and the evidence is the same sent image.
findings.evidence:
FaithC4 (arXiv 2607.21617, Sept 2026): VLMs 'rewrite it into a more plausible form'. Rewrite rate on scrambled words: Qwen3-VL-4B 31.33%, Qwen3.5-4B 27.35%, traditional OCR 0%. A literal-transcription instruction cut degradation by only about 30-50% for two Qwen models. OCR-then-LLM reached a median F1 of 93.5% vs 68.6% for direct VLM extraction on compliance PDFs (https://www.alphaxiv.org/ru/abs/2607.21617). Content AI (Habr, Feb 2026): VLMs restore text to statistically likely word forms when strict fidelity is required (https://habr.com/ru/companies/contentai/articles/993628/). Cyrillic strength of small OCR models:
- MORE (Jul 2026), Russian overall: HunyuanOCR 99.02, PaddleOCR-VL 98.31, dots.ocr 94.84, Qwen3-VL-2B 96.03 (https://arxiv.org/html/2607.02956).
- GlotOCR, Cyrillic Acc@5: HunyuanOCR 86.8, dots.ocr 86.0, dots.mocr 83.5, Qwen3-VL-8B 79.0, PaddleOCR-VL-1.5 78.0 (https://arxiv.org/html/2604.12978).
Code: sever/image_agent.py:71 already has the 'Read abbreviations character by character' instruction.
findings.expected_speed_effect: Small added cost per checked field. The MTS AI benchmark measured PaddleOCR-VL at 98.7-110.8 pages/min on an A100 (https://habr.com/ru/companies/mts_ai/articles/1065182/), which is negligible next to about 5.7 s per VLM call. Vetoes create more unconfirmed fields, which can add frames or joint-review calls. Net effect: slightly slower.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Higher precision on address and name fields (fewer confidently wrong values like корп./соор.), with some recall loss when the OCR model itself errs on photographed crops. MDPBench reports open models losing 17.8% on photographed documents.
findings.risk: A second model needs VRAM: 26 GB of 32 GB is in use, and a 1B model is about 2-3 GB at BF16 (my estimate). The OCR model can be wrong in the other direction (Latin lookalikes for PaddleOCR-VL per Habr 966846), which would veto correct VLM values. HunyuanOCR is under the Tencent Hunyuan Community License (check its territory terms). Must not be presented as independent corroboration, since it reads the same frame. It is only a veto.
findings.how_to_test: Offline measurement on stored crops, without replaying answers into results. For the 44 labelled fields, run the candidate OCR model on the exact evidence crops already cited and compute: number of the 9 wrong values that would have been vetoed vs number of the 35 correct values falsely vetoed. Adopt only if vetoes of wrong values clearly exceed false vetoes.

findings.title: Validate embedded ИНН with the existing local checksum as a confirmation veto
findings.claim: Address and party fields include the printed ИНН/КПП block, but the native pipeline never applies the checksum code it already has. Before confirming such a value, extract the literal 10- or 12-digit ИНН that follows 'ИНН' and require validate_inn(...)['checksum_valid']. If it fails, mark the field unreadable or conflict with reason 'printed-INN checksum fails'. Never choose between candidate INNs by checksum and never correct digits; that matches the existing rule in inn.py: 'no majority/checksum selection'.
findings.evidence: sever/inn.py:39 `def validate_inn(value)` with the 10-digit checksum at :47 and 12-digit at :51. sever/native_pipeline.py:1045-1046: inn_verification status 'not_performed' with reason 'Native image reading does not yet provide separately corroborated role-bound printed INNs'. ScanReader (Habr): zero-trust check digits for INN, OGRN, BIK and accounts; VLMs produced 'a non-existent INN with a valid format' and tenfold amount errors (https://habr.com/ru/articles/1091144/). Content AI hybrid verification on УПД focused on INN/KPP, dates and sums (https://habr.com/ru/companies/contentai/articles/1021880/).
findings.expected_speed_effect: Negligible compute. Vetoed fields may trigger extra frames or joint review (rare).
findings.expected_precision_effect: Catches digit glyph errors (6/8, 3/8, 1/7) inside confirmed address blocks. These are invisible to two-frame agreement when both frames make the same error. Small but certain gain, with no recall loss on correctly read valid INNs.
findings.risk: A wrong INN that happens to pass the checksum still gets through, so this is a veto, not proof. Rare genuinely misprinted INNs become unconfirmed, which is acceptable and should be flagged. Requires correct association of the ИНН with its own role block; KPP has no checksum.
findings.how_to_test: Analysis only: across V7 batch outputs and the labelled set, count confirmed address and organization values containing 'ИНН' plus 10 or 12 digits, and how many fail validate_inn. Inspect each failure against the cited crop to classify it as a model digit error or a printed anomaly.

findings.title: Targeted one-crop re-read for single-character confusable disagreements (Й/И, Ё/Е, 6/8, О/0)
findings.claim: When two frames disagree on a field by exactly one character in a known confusable class, do not start the general joint review (up to 4 frames, 12 requests, 12 crops). Instead, request one tight native crop of just that word on each disagreeing frame and ask a closed question ('Is the character at position N Й or И?'). The comparison key should keep treating Й≠И and Ё≠Е as different, which NFKC already does and the literal rule requires.
findings.evidence: CC-OCR V2 (arXiv 2605.03903) failure attribution includes 'shape-similar substitution' ('confusion between visually similar characters') and seal patterns that 'induce hallucinated but visually plausible text' (https://arxiv.org/html/2605.03903). MDPBench: for Hindi, models 'keep base characters and drop vowel diacritics' (https://arxiv.org/html/2603.28130v1). This is the closest documented analogue of the project's РИТЕЙЛ -> РИТЕИЛ breve loss. No 2025-2026 source was found that quantifies Й/И or ё/е confusion for Russian (searched). Project facts: joint_review used 55 of 424 requests on video 5, and 'cross-frame conflicts never resolved' is a known error class.
findings.expected_speed_effect: Could replace a 12-request joint review with 1-2 small requests for this conflict class. Share of conflicts affected is unknown.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Focused native-resolution attention on the deciding mark may resolve conflicts that general review leaves unresolved. Low evidence base.
findings.risk: A closed either-or question can bias the model toward one of the two options. Keep a third answer, 'unreadable', and still require two frames to agree. The business rule is unchanged: the confirmed value must be the literal reading of two frames.
findings.how_to_test: From existing V7 and phase1 conflict records, count conflicts whose two values differ by edit distance 1 within {Й/И, Ё/Е, Ш/Щ, 6/8, 3/8, О/0, З/3}. If that is at least 10% of conflicts, implement it and A/B on video 5: joint-review requests, conflicts resolved, labelled-field accuracy.

findings.title: Ask for grounding boxes in the Qwen-native relative 0-1000 integer convention
findings.claim: The zoom tools currently ask for floats in [0,1] (sever/image_agent.py:36, :75). The Qwen3-VL family is reportedly trained on relative 0-1000 integer coordinates, and grounding is the weakest skill of the Qwen3.6 models on MWS (0.062-0.099). Exposing CropRegion as integers 0-1000 and dividing by 1000 server-side may place zoom crops more accurately. Better crops mean fewer wasted crops and requests, and the right glyphs at native resolution.
findings.evidence: QwenLM/Qwen3-VL issue #1616 (15-16 Oct 2025), reply: 'It is recommended to use option A for qwen2.5-vl and to use option B for qwen3-vl', where option B means relative 0-1000 coordinates (https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/issues/1616). The commenter is not identified as a maintainer, and the convention is not verified for Qwen3.6 or 3.8. MWS grounding scores: Qwen3.8-27B 0.236/0.223 vs Qwen3.6-27B 0.071/0.062. MWS asks for absolute 0-2048 coordinates (https://habr.com/ru/companies/mts_ai/articles/953292/, https://github.com/mts-ai/MWS-Vision-Bench). Code: sever/image_agent.py:36 `Coordinate = Annotated[float, Field(ge=0, le=1, ...)]`; :75 'The tool accepts normalized left, top, right, bottom in [0, 1]'.
findings.expected_speed_effect: Potentially fewer zoom_source retries and fewer requests per leaf (up to 8 per frame). Matters most if switching to Qwen3.6, whose grounding is weaker.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Indirect: crops that actually contain the caption and value improve reading and lower the 'outside crop' unreadable rate.
findings.risk: If Qwen3.8 or 3.6 was trained on a different convention (unverified), accuracy could drop, so it must be A/B tested. Changing the tool schema changes the prompt-cache prefix (a one-time cache miss).
findings.how_to_test: A/B on video 5 with the phase1 per-call timing log: zoom crops per frame, share of returned crops cited as evidence, requests per leaf, and labelled-field accuracy, for [0,1] floats vs 0-1000 integers, on each candidate model.

findings.title: Set expectations and consider an 'OCR draft + VLM verify' path for УПД/ТОРГ-12
findings.claim: Russian industry results show field-perfect УПД extraction is rare for every approach, and ТОРГ-12 is hard for VLM-only extraction. Hybrid pipelines where a classic or OCR engine supplies a draft with text and boxes and the VLM verifies it against the image do much better. For the 4 hard leaves (72% of calls and 74% of time), a single fast full-frame OCR pass could give the VLM candidate caption and value lines with coordinates, replacing several exploratory zoom rounds. Final values must still be read and cited from sent crops.
findings.evidence: Content AI (Habr): PTR (whole document correct) for УПД: ContentCapture only 2.67%, VLM only 4%, hybrid best 36.67% (LLaMA-4), 23.3% with local Qwen2.5-VL-7B. ТОРГ-12: no fully correct documents with IDP only, about 41% for the best cloud VLM, hybrid 80% (LLaMA-4) and 51% (local Mistral). These are synthetic, near-ideal documents (https://habr.com/ru/companies/contentai/articles/1021880/). Content AI also reports that VLMs mis-split lines and columns and confuse nearby number and date fields (https://habr.com/ru/companies/contentai/articles/993628/). FaithC4: OCR-then-LLM 93.5% vs 68.6% median F1 for direct VLM extraction (https://www.alphaxiv.org/ru/abs/2607.21617).
findings.expected_speed_effect: Potentially large on hard leaves, with fewer exploratory zoom requests (44-106 calls per hard leaf today). Unmeasured.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Possibly better role and boundary handling (address block versus neighbouring role). There is a risk of anchoring on OCR errors.
findings.risk: Anchoring: the VLM may accept OCR typos, so OCR text must be marked as unverified hints and values must be re-read from the crops. Business rules: OCR text must not become the value or the evidence. The evidence is synthetic documents, not phone video. Large change, so it should come after the model A/B.
findings.how_to_test: Prototype on the 4 hard leaves of video 5 only. Run one OCR pass per primary frame, inject 'candidate lines with boxes' into the first agent message, and compare requests per leaf, wall time, conflicts and labelled-field accuracy against phase1.

research:engines.topic: Serving engines and settings for a 27B-class VLM (Qwen3.8-27B) on one RTX 5090: llama.cpp vs vLLM/SGLang/TensorRT-LLM/ExLlamaV3, MTP, MoE, KV quantization, concurrency
research:engines.summary:
Decode is where the time goes. The 2026-10-17 server A/B on phase1-speed (analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md) logged 5.34 s per call. That splits into about 1.45 s of prefill (3,403 new tokens at 2,340 tok/s), 3.66 s of decode (222 tokens at 61 tok/s, 69% of model time) and about 0.23 s of other time. Our 61 tok/s matches a community RTX 5090 baseline for Qwen3.8-27B Q6_K (61.9 tok/s).

Largest per-call speedup without changing the weights: turn on MTP self-speculative decoding (--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 2) in the llama.cpp v0.6.0 already deployed.
- Qwen3.8-27B ships a trained MTP head.
- On RTX 5090s, Q6_K went from 61.9 to 130 tok/s at n-max 2 (+110%). Other 5090 quants showed +75–137%.
- Single-GPU CUDA prefill drops only about 3%. The prompt cache still works with MTP upstream. Speculative decoding after image input was fixed in v0.4.1 (#28715).
- Expected per-call time is about 3.4–4.0 s (1.35–1.55x), assuming our Cyrillic JSON and image turns keep acceptance at 0.5–0.8. One vision turn elsewhere measured 0.62.
- Cost: about 2 GB more VRAM. The deployed GGUF must contain the MTP tensors.

Largest per-call speedup overall: switch to the MoE Qwen3.6-35B-A3B.
- On an RTX PRO 6000 at Q8_0, it decoded at 193 tok/s against 45.8 for the 27B dense (4.2x).
- On RTX 5090 at Q4, MoE models of this class prefill 2.3–3.1x faster.
- Derived per-call time is about 1.7–2.0 s (2.7–3.1x), but MTP adds only 1.17x on the MoE.
- Published OCR scores are close: CC-OCR 81.9 vs 81.2 for Qwen3.6-27B; OmniDocBench 89.9 vs 91.1 for Qwen3.8-27B. A broad vision suite scores it lower (64.8 vs 69.5).
- The earlier in-house one-clip trial got the same 9/10 fields but only 1.47x end to end. It needs a full labelled A/B before adoption.

NVFP4 (llama.cpp or vLLM):
- Gives about +60% prefill and +20% decode over Q6_K.
- Community KLD reports put NVFP4 below Q6_K for Qwen3.6-27B. That is a poor trade for literal glyph-level OCR unless an A/B proves otherwise.

FP8 27B (about 29 GB) does not fit a 32 GB card alongside the vision tower and KV cache.

vLLM 0.31 with nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 works on an RTX 5090.
- Single-stream decode: 65–86 tok/s.
- Prefill is much faster: TTFT 134 ms at about 2k tokens.
- It scales far better with concurrency (all 5090 measurements):
  - 78 to 137 to 267 tok/s aggregate at 1, 2 and 4 streams.
  - With MTP at 4 streams: 413 vs 261 tok/s.
  - At 32 streams: 936 vs 369 tok/s for llama.cpp.
- Costs:
  - W4A4 precision risk.
  - Prefix caching for hybrid Gated DeltaNet models is experimental ("align" mode, roughly 784-token blocks). Combined with MTP, cache hits fell to 0% unless the state is bf16 and prompts are block-aligned.
  - Outputs are not batch-invariant.

Other engines:
- TensorRT-LLM 1.3.0rc29 runs the model (73 tok/s single stream, 1,361 tok/s at 32 streams). KV block reuse is unsupported for this architecture, and its mm-encoder flag crashes, so it is a poor fit for our cache-heavy agent loop.
- SGLang's 5090 recipe relies on DFlash2. Its 206 tok/s figure is the project's own claim, and one card says DFlash2 does not support greedy decoding, which conflicts with our temperature 0.
- ExLlamaV3 1.4.2 has an EXL3 quant with MTP and the vision tower, but no 5090 or vision measurements.

Concurrency, 2–4 streams:
- llama.cpp: no direct 2–4 stream measurement found for this model. Derived estimate: aggregate model throughput about 1.3–1.5x at 2 streams and 1.6–2.0x at 4.
- llama.cpp with MTP: one tester reports the MTP gain is gone by 4 streams, and a --parallel 2 single-stream baseline reads about 20% low.
- vLLM: 1.76x at 2 and 3.4x at 4 (measured, short prompts). Derived for our mix: about 3–6x at 4 streams with MTP.
- Video wall time is capped by the slowest leaf (301 s of 1,134 s on phase1). Realistic wall gains: about 1.4x at 2 streams and about 2x at 4 on llama.cpp; about 2.5–3x at 4 on vLLM.

Recommended order:
1. MTP at --parallel 1 (S effort).
2. Two-slot llama.cpp with id_slot pinning (S/M).
3. MoE accuracy A/B (M).
4. vLLM NVFP4 trial only if throughput at 4+ streams becomes the goal (L).

The KV cache is small for this hybrid model: 16 of 64 layers, 64 KiB per token in f16, 4 GiB at 65k. Moving q8_0 to f16 is cheap insurance (q8_0 KL about 0.024) but not a speed lever.

findings.title: Enable MTP self-speculative decoding on the existing llama.cpp v0.6.0 + Qwen3.8-27B Q6 (largest per-call lever without changing weights)
findings.claim: Decode is 69% of model time per call: 222 output tokens at 61 tok/s is about 3.66 s of the 5.34 s per call. Qwen3.8-27B has a trained MTP head, and llama.cpp has run MTP since PR #22673 (merged 2026-05-16); the server's v0.6.0 includes it. Add `--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 2` (then try 3) and keep `--parallel 1`. Community RTX 5090 rows for this exact model at Q6_K: 61.9 to 130.0 tok/s, acceptance 0.52–0.95. Even at a conservative 1.6–2.1x on our Cyrillic JSON and image turns, decode drops to about 1.7–2.3 s per call. Prefill rises about 3% on a single CUDA GPU. Derived total: about 3.4–4.0 s per call (1.35–1.55x), and the phase1 video-5 run would fall from about 1,134 s to roughly 750–850 s. Greedy verification keeps the target model's output in principle, so the business rules (literal values, two-frame agreement) do not change.
findings.evidence:

findings.expected_speed_effect: Decode 1.6–2.1x (61 to about 100–130 tok/s); per call 5.34 s to about 3.4–4.0 s (1.35–1.55x); phase1 video-5 wall about 1,134 s to about 750–850 s (derived).
findings.expected_precision_effect: Neutral by design: greedy verification accepts only tokens the target model would choose. Batched verification is not bit-exact, so some field strings may differ by run; one report mentions a greedy-vs-baseline divergence in the shared verify path on CDNA.
findings.risk:
- The deployed UD-Q6 GGUF may lack MTP tensors; then the server errors or acceptance is about 0, and the MTP GGUF variant must be fetched.

findings.title: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (MoE) gives the largest raw per-call speedup but needs a labelled accuracy A/B
findings.claim: Per-token decode for a 3B-active MoE is roughly 4x the 27B dense on Blackwell-class bandwidth, and prefill is 2.3–3.1x faster. With 222 output and 3.4k new input tokens, the derived per-call time is about 1.7–2.0 s vs 5.34 s (2.7–3.1x). MTP adds little on the MoE (1.17x), so its gain comes from the architecture alone. Published document and OCR scores are close to the 27B models; the broader Roboflow vision suite is lower. The in-house one-clip trial (same 9/10 fields, 156.8 s vs 231.2 s) already showed a smaller end-to-end gain than per-call math predicts. Re-run it on phase1-speed with the per-call timing log to see whether call count or image encoding absorbs the gain.

findings.title: Concurrency 2–4 on llama.cpp: modest gain, poor fit with MTP, and wall time is capped by the slowest leaf
findings.claim:
Decode is memory-bound, so batching 2–4 sequences raises aggregate tok/s. Prefill (27% of call time) is compute-bound and does not batch for free. llama.cpp's multi-slot scaling is much weaker than vLLM's (369 vs 936 tok/s at 32 streams on a 5090). For MTP, one tester reports 'the spec advantage is gone by 4 concurrent streams' and that a --parallel 2 baseline reads about 20% low per stream. Each slot also adds recurrent state: about 150 MiB per row, about 600 MiB per slot with MTP n-max 3.

Derived estimate for our mix without MTP: about 1.3–1.5x aggregate model throughput at 2 slots and 1.6–2.0x at 4. Wall time is bounded below by the longest leaf (page-0015, 301 s of the 1,134 s phase1 run), slowed further by the per-stream decode drop. Realistic wall: about 1.4x at 2 leaves and about 1.8–2.2x at 4.

MTP at --parallel 1 gives a similar gain (about 1.45x) at lower risk and keeps calls deterministic per slot. Test MTP@np1, then no-MTP@np2, then MTP@np2. When using slots, pin each leaf worker to its own slot (id_slot) so slot reassignment does not discard hybrid-model checkpoints.
findings.evidence:
Repo:
- sever/cli.py:29-30 '# Match llama-server --parallel; 1 keeps leaves strictly sequential. leaf_concurrency=int(os.getenv("HARNESS_LEAF_CONCURRENCY","1"))'
- analysis/ab-speed-20261017/comparison.md: page-0015 301.33 s, wall 1,134.49 s.

Web sources:
- 'RTX 5090 | llama.cpp | 32 | 369'; 'RTX 5090 | vLLM | 32 | 936'; llama.cpp single stream 77.8. https://computingforgeeks.com/?p=171658
- 'a `--parallel 2` BASELINE reads ~20% low'; 'the spec advantage is gone by 4 concurrent streams'. https://github.com/sudoingX/qwen38-mtp
- 'RS buffer growing from 598.5 MiB at 1 slot to 2394.0 MiB at 4 slots'. https://github.com/janhq/jan/pull/9186
- Slot reassignment 'collapsed' reuse and discarded 15 checkpoints at 149.626 MiB each. https://particula.tech/blog/prompt-reprocessing-swa-hybrid-models-kv-cache
findings.expected_speed_effect: Without MTP: about 1.3–1.5x model throughput at 2 slots, about 1.6–2.0x at 4. Video wall about 1.4x at 2 leaves, about 1.8–2.2x at 4 (derived). MTP's own gain mostly vanishes by 4 slots.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Neutral in expectation, but outputs are not batch-invariant: the same frame can read differently depending on what shares the batch. That adds noise to the two-frame agreement rule.
findings.risk:
- Context per slot: --ctx-size 65536 is shared via the unified KV, so check the maximum prompt size per call.
- Host RAM for checkpoints grows with slots (raise --cache-ram above the default 8192 MiB).
- Image encoding in one slot may stall decode in the others (not verified).
- No direct 2–4 stream measurement exists for this model.
findings.how_to_test:
1. Run llama-batched-bench on the server model with -npl 1,2,4 and a prompt of about 3.4k tokens plus 222 generated tokens, to get S_TG and S_PP per stream count.
2. Then run video 5 with HARNESS_LEAF_CONCURRENCY=2 and --parallel 2 (each worker sends id_slot), with and without MTP.
3. Compare wall time, sum of per-call model time, per-stream predicted_per_second, cache_n, and the 22-label accuracy.

findings.title: vLLM 0.31 + nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 (+MTP) is the throughput option for 4+ concurrent streams, not a per-call precision-safe swap
findings.claim:
vLLM's measured RTX 5090 numbers:
- Single-stream decode: 65.6–85.7 tok/s.
- TTFT 134 ms at about 2k tokens and 8.52 s at 61.8k, i.e. roughly 7–15k tok/s prefill vs our 2,340.
- Aggregate: 137 tok/s at 2 streams and 267 at 4 (1.76x and 3.4x); with MTP at 4 streams, 413 vs 261 tok/s.

Derived for our call shape: about 2.7–4.4 s per call single-stream (1.2–2.0x). At 4 streams, about 3–6x aggregate model throughput, depending on whether prefix caching survives.

Costs:
- NVFP4 is W4A4 (activations quantized too). NVIDIA's own card shows small drops (MMMU-Pro 75.14 to 74.86, IFBench 80.07 to 78.93) and no OCR evaluation.
- Mamba/GDN prefix caching is 'experimental' in 'align' mode, with large blocks.
- MTP combined with hybrid prefix caching gave 0% hits by default; bf16 state plus block-aligned prompts recovered 72%.
- FP8 27B (about 29 GB) does not fit 32 GB alongside the vision tower and KV.
- Multimodal prefix caching itself is supported: the block hash includes the image hash.
findings.evidence:
- Friendli card, 2026-08-14, vLLM 0.27.1: 'Decode @ conc 1 (OSL 256) ... 80.6 tok/s'; '2 | 73.1 | 137'; '4 | 71.0 | 267'; 'TTFT p50 @ ~1,967 tok 134 ms'; '@ ~62k 8.52 s'; vision tower kept in BF16. https://friendli.ai/models/gittensor-model-hub/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4
- 'RTX 5090 | vLLM with MTP | 413' vs 'without MTP | 261' (4 concurrent). https://computingforgeeks.com/?p=171658
- NVIDIA card: 'MMMU-Pro 75.14 → 74.86'; MLP NVFP4, attention FP8. https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4
- vLLM recipe: 'Prefix caching for Mamba is listed as experimental in "align" mode'; FP8 needs 'a single 40 GB GPU'. https://recipes.vllm.ai/Qwen/Qwen3.5-27B
- 'MTP K=2, default state | 1449 | 0%'; 'bf16 state + block-aligned ... 72%'; '784 tokens' block. https://friendli.ai/models/Twu31/Qwen3.8-27B-AWQ-INT4-ZhChat-MTP
- vLLM design doc: multimodal blocks carry '<image hash>' in the extra hashes. https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/design/prefix_caching/
findings.expected_speed_effect: Single stream 1.2–2.0x per call. At 4 streams, about 3–6x aggregate model throughput and about 2.5–3x video wall (critical-path bound). Derived; the cited runs were text-only and short-prompt.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Risk of degradation from W4A4 NVFP4 on fine Cyrillic glyphs (unmeasured for OCR). Not batch-invariant at temperature 0.
findings.risk:
- New server stack: FlashInfer JIT took 718 s on first start, plus CUDA-graph bugs on 5090 recipes (vLLM #40807/#40831 cited by a community repo).
- Different tool-call parser (qwen3_coder) and chat template behaviour.
- Prefix-cache misses on hybrid models.
- Must keep llama.cpp as the fallback, and the model fingerprint changes.
findings.how_to_test:
1. In a separate port or session window, serve nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 with vLLM 0.31 (--enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16, speculative-config mtp n=1..3).
2. Replay video-5 phase1 calls at concurrency 1 and 4.
3. Log TTFT, decode tok/s, prefix-cache hit rate (vLLM metrics), the 22/44-label accuracy, and diffs vs llama.cpp Q6.

findings.title: Do not switch to NVFP4 GGUF in llama.cpp for this OCR task without an A/B; the speed gain is mostly prefill
findings.claim: llama.cpp has run NVFP4 natively on Blackwell since b8967. On an RTX 5090 with Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4 it prefills at about 5,000 tok/s at 8k depth (vs our measured 2,340) and decodes at 72–74 tok/s (vs 61 for Q6). Derived per call: about 4.0 s, or about 2.9–3.2 s with MTP. Community reports, however, say NVFP4 GGUFs have 'much higher KLD than Q6_K', and one perplexity comparison put NVFP4 at 7.2 vs 6.6 for Q8_K_XL. For literal glyph reading, MTP on Q6 delivers most of the gain without that loss.
findings.evidence:
- 'pp2048 @ d8192 | 3117.80 | 5005.44'; 'tg512 @ d8192 | 71.65 | 71.61'. https://reddit.sentinel-team.org/posts/1syxckc/snapshots/2026-05-02T03%3A06%3A21.60641Z
- 'Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4-MTP 5,100 pp / 79.4 tg' vs 'AD-Q4_K_M 3,830 / 74.2'. https://atomic.chat/blog/guides/best-local-llms-for-rtx-5090
- 'NVFP4 and AWQ variants having much higher KLD than Q6_K quants'. https://reddit.sentinel-team.org/posts/1u1r8yy/snapshots/2026-06-13T02%3A56%3A06.64152Z
- 'one NVFP4 conversion dropped MTP speculative decoding (0% draft acceptance)'; quality 'unsettled'. https://insiderllm.com/guides/fp4-inference-llamacpp-nvfp4-mxfp4/
- 5090 NVFP4 MTP row: '62.7 → 108.7 (3)'. https://github.com/sudoingX/qwen38-mtp
findings.expected_speed_effect: Prefill about 2x and decode about 1.2x; per call about 1.3x, or about 1.7–1.8x combined with MTP (derived).
findings.expected_precision_effect: Likely negative (higher KLD than Q6_K per community reports; no OCR data).
findings.risk: Silent glyph-level regressions that the 44 provisional labels may not detect; community conversions vary in quality.
findings.how_to_test:
1. Run llama-perplexity --kl-divergence of an NVFP4 GGUF against Q6_K logits on the stored INSTRUCTIONS plus the text of actual answers.
2. Run a video-5 and 4-video labelled A/B.

findings.title: KV cache: keep it small but drop q8_0 to f16 (or shrink ctx); it is cheap for this hybrid model and not a speed lever
findings.claim: In Qwen3.8-27B, only 16 of 64 layers are full attention (4 KV heads × 256 dim), so f16 KV costs 64 KiB per token: 4 GiB at 65,536 ctx vs about 2.1 GiB for q8_0. q8_0 is near-lossless on Qwen3.6-27B (KL 0.024 vs f16) but not zero, and one practitioner reports quantized K breaking JSON tool calls. Switching to f16 costs about 1.9 GiB. Combined with MTP's about 2 GB on the 26.7 GB already used, that is tight on 32.6 GB, so either keep q8_0 with MTP, or use f16 with --ctx-size 32768 after confirming the largest prompt fits. Speed impact is within about 5% either way.
findings.evidence:
- deploy/sever-model.service:12 '--ctx-size 65536 ... --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0'
- analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md: 'GPU memory (min–max) | 26,180–26,683 MiB'
- Architecture: '16-block layout of three Gated DeltaNet ... followed by one Gated Attention block'; 'Gated Attention: 24 Q heads, 4 KV heads, head dim 256'. https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B
- 'Qwen 3.6 27B, q8_0: 0.024'. https://localbench.substack.com/p/kv-cache-quantization-benchmark
- 'quantizing k leads to broken json on tool calls'. https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48545335
- Jan measured 'KV cache stays at 512 MiB' (consistent with 64 KiB/token at 8k). https://github.com/janhq/jan/pull/9186
findings.expected_speed_effect: About 0 to +5% (flash attention with quantized KV is roughly at parity); no meaningful per-call change.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Small positive: removes a measured (if small) distribution shift on long multi-image prompts.
findings.risk: VRAM headroom once MTP is added; reducing ctx could truncate the largest joint-review prompts (check the maximum input tokens per call in the timing log first).
findings.how_to_test:
1. From the phase1 timing log, take the maximum prompt_n plus cache_n per call.
2. Run llama-perplexity --kl-divergence with q8_0 vs f16 KV on a recorded 11k-token multimodal prompt text.
3. Run video-5 accuracy with both settings and check VRAM via nvidia-smi.

findings.title: Verify hybrid-model prompt-cache checkpoints are not forcing re-prefill (default --checkpoint-min-step 8192, --no-reasoning-preserve)
findings.claim: For Gated DeltaNet hybrids, llama.cpp cannot roll the recurrent state back to an arbitrary point; it relies on context checkpoints. When no checkpoint covers the divergence point it silently re-processes the whole prompt; the message is logged only at -lv 4. Our calls average 3,403 new tokens (68% cache), which is about one native crop, so the cache mostly works; but any fraction of full re-prefills (about 10.6k tokens, about 4.5 s) is pure waste. The service sets --no-reasoning-preserve while thinking is off. Particula reports that re-rendering prior turns (for example stripping empty think blocks) changes the prefix. Particula also describes -cms as an eviction floor that can drop checkpoints spaced closer than 8192 tokens. Check both before tuning.
findings.evidence:
- deploy/sever-model.service:12 '--chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}' --no-reasoning-preserve'
- analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md:23 '68% of input tokens came from the prefix cache'
- '-cms, --checkpoint-min-step: default 8192 ... acts as an eviction floor'; 'The message is logged at trace level (verbosity 4)'; 'Even -rea off still churns context'. https://particula.tech/blog/prompt-reprocessing-swa-hybrid-models-kv-cache
- '-ctxcp ... (default: 32)'; '-cms ... (default: 8192, 0 = no minimum)'; '-cram ... (default: 8192 ...)'. https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/server/README.md
findings.expected_speed_effect: 0 to about 10% per call, depending on how many calls currently fall back to full prefill (unknown).
findings.expected_precision_effect: None (cache reuse is exact for the matched prefix).
findings.risk: Lower -cms raises host-RAM checkpoint use (about 150 MiB each). Changing reasoning-preserve may alter the rendered prompt and hence outputs, so A/B it.
findings.how_to_test:
1. Run one video-5 pass with -lv 4 and grep 'forcing full prompt re-processing'.
2. Histogram per-call prompt_n (new tokens) from the timing log; calls near the full prompt length indicate misses.
3. Retry with -cms 1024 and/or --reasoning-preserve and compare cache_n and prefill seconds.

findings.title: SGLang, TensorRT-LLM and ExLlamaV3 are not better fits today
findings.claim: TensorRT-LLM 1.3.0rc29 runs Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 on a 5090 (73 tok/s single stream, 1,361 tok/s at 32 streams). Its supported-models table lists KV block reuse as unsupported for this architecture, so there is no prefix caching for our agent loop that is 68% cached, and its disable_mm_encoder option crashed. SGLang's single-5090 Qwen3.8-27B recipe uses NVFP4 plus DFlash2: 206.1 tok/s, project-reported. One DFlash2 card states greedy decoding is unsupported, which conflicts with temperature 0, and an NVFP4 output-repetition issue is open. ExLlamaV3 1.4.2 has an 8.0bpw EXL3 with MTP (1.87x) and the BF16 vision tower, but it was tested only on a 4070+3090 with no visual-quality evaluation.
findings.evidence:
- 'enable_block_reuse: false, because the supported-models table lists KV cache reuse as unsupported for this architecture'; 'disable_mm_encoder ... AttributeError'. https://computingforgeeks.com/tensorrt-llm-vs-vllm/
- 'One RTX 5090 for the 206.1 tokens/s figure ... project-reported'; 'NVFP4 compressed-tensors output repetition issue (sgl-project/sglang #34895)'. https://runtimewire.com/article/sglang-qwen3-8-27b-nvfp4-dflash2-cookbook
- 'Greedy decoding is unsupported for DFlash2'. https://friendli.ai/models/dfischermittwald/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4-DFlash2
- EXL3: 'exllamav3 1.4.2', 'median end-to-end time dropped from 109.87 s to 58.72 s (1.87×)', 'no visual-quality evaluation'. https://huggingface.co/billmccartney/Qwen3.8-27B-exl3
findings.expected_speed_effect: Not quantifiable for our workload; TensorRT-LLM would lose prefix-cache reuse (about +7k prefill tokens per call).
findings.expected_precision_effect: Unknown; DFlash2 sampling-only would break temperature-0 determinism.
findings.risk: Engine immaturity for hybrid VLMs on sm_120, plus migration cost.
findings.how_to_test: Only if vLLM is adopted and still insufficient: run the same replay harness at concurrency 1 and 4, with the same accuracy gate.
