research:techniques.topic: Phone-video OCR of Russian printed forms with a local VLM: cutting model calls and improving literal accuracy (image token budgets, agentic vs one-shot zoom, rectification, frame choice, MTP, prefix caching on hybrid Qwen3.x, grammar cost) for the Север phase1-speed pipeline on one RTX 5090 with llama.cpp
research:techniques.summary:
Main finding: each model call is limited by how fast it generates output, not by how fast it reads input. In the phase1-speed run on video 5 (analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md), generation took 688 s of 1004 s model time (69%) at 61 tok/s. Prefill took 273 s at 2,340 tok/s. So the biggest per-call gains come from faster decoding.

1. Faster decoding (largest lever)
- Turn on MTP speculative decoding with `--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 2` and keep `--parallel 1`. It has been in mainline llama.cpp since PR #22673 (merged 2026-05-16) and is stated to work with vision input. Unsloth says its Qwen3.8-27B GGUFs include MTP.
- RTX 5090 users report Qwen3.8-27B Q6_K_XL at about 52–56 tok/s without MTP and about 92 tok/s with vision plus MTP.
- Expected effect: about 20–25% less model time, provided prefill does not slow down. One user on a 3090 saw prefill halve with MTP, so measure it.
- Alternative: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, an MoE model with 3B active parameters. It decodes at about 180 tok/s on a 5090. Its document scores are close: OmniDocBench1.5 89.9 vs 91.1 for Qwen3.8-27B; CC-OCR 81.9. It could cut model time by 40% or more, but its accuracy on your labelled fields must be checked, and the 27B was the model you chose.

2. Two things that break prompt caching. Qwen3.8-27B mixes Gated DeltaNet layers with full attention, so llama.cpp can reuse a cached prompt only from a saved checkpoint. Everything after the first changed token is processed again.
- Changing the tool list mid-run. The Qwen3.8 chat template writes the tools block first in the system message. When `prepare_zoom` drops the zoom tools (image_agent.py:256-265, image_conflicts.py:461-465), the prompt changes about 10 tokens in. The whole request is then processed again: tools, instructions, context image and every crop. Fix: keep the tool list identical on every request and rely on the decline message `zoom_source` already returns.
- Checkpoint spacing. Checkpoints are saved every 8192 tokens by default (`--checkpoint-min-step`). The prefix every frame shares (tools, instructions, prompt) is probably shorter than that, so each new frame likely re-processes it. Try `--checkpoint-min-step 1024 --ctx-checkpoints 64`, keep `--cache-ram` on, and check `cache_n` on the first request of each run.

3. Image sizes. A Qwen3.x image token covers 32×32 px (patch 16, merge 2). `--image-min-tokens 1024` makes llama.cpp enlarge every image under about 1.05 MP. Today the 576×1024 context is shrunk on our side, then enlarged by the server to about 768×1376. Small native crops are enlarged too, which contradicts the "without magnification" wording in ZOOM_INSTRUCTIONS and README.md:213. Let the client set the sizes:

| Image | Size | Tokens |
|---|---|---|
| Context (from native pixels) | 768×1376 | 1032 |
| Full-frame one-shot (2160×3840 source) | 1536×2720 | 4080 |
| Orientation, per rotation | 288×512 | 144 |
| Crops | native | 256 minimum |

Server settings to A/B: `--image-min-tokens 256` (Qwen3-VL's README example uses 256–1280) and `--image-max-tokens 4096`.

4. Fewer calls
- Save the ORB+RANSAC homography that video.py:163 already computes. Use it to map frame 1's selected regions onto later frames of the same sheet, and send those crops in the first request. This removes the context-then-zoom round trip: about one fewer request (about 5.3 s) per extra frame read.
- Merge orientation into triage, or send the four rotations at 144 tokens each.
- Use whole numbers on the 0–1000 grid for zoom coordinates, and cap `max_tokens` on each step.
- A 2026 study found that agents make unnecessary visual tool calls 36–87% of the time.

5. Accuracy
- Rectify or deskew the context and crops with a 4-corner homography, record the warp matrix, and keep the native crop. Use UVDoc or ForCenNet only for curled sheets. TeleOCR (Sep 2026) reports that removing geometric distortion substantially improves two-stage parsing. Qwen3-VL-8B scores 72.4 on clean pages and 62.7 on real photographed ones.
- Pick the sharpest frames for each field region, not for the whole frame. quality.py:63 itself notes that sharp page edges can hide blurred text.
- Avoid multi-frame super-resolution or fusion. A fused image is not one of the frames actually sent, which breaks the two-distinct-source-frames rule, and generative SR can invent glyphs. MME-VideoOCR also shows models are weak at combining information across frames, so keep cross-frame logic in code.

6. Constrained JSON is not the bottleneck. Constrained decoding runs at 61 tok/s, about the speed reported for unconstrained decoding on the same GPU and quant. Keep the schema unambiguous (`extra=forbid`), but do not switch to llguidance for speed.

Caveats
- All numbers are from the sources listed or from your one A/B run. Nothing was measured here.
- PaddleOCR helpers would conflict with the README's "no separate classifier / no Tesseract" design statement.
- MTP currently needs `--parallel 1`, so it rules out leaf concurrency. A/B it against `--parallel 2 --kv-unified`.

findings.title: Enable MTP speculative decoding on the existing Qwen3.8-27B GGUF
findings.claim: Add `--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 2` to llama-server and keep `--parallel 1`. Generation is 69% of model time at 61 tok/s. MTP in mainline llama.cpp verifies drafted tokens with the target model, so at temperature 0 the output should be the same apart from batch-size numerics. RTX 5090 users report about 92 tok/s for Qwen3.8-27B Q6 with vision and MTP, against about 52–56 without. Raising n-max beyond 2 lowered throughput in a user sweep.
findings.evidence: analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md:22-23 "prefill 639,726 new input tokens in 273 s (2,340 tok/s); generation 41,696 tokens in 688 s (61 tok/s) = 69% of model time"; deploy/sever-model.service:12 ExecStart has no --spec-type; https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/22673 (merged 2026-05-16): "MTP is compatible with Vision input", RTX 5090 27B q4_0 63.72 -> 105.47 tok/s, acceptance 0.797; prefill warning "Prompt processing (PP) speed typically takes a negative hit"; https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF/discussions/14: Q6_K_XL no vision/MTP ~52-56 tok/s, vision+MTP ~92 tok/s; n-max 1 1.47x, n-max 2 1.51x, n-max 6 worse; https://unsloth.ai/docs/models/qwen3.8.md: "Unsloth quants have MTP enabled", 1-2 GB extra memory; llama.cpp server README --spec-type list includes draft-mtp.
findings.expected_speed_effect: Decode about 61 -> 85-95 tok/s. Generation time on video 5 would drop from 688 s to about 440-490 s, so model time from about 1004 s to about 760-800 s (-20-25%), if prefill is unchanged. If prefill halves, as one 3090 user saw (1315 -> 665 tok/s), most of the gain is lost.
findings.expected_precision_effect: None expected at temperature 0. Rare token flips are possible because llama.cpp logits are not bit-identical across batch sizes.
findings.risk:
- MTP needs n_parallel=1, so it excludes HARNESS_LEAF_CONCURRENCY>1.
- It adds 1-2.5 GB VRAM (26.7 GB in use today -> about 29 of 32 GB).
- An MTP+vision slot-corruption bug (#22867) was closed in May 2026; confirm the v0.6.0 build has the fix.
- The deployed GGUF must contain the MTP layer.
- Changing server flags changes the batch fingerprint.
findings.how_to_test:
1. On the idle server, confirm `llama-server --help` lists draft-mtp and the startup log shows an MTP/nextn layer loaded.
2. Restart sever-model with the MTP flags.
3. Rerun phase1-speed on 20260818-5_132107.mp4; the baseline is 1134 s wall, 188 requests, 1004 s model.
4. With tools/compare_runs.py, compare server_timings predicted_n/predicted_ms (tok/s), prompt_n/prompt_ms (prefill tok/s), total model time and the 22 labelled fields.
5. Record draft acceptance from the server log.

findings.title: Keep the tool list constant within a run so the cache survives
findings.claim: `prepare_zoom` returns None after 8 crops or at request 7. That removes zoom_source and zoom_regions from the tools sent in that request. The Qwen3.8 chat template writes `<|im_start|>system\n# Tools ... <tools>` before the system text. So the prompt changes about 10 tokens in, and the request re-processes tools, about 9k characters of instructions, the context image and all crops. On a hybrid DeltaNet model there is no checkpoint that early. The zoom instructions push the model to request all regions in one call, so 8-crop first calls, and therefore this re-processing, are likely common on УПД sheets. Fix: always send the same tools. `zoom_source` already returns a no-image decline (`zoom_limit_reached`); keep that and add "submit now" to its text.
findings.evidence: sever/image_agent.py:256-265 `async def prepare_zoom(...)` ... `or deps.requests_started >= MAX_MODEL_REQUESTS - 1` ... `return None`; sever/image_conflicts.py:461-465 same pattern; sever/image_agent.py:64 "Use zoom_regions to request the heading and all needed caption-and-value regions together in ONE call"; https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/tools-toolsets/tools-advanced/: prepare can "return None to omit the tool for that step"; https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B/resolve/main/chat_template.jinja: the tools block opens with '<|im_start|>system\n' and '# Tools ... <tools>', and the system content is appended after </tools>; https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/20087: "once any prefix is invalid, you have to reprocess"; https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/18497: "The problem is the recurrent state, not the KV cache".
findings.expected_speed_effect: Saves one full re-processing per affected request: about 8k tokens of prefix, plus 1032 for the context image, plus up to 8 crops of about 1032 each, roughly 10-17k tokens or 4-7 s at 2,340 tok/s. Per video, about 1-5% of model time depending on how often the limit is hit (not measured).
findings.expected_precision_effect: Neutral. The model may occasionally call zoom after the limit and get the decline message, costing one more request.
findings.risk: Budget accounting must still reserve the final request; the existing `_CropLimitExceeded` and decline path already cover this. This is a code change only; no business rule is affected.
findings.how_to_test:
1. In the existing phase1-speed trace on the server, find requests where the tool count dropped; mark them in the trace with a new tool_names field if needed.
2. Compare their `cache_n` with the previous request's prompt_n+cache_n. Expect cache_n near 0 now.
3. After the change, rerun video 5 and expect cache_n of at least the previous prompt length on those steps, with lower total prompt_ms.

findings.title: Space hybrid-model checkpoints so the shared prefix is reused across frames
findings.claim: Qwen3.8-27B is a hybrid model: three Gated DeltaNet blocks for each full-attention block. llama.cpp reuses a cached prefix on such models only by restoring a context checkpoint at or before the first changed token, and the default spacing is 8192 tokens. The prefix shared by every frame's run (tools with the ~15k-char schema, ~9k chars of instructions, the prompt) is roughly 7-9k tokens by my estimate. Each new frame then differs at its image. With `--parallel 1`, orientation, triage and joint-review calls also evict the slot. So every new field-agent run probably re-processes the whole prefix. Set `--checkpoint-min-step 1024` and `--ctx-checkpoints 64`, and keep `--cache-ram` at 8192 MiB or more so idle prompts are saved when the call type changes. Optionally run all calls of one type together.
findings.evidence: llama.cpp server README (master): "-cms, --checkpoint-min-step N | minimum spacing between context checkpoints in tokens (default: 8192, 0 = no minimum)"; "--ctx-checkpoints ... (default: 32)"; "--cache-ram ... (default: 8192 ...)"; "--cache-idle-slots ... save idle slots to the prompt cache on new task"; https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/18497 (forced full prompt re-processing on hybrid models); https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/20087: checkpoints every N tokens during prompt processing; https://github.com/lmstudio-ai/lmstudio-bug-tracker/issues/1818: 60K-token repeat prompt TTFT ~70-80 s -> ~1.0 s with checkpoint flags on Qwen3-Next; https://playground.roboflow.com/models/compare/qwen3-6-27b-vs-qwen3-8-27b: 64 layers, three Gated DeltaNet blocks then one full-attention block; analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md: 68% of input tokens came from cache; 639,726 new prompt tokens in 273 s.
findings.expected_speed_effect: Upper bound: about 45 run starts per video re-processing about 8k tokens is about 360k tokens, or about 150 s of the 273 s prefill. A realistic saving is 50-150 s per video (5-15% of model time), to be confirmed by measurement.
findings.expected_precision_effect: None. Cached and fresh prefill may differ in the last bits of the logits.
findings.risk:
- Each checkpoint stores the recurrent state; more checkpoints use more memory and add a little prefill overhead.
- The flag name may differ in the deployed v0.6.0 build; check `llama-server --help`.
- Adds a server-config fingerprint change.
findings.how_to_test:
1. From trace.jsonl server_timings, take the first request of every field_agent and joint_review run and compute cache_n/(cache_n+prompt_n).
2. Measure the prefix length with llama-server /apply-template plus /tokenize on the rendered prompt up to the image marker.
3. If the cache ratio at run start is about 0 today, restart with the new flags and rerun video 5.
4. Expect cache_n of about the prefix length and lower total prompt_ms.

findings.title: Let the client set image sizes: send real 768x1376 contexts and stop server-side upscaling of crops
findings.evidence: deploy/sever-model.service:12 `--image-min-tokens 1024 --image-max-tokens 4096`; sever/image_agent.py:141 `uploaded.thumbnail((1024, 1024), Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)`; sever/image_agent.py:77 "lossless native crops, without magnification or invented pixels"; README.md:213 "без изменения нативного масштаба"; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/master/tools/mtmd/mtmd-image.cpp: `else if (opts.min_pixels > 0 && h_bar * w_bar < opts.min_pixels)` upscales, aligned to patch_size*n_merge; https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B/resolve/main/preprocessor_config.json: patch_size 16, merge_size 2, shortest_edge 65536 (= 64 tokens), longest_edge 16777216; https://github.com/qwenlm/qwen3-vl README: `{"longest_edge": 1280*32*32, "shortest_edge": 256*32*32}` for 256-1280 tokens, "the compression ratio is 32 for Qwen3-VL".
findings.expected_speed_effect: About 790 fewer prefill tokens per crop under 1 MP. At an estimated 150-200 crops per video (field agent plus joint review), that is about 120-160k tokens, or 50-70 s (5-7% of model time). The context change costs nothing extra.
findings.expected_precision_effect: The real 768x1376 context should improve region localization and may reduce re-zooms. Not enlarging tiny crops could hurt small glyphs, so A/B it against the labels.
findings.risk:
- Accuracy may drop on thin, single-line crops; fallback is to keep min 1024 for crops and change only the context.
- Fingerprint and schema-version change.
- Evidence records should note the server-side resize rule whichever setting is used.
findings.how_to_test:
1. Run A: context 768x1376 with min-tokens 1024.
2. Run B: context 768x1376 with min-tokens 256.
3. Run both on the 4 labelled videos (44 fields) and compare field accuracy, zoom requests per frame, prompt_n per request and model time against the phase1-speed baseline.

findings.title: Send homography-mapped crops in the first request for later frames of the same sheet
findings.claim: video.py already registers views of one sheet with ORB+RANSAC (`cv2.findHomography`) on 384-px thumbnails, but keeps only statistics. Save the 3x3 matrix, scaled to full resolution as H_full = S*H*S^-1 with S = 2160/384. Use it to map frame 1's model-selected rectangles (heading and caption-plus-value boxes, padded by about 3% of the frame) into frame k. Send the context plus those native crops in frame k's first request, with zoom tools still available for misses. Every value is still read fresh from frame k's own pixels; only coordinates are reused. 2026 work shows agentic visual calls are often unnecessary: in one study only 10-12% of calls were both needed and used at cold start, and released agents made spurious calls 36-87% of the time.
findings.evidence: sever/video.py:163 `matrix, inlier_mask = cv2.findHomography(pb, pa, cv2.RANSAC, 3.5)` (matrix not stored in evidence); sever/image_agent.py:64-66 zoom-first protocol (context -> zoom_regions -> submit, at least 2-3 requests per frame); analysis/ab-speed-20261017/comparison.md: field_agent 115 calls for 15 leaves; https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.22910 (19 Sep 2026): "only 10% to 12% of visual calls were both needed and used", spurious calls "36% to 87%"; https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.21333 (MME-VideoOCR): models have "limited capability" on tasks needing holistic multi-frame comprehension.
findings.expected_speed_effect: About one fewer request (about 5.3 s) per extra frame read. Estimated 25-35 fewer requests per video, about 130-185 s (13-18% of phase1 model time). Not measured.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Neutral to positive: tighter crops are chosen with knowledge of the layout. The risk is anchoring, where a wrong region is repeated.
findings.risk:
- If the sheet moved or curled, a mapped crop misses text; the zoom tools remain as fallback.
- Region choice is no longer independent between the two frames, so record it in the proof. Ask the customer whether coordinate reuse still counts as two distinct source frames; values and pixels stay independent and no answer is replayed.
findings.how_to_test:
1. Put the feature behind a flag.
2. On video 5 and the other 3 labelled videos, compare requests per extra-frame read, conflict count, joint_review calls, labelled-field accuracy and model time against phase1-speed.
3. Log the reprojection error of mapped boxes against the model's own zooms.

findings.title: Pick frames by per-region sharpness; avoid multi-frame super-resolution
findings.claim: Rank candidate frames for each field region instead of for the whole frame. For each candidate, compute the variance of the Laplacian on the homography-mapped field region, decoded at 1024 px or more for that region. Choose the two sharpest distinct frames per unresolved field for extra reads and joint review. Do not fuse frames: a fused or super-resolved image is not an actually-sent source frame, so it breaks the two-distinct-source-frames rule, and generative SR can invent glyphs. MME-VideoOCR shows models struggle to combine information across frames, so keep fusion as code-side agreement checks.
findings.evidence: sever/frame_pool.py:128-136 `sharpest = max([primary_feature.quality.get("sharpness_laplacian_variance", 0) ...` (whole-frame score); sever/quality.py:63 "sharp_background_or_page_edges_can_hide_blurred_text"; https://arxiv.org/html/2506.22139 (Q-Frame, Jul 2025): giving text-bearing frames higher resolution raised the Video-MME OCR subtask from 56.8 to 68.3 for Qwen2-VL-7B; https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.21333; I found no 2025-26 paper that benchmarks per-region sharpness for document video.
findings.expected_speed_effect: Fewer wasted views before stops such as source_views_exhausted or the no-progress stop. Not quantified.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Targets glyph errors (РИТЕЙЛ->РИТЕИЛ, соор./корп.) and one-glyph cross-frame conflicts (Кашириных/Каширных). Not quantified.
findings.risk: Needs full-resolution region decodes, which costs some CPU and ffmpeg time. Sharp frames can still have glare.
findings.how_to_test:
1. Offline, with no model calls, on the labelled videos: for each field with readings from two or more frames, compute region sharpness from the saved panels and check whether the wrong readings came from lower-sharpness regions.
2. If they did, run a live A/B on video 5 for conflicts and accuracy.

findings.title: Deskew or rectify the context and crops with a 4-corner homography; use learned dewarping only for curled sheets
findings.claim: Detect the page quadrilateral (largest 4-point contour of the leaf mask, or the registration homography to the sheet's best view). Build deskewed contexts and crops with cv2.warpPerspective, record the matrix in each panel's proof, and keep the native crop as well. On skewed sheets, axis-aligned crops pull in neighbouring lines, which matches two known error classes: address-block boundary and role confusion. For curled sheets, UVDoc (PaddleOCR, 19 ms on a T4) or ForCenNet are options.
findings.evidence: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.12898v3 (TeleOCR, 10 Sep 2026): removing geometric distortion "substantially improves two-stage parsing performance"; Qwen3-VL-8B Clean 72.44 vs Real Degraded 62.73 (PureDocBench); https://arxiv.org/html/2507.19804v1 (ForCenNet, ICCV 2025): DocUNet CER 0.136 vs DocTr 0.183, DocGeoNet 0.182, UVDoc/CGU-Net 0.178; https://www.paddleocr.ai/latest/en/version3.x/pipeline_usage/doc_preprocessor.html: UVDoc CER 0.179, 30.3 MB, 19.05 ms GPU (T4); https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.03145 (v3 Nov 2025): YOLOv8 mask plus polynomial grid, CER 0.0235 median vs DocTr++/DocGeoNet/apps.
findings.expected_speed_effect: Neutral to slightly positive: tighter crops mean fewer tokens and fewer re-zooms. The warp costs milliseconds on CPU.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Expected gain on address-boundary and role-confusion errors. The size on this data is unknown.
findings.risk:
- Warping resamples pixels, which conflicts with the 'no magnification / no invented pixels' wording, so evidence must cite the warped panel plus its transform.
- Learned dewarpers can distort glyphs.
- Adding PaddleOCR conflicts with README.md:38 "Отдельного классификатора и предварительного Tesseract нет"; that needs a customer decision.
findings.how_to_test:
1. Offline: measure the skew angle of the page quad on all labelled primary frames.
2. Live: A/B deskewed crops against native crops on the 4 labelled videos, looking mainly at the consignor/consignee address fields (upd.consignee_address is 0/2 today).

findings.title: Try Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (MoE) as the decode-speed option
findings.claim: The workload is limited by generation speed. An MoE model with about 3B active parameters decodes about 3x faster on an RTX 5090 than the 27B dense model, and its document benchmarks are close. An earlier trial in this repo got the same 9/10 fields at 156.8 s vs 231.2 s. MTP also works with it in llama.cpp.
findings.evidence: https://zenn.dev/toki_mwc/articles/rtx5090-qwen36-35b-a3b-llmacpp-bench: RTX 5090, llama.cpp b8870, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B TG128 180 tok/s (UD-Q5_K_S) and 183 (UD-Q4_K_M), PP512 3293/2892; https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B/raw/main/README.md: OmniDocBench1.5 89.9, CC-OCR 81.9; https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B/raw/main/README.md: Qwen3.8-27B OmniDocBench1.5 91.1; README.md:78 "обе модели дали 9/10 полей ... Q36 за 156,83 с и Qwen3.8-27B Q6 за 231,19 с"; analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md: 61 tok/s on the 27B.
findings.expected_speed_effect: Generation about 688 s -> 230-260 s; model time -40-45% on video 5, more with MTP.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Unknown for literal Cyrillic glyphs; OmniDocBench is 1.2 points lower than Qwen3.8-27B.
findings.risk:
- The 27B is documented as the user-chosen model (deploy/README.md:260), so switching is the user's decision.
- Glyph-level regressions are possible.
- Requires a new fingerprint and batch.
findings.how_to_test:
1. Point sever-model at the stored Qwen3.6-35B-A3B Q6 GGUF and mmproj.
2. Run phase1-speed on the 4 labelled videos.
3. Compare the 44 labelled fields, conflict rate, requests, and generation/prefill tok/s from server_timings.

findings.title: A/B two parallel slots with a unified KV pool against MTP
findings.claim: One decode stream is limited by memory bandwidth, so two concurrent leaves (`--parallel 2 --kv-unified` with HARNESS_LEAF_CONCURRENCY=2) should batch their decodes for higher total throughput. MTP currently requires n_parallel=1, so the two options compete and need an A/B. deploy/README.md says the context is split per slot (32768 each at N=2). With `--kv-unified` the 65536 pool is shared instead, which keeps room for 4-frame joint reviews.
findings.evidence: llama.cpp server README: "-kvu, --kv-unified ... use single unified KV buffer shared across all sequences (default: enabled if number of slots is auto)"; "--kv-unified-per-slot N"; deploy/README.md:588-590 "При --parallel N контекст --ctx-size делится между слотами"; https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/22673 comment: "MTP currently supports only n_parallel=1".
findings.expected_speed_effect: My unsourced estimate is 1.5-1.9x total decode throughput, so 25-40% less wall time on videos with several independent leaves. Per-request latency goes up.
findings.expected_precision_effect: None.
findings.risk:
- Not compatible with MTP today.
- Budget and stop semantics across concurrent leaves.
- Each slot needs its own recurrent state and checkpoints.
- Watch peak VRAM in gpu-*.csv.
findings.how_to_test:
1. Restart sever-model with `--parallel 2 --kv-unified`.
2. Run deploy/ab_speed_test.sh with LEAF_CONCURRENCY_B=2 on video 5.
3. Compare wall time, model time and peak memory against the MTP run from the first finding.

findings.title: Remove or shrink the orientation call
findings.evidence: sever/image_detail.py:88 `uploaded.thumbnail((1024, 1024), ...)` and sever/image_orientation.py:61-80 (four rotated contexts in one call); analysis/ab-speed-20261017/comparison.md: orientation 15 calls; https://www.paddleocr.ai/latest/en/version3.x/pipeline_usage/doc_preprocessor.html: PP-LCNet_x1_0_doc_ori 99.06% top-1, 2.62 ms GPU (T4), 7 MB; README.md:38 states no separate classifier.
findings.expected_speed_effect: 15 calls at about 2-2.5 s each is about 30-40 s per video (3-4%) if removed. With 144-token rotations, prefill per orientation call drops about 3.5k tokens.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Low risk. A wrong rotation is already caught by the insufficient_evidence path, which re-picks the rotation for the next frame (deploy/README.md phase-1 notes).
findings.risk: Option c contradicts the documented no-classifier design. Low-resolution rotations may fail on mostly blank sheets.
findings.how_to_test:
1. Offline: rerun the orientation decision with 288x512 panels on the 15 primaries of video 5 plus the other labelled videos, comparing against the rotations chosen in existing traces (this needs model calls on the server).
2. Live: measure calls and time saved.

findings.title: Fewer output tokens: integer 0-1000 zoom coordinates and per-step max_tokens caps
findings.claim: Generation is 69% of model time, averaging 222 output tokens per call. Zoom arguments are floats on 0..1, up to 32 numbers per zoom_regions call. Qwen3-VL grounds boxes in relative coordinates, which the community describes as an integer 0-1000 grid. Integer coordinates on that grid are shorter and match how the model was trained. Also cap max_tokens per step (about 512 for zoom steps, about 2048 for submit_reading) instead of the global 8192. At 61 tok/s a runaway 8192-token answer costs about 134 s.
findings.evidence: sever/image_agent.py:36 `Coordinate = Annotated[float, Field(ge=0, le=1, allow_inf_nan=False)]`; sever/image_agent.py:328 `"max_tokens": effective.max_output_tokens`; README.md:42 output limit 8192; https://github.com/qwenlm/qwen3-vl: grounding uses "relative position coordinates"; https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL/issues/1616 (community reply): use 0-1000 relative boxes for Qwen3-VL; analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md: 222 output tokens per request.
findings.expected_speed_effect: Perhaps 20-60 fewer output tokens per zoom_regions call (0.3-1 s at 61 tok/s). This depends on how Qwen3.8 tokenizes digits, which I did not verify (confidence 0.3). The caps protect tail latency.
findings.expected_precision_effect: Neutral to slightly positive for region choice. The caps must not truncate legitimate long address blocks.
findings.risk:
- Coordinate conversion bugs.
- A truncated submit fails the schema and wastes the run.
- Requires a schema and prompt version bump.
findings.how_to_test:
1. POST sample arguments in both formats to llama-server /tokenize and count tokens.
2. From traces, build a predicted_n histogram per call kind and step to choose caps above p99.
3. A/B on video 5.

findings.title: Constrained JSON / grammar sampling is not the bottleneck
findings.claim: Constrained tool-call decoding measured 61 tok/s, about the community figure for unconstrained decoding with the same GPU and quant (52-56 tok/s on Qwen3.8-27B Q6, no MTP or vision). Grammar overhead is therefore within noise, and switching to llguidance for speed is not worth it. Keep the schema unambiguous: extra="forbid" (additionalProperties false gives faster grammars) and no ambiguous unions. llama.cpp warns that `x? x? x? ...` repetition and ambiguous grammars can be very slow, so measure ms per token on submit_reading calls given the large maxLength fields.
findings.evidence: sever/image_reader.py:161-167 `max_length=1200` (raw_value), `max_length=600` (evidence_text), `max_length=240` (reason); analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md: 61 tok/s; https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF/discussions/14: ~52-56 tok/s no vision/MTP; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/master/grammars/README.md: "the syntax `x? x? x?.... x?` ... may result in extremely slow sampling", additionalProperties false "produces faster grammars"; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/master/docs/llguidance.md: mask "50μs of single-core CPU time", p99 0.5 ms; https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/4218: "A deterministic grammar should maintain a constant stack count".
findings.expected_speed_effect: About 0. This mainly stops effort being spent in the wrong place.
findings.expected_precision_effect: None.
findings.risk: If some calls use an ambiguous schema, for example joint review unions, they could be slower; the measurement will show it.
findings.how_to_test:
1. Compute predicted_ms/predicted_n per call kind from trace server_timings.
2. Compare with `llama-bench -m $MODEL_PATH -fa 1 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -p 0 -n 128 -d 10000` on the idle server.
3. If the gap is under 5-10%, the grammar is not the bottleneck.

findings.title: Test a larger physical batch (-ub) for prefill
findings.claim: Prefill is 27% of model time at 2,340 tok/s with the default `-ub 512`. Try `-ub 1024` and `-ub 2048` (with `-b 2048`) to see whether prompt processing on the 5090 gets faster, and check VRAM headroom together with MTP.
findings.evidence: llama.cpp server README: "-ub, --ubatch-size N | physical maximum batch size (default: 512)"; deploy/sever-model.service:12 sets no -ub; analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md: prefill 273 s at 2,340 tok/s. The only found evidence of a large gain is an informal Reddit run on a 3090 with CPU offload, which does not transfer reliably to a fully GPU-resident 5090.
findings.expected_speed_effect: Unknown. A 10-40% faster prefill would save about 25-80 s per video.
findings.expected_precision_effect: None.
findings.risk: Larger compute buffers take VRAM (26.7 GB used now, plus MTP). There may be interactions with image chunk batching.
findings.how_to_test:
1. On the idle server, run `llama-bench -m $MODEL_PATH -fa 1 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -p 4096 -n 0 -ub 512,1024,2048`.
2. If pp improves, restart sever-model with the best -ub and compare prompt_ms/prompt_n on video 5.

candidates.name: Qwen3.8-27B (current) GGUF Q6 with MTP speculative decoding
candidates.params_or_size: About 27B dense hybrid: 64 layers, Gated DeltaNet plus full attention; MTP head
candidates.license: Apache 2.0 per third-party listings; not checked on the fetched card
candidates.benchmarks:
- OmniDocBench 1.5: 91.1 (Qwen3.6-27B 89.4).
- CharXiv RQ: 83.7. Source: https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B/raw/main/README.md
- Roboflow vision evals overall: 69.5% BF16, 69.5% AWQ-INT4. Source: https://playground.roboflow.com/models/compare/qwen3-6-27b-vs-qwen3-8-27b
candidates.russian_or_cyrillic_evidence: In-repo only: V7 got 35/44 provisional labelled fields; phase1-speed got 15/22 on video 5 (analysis/ab-speed-20261017/README.md). There is no public Russian OCR benchmark.
candidates.serving:
- llama.cpp v0.6.0 deployed (deploy/README.md:259).
- MTP via --spec-type draft-mtp, mainline since PR #22673 (merged 2026-05-16), stated compatible with vision; currently needs --parallel 1.
- RTX 5090 user reports: about 92 tok/s with vision+MTP vs about 52-56 tok/s without (https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF/discussions/14).
- The model card lists vLLM and SGLang.
candidates.structured_output:
- Tool calls in Qwen XML format (<tool_call><function=...><parameter=...>), per chat_template.jinja.
- llama.cpp --jinja tool calling with a grammar.
- Measured constrained decode is 61 tok/s, so grammar overhead is negligible.
candidates.vram_estimate:
- Measured 26.2-26.7 GB on the server at ctx 65536, q8_0 K/V, with mmproj.
- MTP adds about 1-2.5 GB (Unsloth doc; PR #22673 user: 2.49 GiB).
- About 16k context would need less KV, since only about 1 in 4 layers is full attention. That is an estimate, not measured.

- RTX 5090, llama.cpp b8870: TG128 180 tok/s (UD-Q5_K_S) and 183 (UD-Q4_K_M); PP512 3293 and 2892. Source: https://zenn.dev/toki_mwc/articles/rtx5090-qwen36-35b-a3b-llmacpp-bench?locale=en

candidates.vram_estimate: Small; CPU is fine.
